drills.name: Balloon Tennis
drills.works: Gives every child success because balloons move slowly; tracking at all heights, both sides of body; rallying with a partner before a ball is introduced.
drills.players: 1-2+ players; round balloons inflated medium-to-low so they float a little; a 3-5 m string/ribbon; tape; paper plates + paint-stir sticks taped on as "racquets" (or real racquets / hands).
drills.setup: String hung horizontally about 1 m off the floor between two chairs/shelves = net. One child each side, roughly 1-2 m from the string [coach suggestion].
drills.steps: Hit the balloon back and forth over the string. If it touches the floor on your side, the other player scores. First to 5, then restart. Racquets may not cross over the net. Multiple touches on your own side are allowed.
drills.cues: Watch the balloon all the way onto the plate; "pancake hand" (flat palm under the balloon) [added].
drills.progression: Solo keep-ups counting taps → partner rallies → light tennis balls for older children → JM: use left and right hands, forehand/backhand side of hand, then racquet.
drills.regression: Hands only; catch-and-throw the balloon instead of hitting.
drills.source: Net Generation at-home balloon tennis instructions as summarised in search results from [USTA Florida](https://www.ustaflorida.com/tennis-tip-thursday-balloon-tennis-edgies-fast-feet/) and [Active for Life](https://activeforlife.com/activity/balloon-tennis/) (both pages returned 403 to direct fetch); [JM](https://education.gov.scot/media/tunlek1v/jm-tennis-resource-primary.pdf); [Premier Education](https://www.premier-education.com/news/tennis-games-for-kids/) (ages 4-7 variant, count taps)
drills.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8i5I3z0lgz0 — "Net Generation: Balloon Tennis Pt. 1" — United States Tennis Association (USTA)

drills.name: Beanbag Racket Rally (Judy Murray progression)
drills.works: Children who cannot yet control a racquet; beanbags don't roll away and are easier to trap than a ball (good for big groups).
drills.players: Pairs; beanbags; one racquet each, later two racquets each.
drills.setup: Pairs in small spaces facing each other, starting close (about 1-2 m) [coach suggestion]; hoops can mark target areas.
drills.steps: (1) Start with the hand: mimic the shape of the shot sending the beanbag to partner. (2) Add the racquet when the child is succeeding. (3) Paired beanbag exchanges with one beanbag, then add a second, then increase distance, working towards a "mini rally". (4) "Double racket" exercise (a racquet in each hand) mirrors forehand and backhand.
drills.cues: Start statically, then add movement; work both left and right sides (tennis is two-sided). "Shake hands with the racquet" for grip [added].
drills.progression: Second beanbag; more distance; switch to fluff ball, then ball on the floor, then bouncing ball.
drills.regression: Hand only; partner closer; balance the beanbag on the strings and walk.
drills.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lYuzwTnQYUc — "Primary Racket Skills" — Education Scotland. Also related: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Istx1NxbRuc — "Stay and Play - Let's play Tennis Racket Bean Bag Toss with Stacy" — Portland Parks & Recreation

drills.name: Pizza Delivery
drills.ages: Red 5-8 (NG C1); easily run with tots
drills.works: Body awareness, keeping a flat palm (precursor to balancing the ball on strings), moving while controlling an object.
drills.players: Whole group; one "pizza" per child (poly-spot, paper plate, or a ball on an open hand); chalk/TDLs for boundary.
drills.setup: Defined area marked with chalk/TDLs; players spread out.
drills.steps: Carry the pizza flat in one palm around the area; walk fast, no running. Try to gently knock down other players' pizzas or chase them so they drop it. Dropped pizza → go to the sideline and cheer, or do five reps of a fun exercise (e.g., "I'm a Star" jumps, donkey kicks); coach decides re-entry.
drills.cues: Stay low, be aware, keep moving.
drills.progression: Carry the "pizza" on the racquet strings (see #5); switch hands.
drills.regression: No knocking — just walk the pizza through cones.
drills.video: None verified for this exact activity.

drills.name: Bungee Jump (and Bungee Flips)
drills.ages: Red 5-8 (NG C1-C3); tots with a large foam ball
drills.works: Watching the ball onto the strings, soft hands, steady head and wrist; introduces palm-up (forehand face) and knuckles-up (backhand face).
drills.players: Individuals; racquet + red ball each.
drills.setup: Each player in their own space (spread on both sides of the net if on court).
drills.steps: Palm up, ball in centre of strings; tilt the racquet so the ball rolls off; let it bounce; catch it back on the strings. Reposition with free hand if needed. *Bungee Flips:* catch each bounce on the opposite face (palm up, then knuckles up).
drills.cues: Pause with the ball on the strings and keep your head still; firm grip, slow and steady; use your knees to get down to the ball, keep the wrist still.
drills.progression: Hold the ball on the strings for less time → knuckles-up → continuous tap-ups → do bungees while moving around the court.
drills.regression: Free hand helps reposition; bigger ball.
drills.source: [NG-Red](https://www.usta.com/content/dam/usta/content-fragments/tennis-service-center/assets/pdfs/Net-Generation-Community-Manual-Red.pdf) (C1 Ch.2, Ch.5; C2 Ch.3; C3 Ch.1-2)
drills.video: None verified for this exact activity.

drills.name: Start Your Engines (with Traffic Lights / "Red Light, Green Light" calls)
drills.works: Balancing the ball on the strings while moving; stopping under control.
drills.players: Individuals or teams; racquet + red ball each; chalk/TDLs for two "sidelines".
drills.setup: Two lines marked (any width the group can cover — e.g., a red-court width of 18 ft [coach suggestion]).
drills.steps:
Do two bungee jumps at the start line, then walk to the opposite line and back with the ball balanced on the strings. Level 2: three then four bungees first. Level 3: continuous bungees line to line. Level 4: alternate palm up and knuckles up.
- **Traffic-lights overlay (generic PE game, tennis adaptation is mine):** Red = stop, amber = walk, green = run (or move faster); extra calls in some versions: roundabout (turn round once), motorway (sprint), speed bump (jump). Applying these calls while carrying the ball on the strings is my adaptation — not documented by a tennis federation in sources I could access.
drills.cues: Eyes on the ball; flat strings ("pizza tray") [added].
drills.progression: Faster calls; tap the ball up while moving.
drills.regression: Carry a beanbag or poly-spot instead of a ball.
drills.source: [NG-Red](https://www.usta.com/content/dam/usta/content-fragments/tennis-service-center/assets/pdfs/Net-Generation-Community-Manual-Red.pdf) (C1 Ch.2 Station 3); Traffic Lights rules from [Perform](https://www.perform.org.uk/child-development/drama-games/traffic-lights) and [Scouts – Red light green light](https://scouts.org.uk/activities/red-light-green-light) (search snippets; non-tennis sources)
drills.video: None verified.

drills.name: Self-Toss ("Bounce-Catch")
drills.works: Judging the bounce; two-hand then one-hand catching.
drills.players: Individuals; one red ball each; chalk/TDLs boundary.
drills.setup: Players spread out in a defined space.
drills.steps: Toss the ball with one hand, palm up, above head height; let it bounce; catch with both hands. Home version: toss to a wall, let it bounce, catch; low, medium, high tosses.
drills.cues: Palm up to the sky on the toss; "bounce — catch!" said aloud [added].
drills.progression: Toss higher → toss farther away → catch with one hand.
drills.regression: Bigger (playground) ball; two bounces allowed.
drills.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lOpIXxHtwp4 — "20 Tennis exercises for groups of 3 4 year olds" — Tenniscoachblog

drills.name: Ice Cream Cones
drills.ages: Red 5-8 (NG C2); tots can do it
drills.works: Waiting for the ball to drop and catching it as it falls (counters rushing in too close).
drills.players: Individuals; red ball + upturned cone each.
drills.setup: Spread around the court.
drills.steps: Toss, let it bounce, catch it in the upturned cone. Call out a different ice-cream flavour after each catch.
drills.cues: Bend your knees and catch it on the way down [added].
drills.progression: Alternate catching after the bounce and in the air; count "scoops" in a row.
drills.regression: Two-hand catch without the cone; LTA Go also recommends "ice cream" cones as a catching aid.
drills.video: None verified.

drills.name: One Bounce, Two Bounce
drills.works: Reading the bounce; patience (not grabbing early).
drills.players: Pairs; one red ball; a line, tape/rope, or object as a "net".
drills.setup: Partners on opposite sides of the line about 8 ft apart.
drills.steps: Take turns tossing. The tosser calls "one" or "two" = number of bounces allowed before the catch.
drills.cues: Ready position before each toss [added].
drills.progression: Toss with non-dominant hand; one-hand catch with an orange ball; toss and trap with the racquet.
drills.regression: Bigger ball; reduce distance.
drills.video: None verified.

drills.name: Tunnel Ball
drills.works: Turning and chasing a moving ball; reacting to a call.
drills.players: Pairs; one red ball; a sideline at each end.
drills.setup: Roller with both feet on a sideline; partner about 5 ft away, feet shoulder-width apart, in ready position, back to the far sideline.
drills.steps: Roll the ball between the partner's legs at medium speed; partner turns, chases it down before it reaches the opposite sideline and tosses it back. Four successful, then swap.
drills.cues: Quick turn, quick feet [added].
drills.progression: Toss over partner's head to catch before the far sideline; tosser shouts 1, 2 or 3 = bounces allowed before catching.
drills.regression: Slower roll; shorter distance to far line.
drills.source: [NG-Red](https://www.usta.com/content/dam/usta/content-fragments/tennis-service-center/assets/pdfs/Net-Generation-Community-Manual-Red.pdf) (C1 Ch.4; C2 Ch.4, Ch.6; C3 Ch.1-2)
drills.video: None verified.

drills.name: Ball Drop
drills.works: Reaction speed, first step, catching to the side (not in front of the face).
drills.players: Pairs; two red or two orange balls (orange is easier to catch one-handed).
drills.setup: Pairs about 4 ft apart. Dropper holds both balls at shoulder height, arms in a "V", palms down.
drills.steps: Drop one ball; partner catches it after the bounce with one hand — right hand on the right side, left hand on the left. Four each side, then switch roles.
drills.cues: Ready position, eyes on the hands [added].
drills.progression: Alternate left/right; dropper's arms straight out to the side; step back.
drills.regression: Two-hand catch from the side with a red ball.
drills.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZORZOfQgS2A — "Net Generation: Ball Drop" — United States Tennis Association (USTA)

drills.name: Shake-Hands Toss
drills.works: One-hand catching; moving the feet together to adjust to a bad toss.
drills.players: Pairs; one orange ball.
drills.setup: Partners shake hands and keep holding — their joined arms form a "net".
drills.steps: With the free hand, gently toss over the arm-net, let it bounce, catch one-handed; repeat. Move feet together to adjust. Four each, then switch hands.
drills.cues: Move together, then catch.
drills.progression: Higher and wider tosses; catch in the air.
drills.regression: Two bounces allowed.
drills.video: None verified.

drills.name: Fire Ants
drills.works: Flat-footed, static players; ready position.
drills.players: Whole group; no equipment.
drills.setup: Spread around the court in ready position.
drills.steps: On "go", stomp as many imaginary fire ants as possible on the spot for a set time.
drills.cues: Stay on your toes; tiny fast steps [added].
drills.progression: Skip around the court and stomp when the coach shouts "fire ants!"; side-shuffle and stomp.
drills.regression: Shorter bursts.
drills.video: None verified.

drills.name: Messy Bedroom / Clean Your Room
drills.works: Overarm throwing pattern for the serve; energy and team spirit.
drills.players: Two teams of 3-5; bucket of red balls per side; net, pop-up net or barrier tape.
drills.setup: Teams on opposite sides of a net/barrier tape (NG prefers balls on the side away from the fence). Coach tips a bucket of balls out on each side.
drills.steps: NG: throw balls overhand one at a time to the other side for ≤1 minute (adjust to ball count); afterwards each team collects and counts the balls it threw and tries to beat its team record. LTA Go variant: aim is to have the fewest balls on your side after 60 s; if an opponent catches your throw before it bounces, the thrower is out. Tennis Canada variant: each player starts with a ball; team keeping its end clearest wins.
drills.cues: Side-on, elbow up, throw high over the net [added].
drills.progression: Throw with non-dominant hand; must land in a service box/designated area.
drills.regression: Two-hand throws; lower net/tape.
drills.video: None verified for this exact game.

drills.name: Hits
drills.works: Aiming at a moving target; rolling then throwing accuracy.
drills.players: Teams of 4-6; basket of red balls per team; coach has two playground balls; tape/rope or no net.
drills.setup: Teams spread on opposite service lines; coach at the side of the court at the centre.
drills.steps: Coach calls "hits!" and rolls a playground ball down the centre of the court; each player rolls a red ball trying to hit it. Teams total their hits; coach rolls a second ball. Repeat for a "team best".
drills.cues: Step and roll toward where the big ball is going [added].
drills.progression: Move back to the baseline; throw at the playground ball.
drills.regression: Coach rolls slower; players closer.
drills.video: None verified.

drills.name: Walk the Dog (and Zig-Zag)
drills.ages: Red 5-8 (NG C1-C2); tots with a big ball
drills.skill: Forehand and backhand (swing path on the ground)
drills.works: Racquet face control, contact to the side of the body, follow-through toward the target, early racquet preparation via footwork.
drills.players: Individuals or pairs; racquet + red ball; poly-spots/paper plates/chalk targets.
drills.setup: Players on a sideline; a spot 15-20 ft away (or on the opposite sideline). Zig-zag: four spots in a zig-zag between two sidelines; 3 players per pattern (next goes when previous reaches spot 2).
drills.steps: Roll the ball with the edge of the racquet to the spot, stop it on the spot, roll it back and stop it again. Partner version: send it back along the ground to your partner, who stops it and repeats. Zig-zag: forehand to spot 1, backhand to spot 2, alternating.
drills.cues: Racquet edge touches the ground, strings stay on the ball; ball to the side of your body, follow through to the target; forehand = palm forward, backhand = knuckles forward; use your feet to get the racquet in position.
drills.progression: Backhand only → zig-zag both sides → bungees on each spot → drop-hit back to partner.
drills.regression: Big ball; smaller racquet; both hands on the racquet.
drills.video: None verified for this exact activity.

drills.name: Keep It Moving / Floor Rally in the Alley (cooperative rolling rally)
drills.works: Over-hitting; facing the net; contact in front; first continuous rally.
drills.players: Pairs; racquets; one red ball; chalk/TDLs.
drills.setup: NG: 2-3 pairs per side of the net, partners facing each other with a court line as the "net"; players mark their own boundaries. Tennis Canada: pair works in the doubles alley, each player's feet on a sideline (singles or doubles line).
drills.steps: Stop the ball, then push/roll it back; once successful, rally continuously. Players set their own rally goal. TC scoring: a point when the ball stays on the ground and inside the alley; play to a set number; practise the backhand side too.
drills.cues: Racquet on its edge, simple motion (NG). Strings point at the target; turn sideways to receive and send; meet it in front of the front foot (TC; TC specifies continental grip).
drills.progression: Change court size/shape each partner change; rotate partners on a timer; forehands only / backhands only; alternate FH/BH; push without stopping; play over a low net.
drills.regression: FH only; shorter area; big ball.
drills.source: [NG-Red](https://www.usta.com/content/dam/usta/content-fragments/tennis-service-center/assets/pdfs/Net-Generation-Community-Manual-Red.pdf) (C1 Ch.5; C2 Ch.3; C3 Ch.2); [TC-LTP](https://assets.tenniscanada.com/production/PDFs/LearnToPlay_ENG.pdf) (Practice Activity 3)
drills.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sH7rUBT-y5o — "Tennis Red Ball games  - Rally progression" — Get Set Tennis

drills.name: Touchdown
drills.works: Aiming through a gate; counting points to 7 (tennis-like scoring).
drills.players: Pairs; racquets; one red ball and two cones per pair.
drills.setup: Three pairs per side of the net (one on each sideline, one on the baseline). Two cones 4 ft apart with a court line between them; partners stand on that line about 4 ft from the cones, on opposite sides.
drills.steps: Roll the ball between the cones with a forehand; partner stops it and rolls back. Each ball through the cones = "field goal" = 1 point. First to 7 = "touchdown" (yell it!).
drills.cues: Edge on the ground, follow through to the gate [added, consistent with Walk the Dog cues].
drills.progression: Backhands; rally without stopping the ball until 7.
drills.regression: Wider gate; closer.
drills.video: None verified.

drills.name: Bullseye
drills.works: Short, controlled swing; feel for "softer / harder".
drills.players: Teams; racquets; supply of red balls; chalk/lines; object for the bullseye.
drills.setup: A big target about 8×8 ft with a smaller target inside and a bullseye (object or chalk) in the centre. Players stand outside the target area.
drills.steps: Take turns tapping the ball with the racquet (palm forward) toward the target. Scoring example: big target 1, small target 5, bullseye 10. Teams add up to a target number, or play by time for a "team best".
drills.cues: Short and simple motion; how can you make it go softer? harder?
drills.progression: Start farther back; forehands and backhands; drop-hit to targets.
drills.regression: Roll the ball with the hand.
drills.video: None verified.

drills.name: Jacks (Onesies to Fivesies) and Splat
drills.works: Getting under the ball, controlled tap height, quick feet to adjust.
drills.players: Individuals; racquet + red ball; cone or spot per player for Splat.
drills.setup: Players spread a safe distance apart.
drills.steps: Toss, bounce, tap up once (palm up), catch with free hand → call "Onesies"; then two taps → "Twosies"… up to "Fivesies". *Splat:* toss, bounce, keep tapping up and try to hit your own cone/target on the bounce.
drills.cues: Bend your knees to get under the ball; catch palm up; tap to at least eye level; quick feet to move out of the way.
drills.progression: Rally until you miss; backhand (knuckles up); alternate FH/BH; Splat with partner alternating; teams count cones hit in 1 minute.
drills.regression: Tap once and catch.
drills.video: None verified.

drills.name: Lobster Trap / Half-Pound Lobster Trap
drills.works: Standing too close / facing the net — players learn to meet the ball to the side of the body at waist height.
drills.players: Pairs; one red ball; Lobster Trap = two racquets for the "lobster"; Half-Pound = one racquet.
drills.setup: Feeder and lobster 6-8 ft apart.
drills.steps: Feeder tosses; after the bounce the lobster traps the ball between two racquets, sets it down and rolls it back with a forehand. Four, then switch. *Half-pound:* trap the ball against one racquet after the bounce, then gently drop-hit it back.
drills.cues: Turn sideways to receive; trap at your side at waist level like a groundstroke; follow through toward your partner when sending back.
drills.progression: Receive on both sides; send back with a drop-hit; make the lobster move (side, back, forward); backhand.
drills.regression: Ball on the ground and roll it back; stand closer.
drills.video: None verified.

drills.name: Battle Spots
drills.skill: Forehand to targets over a net
drills.works: Direction and depth control; drop-feed technique.
drills.players: Pairs (up to two pairs per court); racquets; one red ball; poly-spots, hula hoops, cones or chalk targets.
drills.setup: Partners across the net, service box = boundary; a cluster of targets on each side. Players start on the service line.
drills.steps: Drop-hit a forehand over the net at partner's targets; partner traps and drop-hits back at yours. 1 point per target hit. Timed; beat your record.
drills.cues: For the drop: arm to the side, palm down (non-dominant hand).
drills.progression: Move farther back; rally back and forth.
drills.regression: Shorten distance; let the ball go under a tape/rope net; bigger/more targets.
drills.video: None verified.

drills.name: Survivor (the Island)
drills.works: Consistency under light pressure; extension toward the target.
drills.players: Teams of 3-4; one container of red balls per team; net.
drills.setup: Teams line up behind a line (C2: behind the service line). A player or helper is the "ball machine" (C2: across the net with the coach).
drills.steps: Each hitter gets two gentle tosses (C1: backhands). Get at least 1 of 2 over the net and in to stay on the "island". Miss both → go "out to sea" (other side of net). Sea players get back by catching a hit ball on one bounce; a catch in the air rescues everyone at sea; the hitter whose ball was caught goes to sea. Rotate the "ball machine".
drills.cues: Extend up and out to the target on the follow-through.
drills.progression: Must make both shots; hit to a specific area; add backhands.
drills.regression: Drop-hit instead of a fed ball.
drills.video: None verified.

drills.name: Feed, Hit & Catch
drills.works: Sideways set-up, contact at waist height out in front, recovery to home base.
drills.players: Groups of three (feeder, hitter, catcher); racquet; red balls; marker for home base.
drills.setup: Feeder and hitter at the same home base on one side of the net; catcher on the other side.
drills.steps: Feeder tosses underhand; hitter sends a forehand over the net toward the catcher; catcher catching after one bounce = team point. Rally ends on a double bounce, ball out, or in the net. Rotate roles. Can be run in pairs (points for hitting a specific area).
drills.cues: Turn sideways; hit at waist height, in front, at a comfortable distance; back to home base after every shot.
drills.progression: Backhand only; alternate FH/BH; catcher uses non-dominant hand.
drills.regression: Hitter self-rallies before sending; catcher uses two hands; stand closer to the net.
drills.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vvrHePqMbPw — "Fun kids tennis game for sending & receiving skills (5-7 years / Red)" — Tenniscoachblog

drills.name: Big-Ball Tennis / Throw Rally
drills.skill: Rally pattern without racquet; tracking; recovery
drills.works: Turning sideways to send/receive; recovering to a home base; reading crosscourt vs down-the-line.
drills.players: Pairs; playground ball (NG) or red ball; markers for "home base".
drills.setup: NG: two pairs per side, one player in each service box (boxes = boundaries). TC: pairs on a red court, marker at each player's recovery position.
drills.steps: NG: two-hand toss to partner's box straight ahead; partner lets it bounce, catches with both hands, tosses back. TC Throw Rally: cooperative underhand throws crosscourt or down the line; longest rally wins; rally ends on a double bounce, ball out/net, or a catch in the air (must let it bounce). NG doubles version: pairs vs pairs, two-hand side toss, multiple bounces allowed, count catches in a set time.
drills.cues: Start sideways, finish facing forward (NG); throw and catch sideways and return to home base (TC).
drills.progression: Toss from one side then the other; straight then crosscourt; catch in front then to the side; non-dominant hand; larger area; one bounce only; compete.
drills.regression: Smaller area; same side of net; more than one bounce.
drills.video: None verified for this exact activity.

drills.name: Rally Pyramid
drills.works: First over-the-net rally; returning to ready position.
drills.players: Pairs, two pairs per court; racquets; red balls; tape/rope net for less-skilled players.
drills.setup: Rally on half-court, each player in the middle of a service box. A spot at the side of the court where each pair builds a four-ball pyramid (three in a triangle + one on top).
drills.steps: Player 1 (racquet under arm or on the ground) tosses to Player 2 and gets ready; P2 hits over with either stroke; P1 hits it back. Each successful one-each exchange adds a ball to the pyramid.
drills.cues: Both players back to ready position after hitting.
drills.progression: Two each, then three each to score; increase distance.
drills.regression: Drop-hit and trap.
drills.video: None verified.

drills.name: Card Shark
drills.works: Consistency; choosing stroke; self-paced challenge.
drills.players: Pairs, two per court; racquets; red (or orange) balls; a deck of cards.
drills.setup: One player in the middle of each service box (Orange: start on the 60-ft baseline, half-court).
drills.steps: Coach assigns colours to strokes (e.g., red card = forehand); the card number = rally length (remove numbers players can't achieve; joker = wildcard, player chooses). One player picks a card, runs back, starts with a drop-hit; partner traps and drop-hits back — each drop-hit + trap counts one. Keep the card, pick another. Score as a whole group (until cards are gone) or as teams on time; add up cards at the end.
drills.cues: Back to ready position after each hit; cooperate with your partner.
drills.progression: Move back to service line; rally diagonally/crosscourt; one stroke only.
drills.regression: Lower numbers only; move closer.
drills.video: None verified.

drills.name: Sky Ball
drills.works: Underarm "pushing" serve; no trophy position.
drills.players: Pairs; red balls; home-base markers.
drills.setup: Partners on opposite sides of the net, rallying crosscourt or down the line.
drills.steps: Cooperative overhead-throw rally; longest rally wins. Rally ends on: double bounce, ball out or in net, a catch in the air, or an underhand throw.
drills.cues: Throw upward from slightly sideways with the throwing hand above the shoulder ("trophy position"); catch sideways; recover to home base.
drills.progression: Reduce the playing area; throw and catch with dominant and non-dominant hand.
drills.regression: Increase the playing area; same side of net; allow more than one bounce. (Note: TC lists area changes in the opposite direction to its Throw Rally — possibly an erratum.)
drills.video: None verified.

drills.name: Flying Target
drills.works: Wild toss; contact out in front/above head.
drills.players: Pairs; two balls per player.
drills.setup: Pairs at the baseline near the centre (serve position); the player stands sideways behind the service line.
drills.steps: Toss one ball up with the non-racquet hand, then throw the ball in the racquet hand to hit the tossed ball. One attempt each per turn; pair with most hits wins.
drills.cues: Slightly sideways; toss gently into the hitting spot; reach up from the trophy position with a good throw.
drills.progression: Count hits in a set time; count consecutive hits.
drills.regression: Practise the toss alone; practise the throw alone.
drills.video: None verified.

drills.name: Serve Pyramids
drills.works: Diagonal serving; throw → drop-hit → underhand → overhand progression.
drills.players: Two pairs per court (server + returner); red or orange balls; pyramid spot at the side of the court.
drills.setup: Server and returner diagonal across the net (Orange: both on the 60-ft baseline).
drills.steps: Red: server throws a red ball diagonally into the box; returner catches and throws back. Each successful serve + return adds a ball to the 4-ball pyramid. Switch roles after a pyramid; switch court sides after a full rotation. Orange: server serves, returner hits back, server traps.
drills.cues: Turned to the side, throwing arm bent, hand behind the head (Red); toss with control and reach up to the contact point (Orange).
drills.progression: Red: server drop-hits, returner traps and drop-hits back → server hits underhand out of the air, returner traps after the bounce. Orange: serve, return and rally one ball each to score → full court, return must go away from the server.
drills.regression: Move to the service line.
drills.video: None verified.

drills.name: Climb Serve Mountain
drills.works: Builds serve distance progressively, only when successful.
drills.players: Two teams of 2-3; racquets; balls; markers at short/medium/long distances.
drills.setup: Three serving distances from the net marked on the serving side; target = diagonal service box.
drills.steps: Serve diagonally into the box: short = 1 point, medium = 2, long = 3. Start at the shortest distance and move back after each success. Switch with a teammate after three attempts. First team to a target (e.g., 30/40/50) wins. Can be played individually.
drills.cues: Slightly sideways, racquet above head near the contact point ("high five position"); continental or slight forehand grip; hit in front of the leading foot, above the head, strings to target.
drills.progression: Serve from the baseline only; smaller target.
drills.regression: Bigger balls; serve to the same half of the court.
drills.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2W4zdjPpZa8 — "Serve Challenge using Red, Orange, Green & Yellow Tennis Balls." — Be Gr8 at Tennis - Rob Cherry

drills.name: Serve/Return Progression (red overhand serve)
drills.works: Moving from throw to abbreviated overhand serve; stance.
drills.players: Pairs, two per court; racquets; red balls; TDLs/chalk.
drills.setup: Partners diagonal across the net in the middle of the service boxes; a TDL/chalk line as a "baseline" to stand behind.
drills.steps: (1) Throw from a turned position; partner bounces, catches, throws back. (2) Abbreviated-motion overhand serve; partner traps and serves back. (3) Receiver returns the serve; server traps on the strings. After four sequences, swap server.
drills.cues: Feet at about 45° to the baseline; challenge each player individually — not everyone reaches every step.
drills.progression: Play out points (see Capture the Cone).
drills.regression: Move forward; drop-hit serve.
drills.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=F-9zt5V8dSk — "Serve Tennis Lesson for Kids - My Daddy / My Coach #18" — Cosmin | WebTennis24

drills.name: No Bounce → Volley Ball (LTA Go volley progression)
drills.works: Swinging at volleys; grip changes (one grip for both sides); catching to the side at waist height.
drills.players: Pairs; tennis balls; racquets; TDLs, cones, barrier tape net; "ice cream" cones as catching aids.
drills.setup: Pairs facing each other (No Bounce in open space; Volley Ball over a net/tape).
drills.steps: *No Bounce:* two-hand throw to partner; partner claps once, then catches before the ball bounces. *Volley Ball:* one player throws underarm to partner's forehand; hitter volleys it over the net for the thrower to catch; 10 each, swap; repeat on the backhand side; third set the thrower may go to either side but must call it before releasing.
drills.cues: Catch one-handed, to the side, about waist high (mimics a volley); hold the racquet like a hammer or magic wand so one grip works both sides; the ball goes where the strings point.
drills.progression: One-hand same-side catches; thrower moves left/right after throwing and the volleyer redirects to the new spot.
drills.regression: Solo throw-clap-catch (add claps); hold the racquet head in two hands in front of the face and just block the ball back (target = strings); "Different": catch with two cones and send back; pat the ball back with a palm-up high-five.
drills.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bpNXq48XAiI — "Tennis Volley Drill for Kids" — ExpertTennis

drills.name: Self Volley Keep Ups
drills.works: Soft hands; stable face; continental grip.
drills.players: Individuals; racquet + ball.
drills.setup: Each player in a volley-ready spot.
drills.steps: Keep the ball up continuously on the strings without a bounce. After each set (e.g., 5 or 10) move to the next position: standing → on one knee → on two knees → sitting cross-legged. First to finish all four positions wins.
drills.cues: Continental grip; contact between waist and shoulder, out in front.
drills.progression: Alternate FH/BH; backhand only; more volleys per position.
drills.regression: Pause between positions; fewer volleys per position.
drills.video: None verified.

drills.name: Throw to Volley / Toss, Hit, Catch-Volley
drills.works: Catching action instead of swinging; directing volleys down the line vs crosscourt.
drills.players: TC: pairs. NG Orange: groups of three per half-court; orange balls; TDL/poly-spot home base.
drills.setup: NG Orange: volleyer about 4 ft from the net in the middle of the service box on a home-base marker; feeder about 4 ft from the net on the other side with balls; catcher on the feeder's side standing on the service line.
drills.steps: TC: feeder throws underhand to the net player, who volleys forehands back; feeder catching on one bounce = point. NG: feeder tosses to the forehand above waist height; volleyer hits to the feeder's right (down the line), next ball to the feeder's left (crosscourt); catcher moves to catch after the bounce. After six balls rotate (feeder → volleyer → catcher → feeder).
drills.cues: Racquet up, extend your hand toward the target (NG); sideways, continental grip, "catching action" with strings to target, contact in front between waist and shoulder, recover (TC).
drills.progression: Backhand side; alternate sides; random feeds; groundstroke-to-volley rally in pairs.
drills.regression: Feeder closer; feeder catches with two hands.
drills.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6qwVWIYRW3c — "Improving Reactions And Fun Tennis Volley Drill" — Feel Tennis Instruction

drills.name: Up-and-Back Volley
drills.ages: Orange 8-10 (NG Orange C2; manual aimed at older beginners)
drills.works: Coming forward after an approach; split-stepping on partner's hit.
drills.players: Pairs, two per court; racquets; orange balls.
drills.setup: Half-court; partners start on opposite service lines.
drills.steps: P1 drop-hits an approach to P2, moves in, split-steps. P2 hits back; P1 volleys back; P2 lets it bounce and traps. P1 retreats to the service line; P2 now drop-hits an approach and comes in. Repeat.
drills.cues: Split step when your partner hits.
drills.progression: Rally every ball without traps; play the point out once each player has been to the net.
drills.regression: Feed by hand; volleyer starts closer.
drills.video: None verified.

drills.name: Make 'Em Move
drills.ages: Orange 8-10 (NG Orange C2); works for Red 7+
drills.works: "Chasing the ball with feet planted" and not recovering — the catcher must move to the ball and return to base every time.
drills.players: Pairs; one orange ball; one TDL per pair; up to four pairs per side.
drills.setup: Partners on the same side of the net, 4-6 ft apart; catcher's TDL = "home base".
drills.steps: Feeder tosses to one side of the catcher with enough height to reach; catcher catches one-handed (right hand on right, left on left), tosses back, recovers to home base. Switch every minute.
drills.cues: Recover to home base after every catch; same-side hand.
drills.progression: Vary high/low and deep/short; increase distance; on high balls catch with opposite foot and hand forward.
drills.regression: Two-hand catch; slower, higher tosses.
drills.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OuHTPCK3EpE — "4 Best Drills to BOOST Movement for Advanced Kids Under 10 | Tennis Lesson" — Tennis With Ema

drills.name: Floor Rally with Recovery
drills.skill: Movement + rally direction (crosscourt / down the line)
drills.works: Recovering with shuffle steps; set up sideways; contact in front.
drills.players: Pairs; racquets; red ball; home-base markers.
drills.setup: Red court; each player starts on a home-base marker (centre recovery spot).
drills.steps: Push along the ground: one player alternates crosscourt then down the line, the other always pushes back to the same corner. Continuous; rally ends if the ball goes out or leaves the ground. Longest rally wins.
drills.cues: Shuffle back to the centre after every push; sideways to send and receive; contact in front of the leading foot, racquet facing the target.
drills.progression: One player always crosscourt, the other always down the line; count passes in 2 minutes.
drills.regression: One direction only; allow stopping the ball before pushing.
drills.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qX07RV8JFaY — "Ball Control Tennis Drill Kids Ages 6-9 Years" — Elite Sports Clubs

drills.name: Triangles
drills.works: Shoulder turn; changing direction.
drills.players: Groups of three (or four); racquets; orange balls; half-court per group if two groups share.
drills.setup: Two feeders on one side in the middle of the service box(es); hitter on the opposite service line.
drills.steps: Feeder 1 tosses to the hitter's forehand; hitter sends it to Feeder 2, who catches and tosses back; hitter changes direction each time. After three sequences rotate one spot. With four, two hitters alternate after two sequences.
drills.cues: Turn the shoulder on each groundstroke and reach to the target.
drills.progression: Backhand; feeders drop-hit and trap; all three rally cooperatively.
drills.regression: Hitter self-rallies first.
drills.video: None verified.

drills.name: Build Up (crosscourt rally goals)
drills.works: Recovering to the middle; consistent crosscourt.
drills.players: Pairs, two per court diagonal; orange balls.
drills.setup: Both players start on the service line, diagonal; for right-handers, forehands on the deuce side and backhands on the ad side.
drills.steps: Coach sets a rally number (e.g., 4); once reached, the goal rises by 2.
drills.cues: Recover to the middle, ready for partner's next shot.
drills.progression: Move to the baseline, any stroke; one stroke only.
drills.regression: Lower starting goal; service-line distance.
drills.video: None verified.

drills.name: In To Net (LTA Go warm-up)
drills.works: Athletic stance; moving forward and back quickly; listening.
drills.players: Pairs; TDLs.
drills.setup: Partners face each other 2+ m apart.
drills.steps: Coach calls a body part; partners move forward and connect (right-hand high five, left hands, both hands, right feet, left feet, both feet), then return to the start.
drills.cues: "Goalie stance" to get switched on; when sidestepping, feet wider than shoulders and head well lowered.
drills.progression: Number codes (1 = right hands … 6 = both feet) for cognitive challenge; combine numbers.
drills.regression: Fewer commands (hands only or feet only).
drills.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DBVEku_UX2E — "Tennis at home - Double Trouble (8-11 years old)" — LTA (an LTA at-home activity video; not the same game)

drills.name: Tag-Team Singles
drills.skill: First point play / rally with rotation
drills.works: Getting many turns; continuous play; team record.
drills.players: Two teams of 4-6 per court; racquets; red balls.
drills.setup: Teams on opposite sides, each in a line behind the service line; points played at the centre, halfway between service line and net (C3: middle of service box).
drills.steps: First player drop-hits over and runs to the back of the line; receiver traps and drop-hits back (C3: rallies it back) and goes to the back; continue until a miss. Try for an overall team record.
drills.cues: Hit and move to the back of the line quickly [added].
drills.progression: Courts compete for the longest rally; play competitively.
drills.regression: Bump up and hit; allow multiple bounces.
drills.source: [NG-Red](https://www.usta.com/content/dam/usta/content-fragments/tennis-service-center/assets/pdfs/Net-Generation-Community-Manual-Red.pdf) (C2 Ch.6; C3 Ch.2, Ch.5). Tennis Canada "Tag Team Tennis" (G7) is a competitive cousin: pairs, each partner plays 2 points then high-fives the partner in, continuous score to 7 or 10 — [TC-LTP](https://assets.tenniscanada.com/production/PDFs/LearnToPlay_ENG.pdf)
drills.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lkwawy09alg — "Net Generation- Red Ball Team Challenge - USTA Middle States" — USTAMiddleStates

drills.name: Endless Bounce
drills.level: Ready to move up (first competitive points)
drills.works: Playing points before strokes are perfect — any number of bounces keeps the ball alive.
drills.players: Teams of 3-4, two teams per court; racquets; red balls.
drills.setup: Teams on opposite sides; service boxes = boundaries; players spread out.
drills.steps: Start with a drop-hit forehand. Any number of bounces is allowed; players may bump the ball up or pass to a teammate. Point ends when the ball starts rolling or hits the net/fence. First to 4, then restart; after two games switch opponents or rebalance teams.
drills.cues: Keep it alive — bump, bounce, send [added].
drills.progression: Backhands only; maximum two bounces.
drills.regression: Rolling rally.
drills.video: None verified.

drills.name: Capture the Cone
drills.works: Serve-and-return under a scoring incentive.
drills.players: Two teams of 2-3 per court (1v1 matches); 5-7 cones per team; TDLs/chalk.
drills.setup: Each team's cones lined up on its own side, outside the court near the net. Points from the middle of the service box.
drills.steps: Serve (drop-hit or out of the air). Not returned → server wins; returned → returner wins. Winner runs to the opponent's side and claims a cone. Play by time: most cones (or all cones) wins. Switch serving team each game.
drills.cues: Turned to the side for the serve (NG serve cue).
drills.progression: Play out the whole point; serve to a designated half of the box.
drills.regression: Toss the serve; trap and drop-hit the return.
drills.video: None verified.

drills.name: Throw Tennis
drills.skill: Point play (serve, rally, score without a racquet)
drills.works: Understanding serve-rally-score and moving an opponent before racquet skills are reliable.
drills.players: Pairs; ball; red court.
drills.setup: Opponents on either side of a red-court net.
drills.steps: Server starts with an overhead throw anywhere in the area; returner catches after one bounce and throws back underhand anywhere. Point ends on a double bounce, ball out or in the net, or a catch in the air.
drills.cues: Coach evaluates teaching points but keeps play flowing.
drills.progression: One hand; catch in the air; one player crosscourt only, other down the line.
drills.regression: Two bounces before catching; two-hand catches.
drills.video: None verified.

drills.name: Floor Tennis
drills.works: Competing on the ground before over-the-net hitting; moving the opponent.
drills.players: Pairs; racquets; red ball.
drills.setup: Both players on the same side of the net with a marked playing area.
drills.steps: Serve by pushing the ball along the ground into the opponent's area; opponent stops it and pushes it back anywhere. Point ends if the ball leaves the ground or goes out.
drills.cues: Stop it, aim it, push it [added].
drills.progression: Alternate FH/BH; push without stopping; bigger area; one player rolls crosscourt, the other down the line.
drills.regression: FH or BH only; smaller area.
drills.source: [TC-LTP](https://assets.tenniscanada.com/production/PDFs/LearnToPlay_ENG.pdf) (Play Activity G2); LTA lists a "Floor Tennis" at-home video — [LTA Tennis at Home](https://www.lta.org.uk/play-compete/lta-youth/tennis-at-home/)
drills.video: LTA Floor Tennis video exists per the LTA page but its YouTube ID was not retrieved/verified.

drills.name: Stop Tennis
drills.works: Short matches with frequent wins; keeping score out loud.
drills.players: Pairs on multiple red/orange courts.
drills.setup: One pair per mini-court.
drills.steps: Regular points; spin for serve; alternate server every 2 points. All matches start on "GO"; the first player anywhere to reach the target score (5, 7 or 9) shouts "STOP" and all matches end. Whoever leads in each match gets a win; draws give both a win. Rotate and replay.
drills.cues: Call the score out loud (TC "Good Sport" behaviour).
drills.progression: Serve to opponent's backhand; win points at the net.
drills.regression: Drop-bounce-hit serve; self-rally allowed; smaller area.
drills.video: None verified.

drills.name: Team Cones (and Up & Down)
drills.works: Individual matches that feed a team score (reduces pressure of losing).
drills.players: Two teams; one large base cone per team at the side of the court; small cones.
drills.setup: 1v1 matches across available courts; team base cones at the side.
drills.steps: Spin for serve; play to 5 or 7 (alternate serve every 2). Winner puts a small cone on the team base; wait for a new opponent from the other team. Timed (10/15/20 min); most cones wins. *Up & Down:* court split into four positions with two players each; winners move up a position, losers down; 4-minute matches; tie → one deciding point.
drills.cues: Shake hands after each game (TC Good Sport behaviour).
drills.progression: Win points from the net; hit to open space.
drills.regression: Self-rally allowed; smaller area.
drills.video: None verified.

drills.name: Four-Square
drills.works: Hitting to space instead of back to the opponent.
drills.players: Two teams of 2-3 per court; orange balls; TDLs/poly-spots.
drills.setup: Full 60-ft orange court; each side divided into four equal squares; the short/deep dividing line about 5 ft in front of the service line.
drills.steps: Singles points starting with serve and return. After the serve, a player may not hit into the same square twice in a row. Players struggling may drop-hit the second serve.
drills.cues: Find a new square every shot [added].
drills.progression: Each player names a "black hole" square the opponent may not hit into.
drills.regression: Play inside the service boxes.
drills.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4Dh5oKAey0A — "The INs and OUTs of Orange Ball Tennis" — Kristin W

drills.name: Gladiator
drills.works: Serving and playing points under fun pressure; net play.
drills.players: Pairs, up to five per court; orange balls.
drills.setup: 60-ft doubles court (sidelines = regulation singles lines); one-up/one-back formation. One team = Champs on one side; Challengers lined up behind the opposite service line.
drills.steps: Challengers serve to the Champs and play the point, then rotate to the back of the line. Challengers keep their own score; at 2 points, before serving, they must shout "Gladiator" — win that point and they take the Champs' side (no shout = no takeover). New Champs: challengers count down 3-2-1 before serving.
drills.cues: Keep the ball deep crosscourt, away from the net person.
drills.progression: Any outright winner takes the Champs spot; a winning volley after approaching takes it.
drills.regression: Singles; play inside the service boxes.
drills.video: None verified.

drills.name: Positive-Negative
drills.works: Consistency first, then competition.
drills.players: Two pairs per court (half-court); orange balls.
drills.setup: Half-court singles.
drills.steps: Coach sets a rally number (e.g., 6 or 8). Rally starts with a serve; both players start at 0. If the rally breaks before the number, the player who erred goes −1; once past the number, whoever didn't make the error gets +1. Two-minute rounds, then switch opponents.
drills.cues: Make one more ball than your partner [added].
drills.progression: Crosscourt with one stroke; full court; serve-and-return games to 3 or 4.
drills.regression: Lower target number.
drills.video: None verified.

drills.name: Simple Forehands & Backhands (stationary hand-feed)
drills.ages: green 9-11; adult beginner. The source targets "beginners & kids".
drills.works: grip, basic swing shape, follow-through; first contact for brand-new players
drills.players: 1 hitter + 1 feeder; basket of balls. [A] Use green ball for juniors and orange/green ball for adult beginners, matching the USTA adult plan.
drills.setup: The hitter stands at the centre of the service line, where the centre line meets the SL. The feeder stands 4-6 ft to the side of the hitter on the same side of the net, holding the basket. The feeder demonstrates the grip and the stroke first.
drills.steps: (1) The feeder tosses so the ball bounces waist-high in front of the hitter. (2) The hitter plays a forehand (or backhand) over the net, focusing on the follow-through. (3) Repeat on the other side. (4) Score = successful hits over the net.
drills.cues: "Start racquet at waist height"; "strong follow-through" (Tennis Companion). "Shake hands with the racquet" (Eastern grip); grip pressure "about a 3 out of 10" ([USTA forehand basics](https://www.usta.com/en/home/improve/tips-and-instruction/national/learning-the-basics--forehand.html)).
drills.progression: D2 (feed from across the net), then D3 (side to side).
drills.regression: start with the racquet already at the contact point, out in front, then add the finish. This is the USTA adult forehand demo sequence: "racquet in front, starting at contact point", then "racquet to side, extend to finish" ([USTA Tennis 101 for Adults](https://www.usta.com/content/dam/usta/content-fragments/tennis-service-center/assets/pdfs/USTA-Tennis-101-for-Adults.pdf)).
drills.source: [Tennis Companion – 12 Essential Tennis Drills for Beginners & Kids](https://tenniscompanion.org/12-essential-tennis-drills-for-beginners-and-kids/)
drills.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FD7kpvPTj3M — "26 Tennis Forehand Drills - Hand & Racket Feeding To Improve Technique" — Martin Kares Tennistraining

drills.name: Ball-Toss Forehands & Backhands (moving ball, fed from across the net)
drills.works: judging ball speed and depth; adjusting feet before the swing (helps late contact and crowding)
drills.players: 1 hitter + 1 feeder; basket
drills.setup: The hitter is in ready position at the centre of the SL. The feeder is on the opposite side at the centre service line, 2-3 ft from the net, with the basket.
drills.steps: (1) The feeder gently tosses so the ball bounces about waist-high to the hitter. (2) The hitter judges speed, adjusts footwork, and hits the forehand or backhand. (3) Alternate sides after each basket.
drills.cues: "Judge the bounce, move your feet"; "turn sideways early" [A]
drills.progression: D3 (alternate sides, unannounced)
drills.regression: D1
drills.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hAfiW1YHyHY — "The Top Tennis Drills For Beginners - Learn To Rally From Day One" — Patrick Smith Tennis Coaching

drills.name: Side-to-Side Forehands and Backhands
drills.level: beginner to intermediate. The source calls it intermediate: it "tests anticipation and grip switching".
drills.works: grip change between wings; lateral movement; flat feet; crowding
drills.players: 1 hitter + 1 feeder; basket
drills.setup: Same as D2: hitter at the centre of the SL, feeder across the net at the centre service line, 2-3 ft from the net.
drills.steps: (1) The feeder alternates tosses to the forehand and backhand. (2) The hitter switches grip, moves, hits, and recovers to the centre. (3) Advanced: the feeder does not say which side is coming.
drills.cues: "Keep racquet head high" in the ready position (source)
drills.progression: unannounced random feeds; [A] racquet feeds from the baseline
drills.regression: D2 (one side per basket)
drills.video: none verified for this exact drill (see D1 video for feeding variations)

drills.name: Forward and Backward Forehands & Backhands
drills.works: judging depth and speed; dynamic footwork; hitting off the back foot or reaching for short balls
drills.players: 1 hitter + 1 feeder; basket
drills.setup: The hitter is at the centre of the SL. The feeder is on the opposite side at the centre service line, 2-3 ft from the net.
drills.steps: (1) A moderate-depth toss that needs no movement. (2) A shorter toss, so the hitter moves forward. (3) A longer toss, so the hitter moves back. (4) The hitter returns to the SL between shots. (5) Advanced: don't announce short, neutral or long.
drills.cues: "Position yourself to catch the ball at about waist height" (source)
drills.progression: unannounced depth; [A] racquet-feed from the opposite baseline with varied spin
drills.regression: announce depth before each feed
drills.video: none verified for this exact drill

drills.name: Hit and Catch
drills.ages: green 9-11 (Sportplan lists it for orange/green ball); adult beginner [A]
drills.works: directing the ball to a person; control over power
drills.players: 2 players; 1 cone used as a "catching cup"; basket
drills.setup: The player is in ready position at the centre of the SL. The feeder/catcher stands on the opposite side on the centre line, halfway between the net and the SL, holding an upturned cone.
drills.steps: (1) The feeder tosses to the player's forehand. (2) The player hits straight back to the feeder. (3) The feeder catches it in the cone, in the air or off the bounce. (4) Repeat on the backhand, then switch roles. (5) Score = successful hit-and-catches.
drills.cues: "Direct the shot to your partner"; "small swing, short distance" (USTA adult cue, cross-applied [A])
drills.progression: alternate forehand and backhand without announcing it (source)
drills.regression: catcher catches with hands [A]
drills.video: none verified

drills.name: Rally Now! / Build Up (step-back cooperative rally — the USTA adult beginner core)
drills.ages: adult beginner (the source is the USTA adult plan); green 9-11 [A]; senior beginner [A]
drills.works: first sustained rallies; matching swing size to distance
drills.players: pairs. Red or foam ball on a 36-ft or 42-ft court, then orange ball on 60 ft, then green ball on 78 ft. Each player has a target in front of them, and boundaries are marked with chalk or TDLs.
drills.setup: Partners face each other on opposite sides of the net, about 10 ft from the net, each with a target in front. In "Build Up", partners start in the middle of the service box on a half-court.
drills.steps:
- **Rally Now:** cooperative forehand/backhand rally aimed at the targets. After a rally of six shots, both players take one big step back, until they reach the SL.
- **Build Up:** the coach sets a rally goal (for example 4). Once reached, raise the goal by 2.
- **Later class:** after six shots with red balls, step back to the 60-ft baseline, switch to the orange ball, and aim to bounce the ball between the SL and the 60-ft baseline. Then use the green ball from the 78-ft baseline.
drills.cues: "Small swing, short distance. Distance affects technique."; "Small swing, short distance; bigger swing, greater distance."; "Ready position and react." (source)
drills.progression: Level 2 crosscourt; Build Up levels go forehand only, then backhand only, then move to the SL. Score a point each time the ball bounces between the SL and baseline, first to 10.
drills.regression: "Instant Rally": tap the ball up eye-high off the strings, palm up, then knuckles up. Then self-rally on a target, partner rally on a target, and partner rally over a line.
drills.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YQcKqXI2Jcw — "Beginner Tennis: Learn to Rally Fast!" — Coach Josh Morain

drills.name: Ten to Move On (mini-tennis to baseline)
drills.ages: yellow 11-14; teens; adult intermediate. The source says intermediate-advanced. [A] Use 5 balls per stage for green ball or adult beginners.
drills.works: consistency under a target; scaling swing length as distance grows
drills.players: 4 players (2 pairs) on one court; 1 ball per pair
drills.setup: Each pair faces each other across the net. Everyone starts on the service line opposite their partner, one pair per half-court.
drills.steps:
1. Rally 10 balls kept only inside the opposite service box.
2. Move to halfway between the SL and baseline and rally 10 balls anywhere in the half-court.
3. Move to the baseline and rally 10.
4. Move back to the halfway position and rally 10.
5. Finish at the SL with 10.
- The first pair to complete the whole sequence wins.
drills.cues: "Same rhythm, longer swing as you move back" [A]
drills.progression: forehands only or backhands only; crosscourt only [A]
drills.regression: 5-ball stages; let the ball bounce twice [A]
drills.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=526H8zXwp2w — "How To Develop Consistent Rally Skills At Any Level Even As A Beginner #tennis" — Patrick Smith Tennis Coaching

drills.name: Mini-Tennis Crosscourt (green warm-up)
drills.ages: green 9-11; yellow 11-14; all adults as a warm-up [A]
drills.works: crosscourt direction; using width
drills.players: 2 pairs per court; green balls
drills.setup: Each pair uses a half-court. All players stand on the service line and hit into the service box plus alley.
drills.steps: (1) Pairs rally crosscourt with the outside stroke only (the forehand-to-forehand diagonal for two right-handers). (2) Switch sides after 2 minutes.
drills.cues: "Take advantage of extra width" (goal)
drills.progression: (1) rally into the corners of the service box; (2) rally with more angle into the alleys. "Mini-Tennis Angles" variant: TDLs split the service box in half horizontally; alternate short sharp angles with deep balls between the TDL and the SL; play points with a bonus for the alley.
drills.regression: straight-ahead mini-tennis [A]
drills.source: [USTA Net Generation Green Ball plans, Green 2 ch. 1-2](https://www.usta.com/content/dam/usta/content-fragments/tennis-service-center/assets/pdfs/Net-Generation-Practice-Plan-Green.pdf)
drills.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uuKtDEXCVnA — "Green ball players drills and exercises: MINI-TENNIS VARIATIONS" — Fitness Instructional Tenis

drills.name: Tempo Drill (one-minute rally count)
drills.works: consistency with spin and speed; a measurable baseline
drills.players: 2-3 pairs per court; 1 ball per pair; timer
drills.setup: Every player on the baseline, with pairs straight across from each other.
drills.steps: (1) Count how many balls the pair can rally in 1 minute with one ball. (2) After a miss, restart at the same number (Green 2 version). (3) Repeat and try to beat the record.
drills.cues: "Hit with spin and speed to increase numbers". The USTA coaching tip says depth is key on the green court. Encourage players to use the lower body to start and then extend the hands all the way through. Players who just hit high, loopy topspin to keep the ball deep will struggle as the game gets more advanced.
drills.progression: straight ahead, then crosscourt with recovery; straight ahead with one stroke; crosscourt with the outside stroke
drills.regression: start from the SL [A]
drills.source: [USTA Green Ball plans, Green 2 ch. 3 & Green 1 ch. 1](https://www.usta.com/content/dam/usta/content-fragments/tennis-service-center/assets/pdfs/Net-Generation-Practice-Plan-Green.pdf)
drills.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ScaOTd2t56o — "7-6-5-4-3-2-1-Go! Tennis Coaching Drill: Rally Consistency with Students" — Cosmin | WebTennis24

drills.name: Alley Rally
drills.works: straight-line direction control; extension through the ball
drills.players: 2 pairs per court; 1 ball per pair
drills.setup: All players on the baseline. Each pair stands in, and hits into, its own doubles alley (one pair per alley).
drills.steps: (1) Rally back and forth inside the doubles alley. (2) Recover outside the alley after each shot. (3) Rally for numbers; a miss resets to zero.
drills.cues: "Stay consistent, hitting with square stance and good extension" (goal)
drills.progression: one stroke only, then alternate strokes; topspin only, then slice only
drills.regression: start from the SL; count misses-allowed [A]
drills.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ixAA_8GikaY — "How to Rally & Hit with Direction | USTA Coaching" — United States Tennis Association (USTA)

drills.name: Up and Down the River (depth game)
drills.works: keeping the ball deep with height, spin and speed
drills.players: 2 pairs per court; TDLs
drills.setup: Each pair uses a half-court. Boundaries run from the middle of the court to the doubles sideline, so alleys are in. TDLs split the court from the service line to the baseline. [A] This means extending the centre line through the backcourt so each half has its own deep zone.
drills.steps: (1) Start points after a serve and return. (2) Both players must let the ball bounce. (3) Play to 4 points, then volley cooperatively until the last court finishes. (4) The winner moves up a court and the loser moves down.
drills.cues: "Use height, spin, and speed to keep ball deep" (goal)
drills.progression: start points straight ahead with one stroke; play crosscourt with the outside stroke only. "Depth Games" variant: every ball must bounce between the SL and baseline.
drills.regression: cooperative count of balls landing past the SL before playing points [A]
drills.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DVRyIjzJ3kI — "Complete Green Ball Class: Rally, Volley, & Point Play" — New Rochelle Racquet Club

drills.name: Height for Depth
drills.ages: yellow 11-14; teens; adult intermediate. The source does not give a level; it appears intermediate.
drills.works: netting; short balls; low net clearance
drills.players: pairs; spare racquets
drills.setup: Pairs on opposite baselines rally up and down the middle of the court. Racquets are placed in the net to force a higher trajectory. [A] Stand them along the net tape so the effective net height rises.
drills.steps: (1) Cooperative rally for the longest possible exchange. (2) Every shot must land beyond the service box. (3) The rally restarts if the ball lands long, wide, short, or in the net. (4) Pairs compete for the longest rally in a set time.
drills.cues: keep proper striking technique and don't just push for consistency ("players can sometimes start to push the ball too much"); "hit through the ball"
drills.progression: a deeper zone, for example 3/4 court [A]; crosscourt only [A]
drills.regression: remove the racquets; count balls past the SL only [A]
drills.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=n9tDwKz1x64 — "Tennis Drill: More Power And Depth On Your Forehand" — Online Tennis Instruction

drills.name: Net-Clearance Crosscourt
drills.works: abbreviated finish / decelerating; netted balls
drills.players: 2 players; [A] a rope or string above the net, or just a visual target
drills.setup: [A] Two players on opposite baselines on the deuce diagonal, rallying forehands crosscourt.
drills.steps: Rally crosscourt forehands with a height goal of 3-4 ft over the net (PlayYourCourt). The LTA similarly recommends rallies aimed at targets a few feet above the net cord, to avoid netting and gain depth.
drills.cues: "Finish over the non-dominant shoulder"; "swing as if hitting three stacked balls" (PlayYourCourt)
drills.progression: add a deep target zone past the SL [A]; backhand diagonal
drills.regression: start at the SL with half swings [A]
drills.source: [PlayYourCourt – Why your forehand has no power (2026)](https://www.playyourcourt.com/news/why-your-forehand-has-no-power-and-how-to-fix-it-for-good/); [LTA – How to play better tennis rallies](https://www.lta.org.uk/play/tennis-tips-and-techniques/how-to-play-better-tennis-rallies/) (from search summary, not fetched)
drills.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zEz9vrm3QYw — "My Top 3 Drills For Rally Quality - Classroom Tennis Lesson (Ep2)" — The Tennis Mentor

drills.name: Call the Bounce
drills.works: flat feet; late reading of depth; hitting off the back foot
drills.players: 2-3 pairs per court
drills.setup: Pairs use a half-court, with all players spread along the baseline.
drills.steps: (1) Rally straight ahead. (2) As the ball comes back, call "up", "back" or "stay", then move to that spot to return it. (3) Follow a really short "up" ball to the net, finish the rally, then move back.
drills.cues: "Call location and move to ball as it crosses net" (goal)
drills.progression: rally crosscourt; any stroke, then one stroke, then alternate strokes
drills.regression: coach calls the depth [A]
drills.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XR83yXLla8w — "Tennis Split Step Timing, Execution And Drills" — Feel Tennis Instruction

drills.name: X Drill (deep roll + short angle)
drills.works: moving diagonally up and back; heavy topspin from deep; attacking a short ball
drills.players: groups of 3 (feeder + 2 hitters). Green 1 version: pairs. Targets: cones or spots.
drills.setup: One hitter stands at the centre of the baseline, with the other waiting behind at a safe distance. The feeder stands mid-court, between the baseline and SL, on the same side as the hitters, with balls. Targets go in the deep and short corners on the other side. Green 1 version: hitters stand mid-baseline of a half-court and the tosser stands in the service box on the same side.
drills.steps: (1) The feeder tosses high and deep to one side. The hitter backs up, returns high and deep crosscourt with heavy topspin, and recovers to the middle. (2) The second feed is high and short to the opposite side. The hitter plays a short angle (Green 1: an aggressive ball to the corner) and recovers. (3) Repeat to the opposite sides. (4) Do 2 sequences (Green 1: 4), then switch hitters and later the feeder.
drills.cues: "Move in diagonals up and back using appropriate stances"; "drop-step and cross moving to deep ball, increased racquet speed on high loop" (goals)
drills.progression: hand-feed, then racquet-feed from the other side of the net, then the coach feeds faster; short angle or rip to the corner; play competitively as teams
drills.regression: feed to one wing only, at walking pace [A]
drills.source: [USTA Green Ball plans, Green 2 ch. 1 & Green 1 ch. 1](https://www.usta.com/content/dam/usta/content-fragments/tennis-service-center/assets/pdfs/Net-Generation-Practice-Plan-Green.pdf)
drills.video: none verified for this drill

drills.name: Crazy Feed (heavy-topspin attack game)
drills.works: high, heavy, deep topspin to the weaker wing; balls that go long because they are hit flat
drills.players: teams of 3-4; full court
drills.setup: Teams on opposite baselines; 2 players play at a time.
drills.steps: (1) The attacker self-feeds a deep ball from behind the baseline, hitting high and deep to the opponent's weakness. (2) Play out the point. The attacker can't come to the net off the feed. (3) Rotate every point. (4) Attackers score 1 for a won point and defenders score 2. First to 7, then change opponents.
drills.cues: "Take advantage of increased length and width by rolling balls deep to corners" (goal)
drills.progression: self-feed forehands, then backhands. The defender feeds a high, deep ball with little spin, and the attacker hits back with heavy topspin.
drills.regression: cooperative "roll it deep" count [A]
drills.video: none verified

drills.name: Figure 8 (cooperative change of direction)
drills.ages: green 9-11 (USTA Green 1 warm-up); yellow; teens; adult intermediate-advanced (Tennis Australia uses a fed "Figure 8" for squads)
drills.skill: direction (crosscourt / down the line), rally consistency
drills.works: controlled change of direction; footwork between wings
drills.players: 2 pairs per court (USTA). TA version: coach-fed.
drills.setup: Each pair uses a half-court (USTA warm-up). One player hits only down the line and the other only crosscourt, so the ball traces a figure 8. Start from the SL, then move to the baseline.
drills.steps: (1) Rally cooperatively, with one side hitting down the line and the other crosscourt. (2) Move the partner a few feet right and left using the outside stroke. (3) After each side has hit both directions, repeat from the baseline. TA lists "Figure 8 (one hit, focus on footwork)" and "Figure 8 (two hits, focus on footwork)" among its 2-ball coach-fed drills.
drills.cues: "Find a rally pace you can control with appropriate speed and spin" (USTA goal)
drills.progression: a set number of shots before switching; slice and topspin from the SL; one side hits all forehands
drills.regression: from the SL only, with a set number of shots [A]
drills.source: [USTA Green Ball plans, Green 1 ch. 1](https://www.usta.com/content/dam/usta/content-fragments/tennis-service-center/assets/pdfs/Net-Generation-Practice-Plan-Green.pdf); [Tennis Australia – Tennis Time Coaching Manual (Geoff Quinlan), "Drills and Activities"](https://www.tennis.com.au/wp-content/uploads/2010/08/Drills-and-Activities.pdf)
drills.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_BSepO2e67c — title: `"Corner Rally" - Tennis Stroke Precision Drill - "Drill of the Week" #031` — Martin Kares Tennistraining

drills.name: Centre Third, Outside Third
drills.works: placing to the middle vs. out wide; using spin and angle
drills.players: 2 pairs per court; TDLs
drills.setup: Pairs hit on a diagonal. On one side of the net, TDLs divide the court lengthwise into thirds, and the SL serves as the baseline (mini-court).
drills.steps: (1) One player hits every ball to the same crosscourt spot. (2) The other alternates between the middle third and the outside third. (3) Switch roles, then switch sides.
drills.cues: "Move player out wide by increasing spin and angle" (goal)
drills.progression: mark both sides and both hit the same patterns; 2-3 players per court using full service-court patterns
drills.regression: halves instead of thirds [A]
drills.video: none verified

drills.name: Zig-Zagging (4-player crosscourt / down-the-line)
drills.works: hitting a fixed direction under rally pressure; recovery
drills.players: 4 players + 1 coach; basket
drills.setup: Players A and B are on one baseline, one in the deuce half and one in the ad half. C and D are on the opposite baseline. The coach stands at the net post with a basket.
drills.steps: (1) The coach feeds to A. (2) A hits crosscourt to C. (3) C hits down the line to B. (4) B hits crosscourt to D. (5) D hits down the line to A. (6) Repeat until 30 balls are used, then rotate clockwise so everyone practises every target and stroke.
drills.cues: "Crosscourt = high and safe, line = when balanced" [A]
drills.progression: competitive version where an error gives the opposite team a point; first to 5
drills.regression: service-line version with green ball [A]
drills.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ue_A3v2JorE — "This Simple Rally Drill Changed My Game | Tennis Consistency + Precision Workout" — Nuno's Tennis

drills.name: Six by Six (down-the-line, switch on the 7th ball)
drills.works: patience; changing direction only on a planned ball
drills.players: 2 players (+ a counter)
drills.setup: Half-court rally. Player A is on the ad side and Player B on the deuce side, so they face each other straight across: for two right-handers, A's backhand faces B's forehand.
drills.steps: (1) A starts the rally down the line using backhand only. (2) B rallies down the line using forehand only. (3) After 6 consecutive balls over, A sends the next ball crosscourt. (4) Continue 6-ball rallies down the line on the other half. (5) The rally ends on a miss. A coach or third player counts the total balls.
drills.cues: "Patience, consistency under pressure" (source)
drills.progression: 8-10 balls before switching
drills.regression: 4 balls; start from mid-court [A]
drills.video: none verified for this drill

drills.name: Around the World (target spots)
drills.ages: the source lists red/orange 1. [A] Adapted for green 9-11 and adult beginners on the full court.
drills.works: aiming at specific spots; focus under a "second chance" rule
drills.players: group; 6 coloured poly spots; youth racquets; basket
drills.setup: On the side opposite the hitters, place 6 spots: 2 at the baseline near the singles sidelines (deep corners), 2 at the SL on the singles sidelines, 1 at the centre mark, and 1 at the centre of the SL (the T). The coach feeds from the opposite side with a basket.
drills.steps: (1) Players start at "home base" with one chance to hit the target shot. A make advances them; a miss loses the turn. (2) From spot 2 onward they get two chances, and may decline the second and stay put. (3) Taking and making the second chance advances them; missing it sends them back to the start. (4) The object is to get all the way around the spots (the world).
drills.cues: "Pick your spot before the feed" [A]
drills.progression: racquet-feed with varied height; only spot hits count [A]
drills.regression: larger hoops as targets [A]
drills.video: none verified

drills.name: Spanish 4-Ball Feed (deep line / short cross, both wings)
drills.ages: teens; yellow 13-14 competitive; adult advanced [A]. The source is a squad manual.
drills.works: changing between depth and angle under fatigue; recovery
drills.players: 4 players (1 drilling, 1 shadowing, 1 picking up, 1 recovering); coach with basket
drills.setup: The coach feeds from the opposite side of the net. The player starts at the centre of the baseline.
drills.steps: Pattern (i): FH deep down the line, FH short crosscourt, BH deep down the line, BH short crosscourt. Pattern (ii): the same, starting on the backhand. Patterns (ix)/(x): the same deep-line/short-cross sequence, 8 balls each, then rotate.
drills.cues: "Deep line, short cross — recover after every ball" [A]
drills.progression: add a drive volley or approach (TA patterns v-viii)
drills.regression: 2-ball versions (D23)
drills.source: [Tennis Australia – Tennis Time Coaching Manual, "Spanish Feeding Drills"](https://www.tennis.com.au/wp-content/uploads/2010/08/Drills-and-Activities.pdf)
drills.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5rqYya9gIag — "TOP 10 Tennis Forehand Drills [U+1F525 fire emoji] Coach Feeding for Advanced Players" — Martin Kares Tennistraining

drills.name: 2-Ball Deep–Short Feeds
drills.works: adjusting from a deep defensive ball to a short attacking ball
drills.players: coach + players in rotation; basket
drills.setup: The coach feeds from across the net; the player starts at the centre of the baseline.
drills.steps: Four variants: (i) deep FH, then short BH down the line; (ii) deep FH, then short BH crosscourt; (iii) deep BH, then short FH down the line; (iv) deep BH, then short FH crosscourt.
drills.cues: "Up and back, not just side to side" [A]
drills.regression: single-ball deep feeds [A]
drills.source: [Tennis Australia – Tennis Time Coaching Manual, "2 Ball Feeding Drills"](https://www.tennis.com.au/wp-content/uploads/2010/08/Drills-and-Activities.pdf)
drills.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FD7kpvPTj3M — "26 Tennis Forehand Drills - Hand & Racket Feeding To Improve Technique" — Martin Kares Tennistraining

drills.name: Off-Forehand: Inside-Out then Inside-In
drills.works: running around the backhand; changing direction off the forehand
drills.players: coach + player; basket
drills.setup: The coach feeds to the player's backhand-side (ad) half from across the net. The player starts at the centre mark.
drills.steps: TA 2-ball variants: (i) "Off F/H – F/H"; (ii) "Off F/H – Inside-in F/H". The player runs around the backhand and hits an inside-out forehand crosscourt to the opponent's ad court, then hits inside-in down the line. TA also lists "Off F/H's Swedish" as a game-based version (live crosscourt from the ad corners). Video coaches use "2 Inside Out, 1 Inside In".
drills.cues: "Get around the ball early", "hit inside the ball for inside-out" [A]
drills.progression: live ad-court points where only forehands from the ad side count [A]
drills.regression: start already positioned in the ad corner [A]
drills.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7kdaTE0c6Ak — "How to Hit Inside Out & Inside In Forehand" — Intuitive Tennis; https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Xr4lVYmVG3U — "Learn How to Hit the Forehand Inside Out: Master the '2 Inside Out, 1 Inside In' Drill! [U+1F3BE tennis-ball emoji]" — Gaby Paz - Vantage Tennis; https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NR__D2k83zQ — "RSPA Quick Tips -- Inside Out Forehand Drill" — Racquet Sports Professionals Association; https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cv80LxVHD2w — "Tennis Drill - Inside-out Forehand Situations" — Edgar Giffenig Tennis - Effective Instruction

drills.name: Crosscourt Points (half court, alleys in) / Crosscourt–Down-the-Line Count
drills.works: crosscourt consistency under scoring; choosing when to change direction
drills.players: 2-4 players
drills.setup: Diagonal half-court with the doubles lines included.
drills.steps: (1) Crosscourt points, one game on each diagonal, first to 11. (2) "Cross Court – Down the Line": count the shots until an error, alternating after each ball. (3) TA's game-based variants: crosscourt forehands with alternating hitters (focus on footwork, to 11); crosscourt backhands where forehands are allowed (to 15); "Change of Direction" where only the single player on one end may change direction.
drills.cues: TA squad notes: "Worst mistake is hitting into the net"; score activities first to 3/5/7 to raise intensity.
drills.progression: only the lone player may change direction (TA "Change of Direction")
drills.regression: cooperative crosscourt count [A]
drills.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-WJ5UrKXyHE — "National Champions demonstrate top drills for tennis consistency #tennis" — StokkeTennis

drills.name: Absorb and Rip (defend, then attack)
drills.works: taking pace off a ball, then attacking the next one
drills.players: teams of 3-4; TDLs
drills.setup: Teams on opposite baselines, with TDLs splitting the court in half.
drills.steps: (1) Play points straight ahead; either side starts with a drop-hit. (2) "Juggle" the first ball: hit it up in the air off the bounce with a continental grip (up and forward is allowed). Let it bounce again, then rip the next ball. (3) Winners stay on for 2 points; play to a set number, then rotate.
drills.cues: "Use spin on first ball to take pace off and set up for next ball" (goal)
drills.progression: all forehands; one-handed backhand on the first ball and forehand on the second; crosscourt points
drills.regression: cooperative "juggle-and-hit" [A]
drills.video: none verified

drills.name: Sideliner / Sideliner Ping-Pong (width game)
drills.works: using spin and height to move the opponent off the court
drills.players: 4-6 per court; TDLs
drills.setup: Half-court split by TDLs, with alleys counting. All points are played crosscourt; two pairs can play at the same time.
drills.steps: (1) Start with a serve; after that, players must hit their outside stroke. (2) Score for winning the point and for forcing the opponent outside the sideline. (3) Use an up-and-down-the-river or champion-of-the-court format. The ping-pong doubles version has partners alternate hits, all balls must bounce, and games go to 7.
drills.cues: "Use spin and proper height to move ball off court" (goal)
drills.progression: every ball must bounce; full court; volleys count (ping-pong version)
drills.regression: cooperative angle rally (D8 Mini-Tennis Angles)
drills.source: [USTA Green Ball plans, Green 2 ch. 2 & Green 1 ch. 1](https://www.usta.com/content/dam/usta/content-fragments/tennis-service-center/assets/pdfs/Net-Generation-Practice-Plan-Green.pdf)
drills.video: none verified

drills.name: Defend and Recover (angle + court coverage)
drills.works: recovery, split step, angle/line combinations
drills.players: teams of 2-3; full court
drills.setup: The feeder stands on the far right of the baseline, behind the alley. The angler starts at the centre of the baseline.
