drills.steps: (1) The feeder feeds crosscourt to the service box, recovers to the centre, and split-steps with the left foot on the centre mark. (2) The angler moves up, plays a short-court angle, and recovers to the baseline. (3) Play out the point. Rotate each point; games to 7; switch roles; switch the feed side every other game.
drills.cues: "Move opponent with combinations of shots (angle/down-the-line)" (goal)
drills.progression: the angler plays the first ball down the line and can come in; angler's choice; the angle must bounce inside the service box and the line ball past the SL
drills.regression: cooperative feed-angle-recover with no point [A]
drills.video: none verified

drills.name: Slice Backhand Progression Ladder
drills.ages: yellow 11-14; teens; adult intermediate-advanced; senior [A]. The source says "all levels". USTA green plans already have 9-11s play slice points with a continental grip and one-handed backhands.
drills.works: floating slice; no backspin; wrist flick
drills.players: coach/partner; basket; target zones
drills.setup: Stage 1 is on your own at the SL. Stage 2: the coach or partner feeds from across the net into zones (deep corners, mid-court, service boxes). Stage 3 is a baseline rally.
drills.steps:
1. Shadow swings and self-feed, focusing on grip, takeback and follow-through; self-bounce into the opposite service box.
2. Coach or partner feeds at moderate pace, targeting depth and then width. Reach about 70% success before progressing.
3. Rally, mixing topspin and slice, with a slice every 2nd or 3rd ball.
4. Points in which a slice must be used at least once before winners are attempted.
- **Diagnostic:** put a ball on the strings and tilt the racquet until it rolls off. That angle approximates the correct face.
drills.cues: continental grip; a high-to-low path of about 45 degrees with the face open 10-15 degrees; "carving a thin layer off its bottom surface"; contact in front of the lead hip; non-hitting arm extends back; firm wrist.
drills.progression: "4 Zones" depth targets; slice approach and close in (source drill list)
drills.regression: USTA green "Mini-Tennis Points — play all slices" from the SL
drills.source: [Sportplan – The Slice Backhand: A Tactical Weapon for Every Level (Apr 2026)](https://www.sportplan.net/drills/Tennis/trends/slice-backhand-tactical-weapon-2025-04.jsp); [USTA Green Ball plans, Green 2 ch. 3](https://www.usta.com/content/dam/usta/content-fragments/tennis-service-center/assets/pdfs/Net-Generation-Practice-Plan-Green.pdf)
drills.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zw-1nzGwhrA — "The Backhand Slice Explained: Stop Floating the Ball (Fix This Mistake!)" — Coachlife - Tennis; https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bL1Q79X8csA — "One Handed Backhand SLICE - Tennis Lesson" — OneHowto

drills.name: Three Slices, then Drive (tactical slice rally)
drills.works: using slice to neutralise, then changing direction with a drive
drills.players: 2 players
drills.setup: [A] The backhand-to-backhand (ad) diagonal, from the baselines.
drills.steps: Three crosscourt slices, then an attempted down-the-line drive. Rotate roles every 3 minutes.
drills.cues: "Firm wrist = penetration" (source)
drills.progression: play out the point after the drive [A]
drills.regression: 2 slices, then a feed for the drive [A]
drills.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kWhzqMc_5R4 — "One Handed Backhand Lesson: Topspin vs Slice" — Performance-Plus Tennis

drills.name: Two-Hander "Driver" Drill (non-dominant-hand forehands)
drills.ages: all stages that use a two-handed backhand: green through adult advanced [A]
drills.works: dominant-arm takeover; pulling across the ball
drills.players: 1 player + feeder (or a ball machine)
drills.setup: [A] The player is at the centre of the baseline or SL and the feeder feeds to the backhand side.
drills.steps: (1) Hit "forehands" using only the non-dominant hand, placed on top of the grip as in the two-hander. (2) Alternate those one-hand shots with full two-handed backhands to feel the top hand driving the stroke.
drills.cues: "Top hand is the driver, bottom hand the passenger"; finish with the non-dominant elbow pointing across the net; "air the armpits" at the finish ([USTA](https://www.usta.com/en/home/improve/tips-and-instruction/national/improve-your-tennis-game--improve-your-backahnd.html), from search summary)
drills.progression: live crosscourt backhand rally (D25 backhand diagonal)
drills.regression: drop-feed from the side at the SL [A]
drills.source: [USTA – Improve Your Game: Driving the Two-Handed Backhand (Karl Davies, 2018)](https://www.usta.com/en/home/improve/tips-and-instruction/national/improve-your-tennis-game--the-driving-force-in-your-two-handed-b.html)
drills.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xn-Bdd74F5c — "Top 3 Drills For Two Handed Backhand In Tennis - Transform Your Tennis Backhand" — Top Tennis Training - Pro Tennis Lessons; https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=M0aIRntFvcE — "How to immediately improve your two handed tennis backhand | + Drills!" — Meike Babel Tennis

drills.name: OK-Sign Two-Hander
drills.works: dominant-arm takeover ("pulling the racquet instead of driving it")
drills.players: player + feeder
drills.setup: [A] Feeds to the backhand from across the net; the player is at the baseline.
drills.steps: Hold the bottom (dominant) hand with only the thumb and index finger, as an "OK" sign. Hit several backhands this way to force the non-dominant arm to take control, then return to the normal grip.
drills.cues: "A left-handed forehand with the right hand along for the ride" (for right-handers)
drills.progression: rally with a normal grip while keeping the feel [A]
drills.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4ELRnF5o7BA — "Tennis Backhand Lesson: The Ultimate Two Handed Backhand drill" — Total Tennis Domination

drills.name: Unit-Turn Catch, then Hit
drills.works: arming the ball; no unit turn; opening up early; rushed takeback
drills.players: player + feeder
drills.setup: [A] Feeder across the net at the SL; player at the centre of the SL or baseline.
drills.steps: (1) Turn the hips and upper body as one unit and catch the fed ball with the non-dominant hand. (2) Progress to finishing the stroke with a forehand.
drills.cues: "Unit turn" (USTA). Pivot the outside foot on the split step and point the non-dominant hand at the ball (PlayYourCourt 2026). Complete the turn and racquet preparation before the ball bounces, with a "slight pause" at the top (PlayYourCourt, Scott Baxter 2019).
drills.progression: D2, then D3 with a pause-and-drop rhythm [A]
drills.regression: shadow swings, 10-15 at the baseline, focusing on early coil/uncoil (PlayYourCourt)
drills.source: [USTA – Get your forehand flowing (Rita Gladstone, 2018)](https://www.usta.com/en/home/improve/tips-and-instruction/national/improve-your-tennis-game--get-your-forehand-flowing.html); [PlayYourCourt – Why your forehand has no power (2026)](https://www.playyourcourt.com/news/why-your-forehand-has-no-power-and-how-to-fix-it-for-good/); [PlayYourCourt – Forehand killer part 2 (2019)](https://www.playyourcourt.com/news/forehand-killer-part-2/)
drills.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=du5uOZfKArw — "Why The Split Step & Unit Turn Are CRUCIAL For Your Tennis Game" — Gaby Paz - Vantage Tennis

drills.name: Drop-Hit Freeze-Finish (spacing & weight transfer)
drills.works: crowding the ball; late contact; hitting off the back foot; abbreviated finish
drills.players: player alone or with a partner; basket
drills.setup: [A] The player stands at the baseline or SL and drops the ball to the side, slightly in front of the front hip.
drills.steps: (1) Drop-hit progression focused on using body weight. (2) Freeze after contact to check the arm extension. (3) Freeze at the finish (over the non-dominant shoulder).
drills.cues: "contact slightly in front of the front hip at waist-to-chest height"; "12-18 inches of space"; "push the ground away with your back foot" (PlayYourCourt)
drills.progression: a partner tosses, then D2/D3
drills.regression: shadow swing to the freeze position
drills.source: [PlayYourCourt – Why your forehand has no power (2026)](https://www.playyourcourt.com/news/why-your-forehand-has-no-power-and-how-to-fix-it-for-good/)
drills.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8kDLHFtVT5c — "5 Drills To Improve Your Forehand FAST I TENNIS LESSON" — Tennis Evolution. Its search description cites "proper spacing, extension, and wrist control".

drills.name: One-Hander Straight-Arm Feed
drills.ages: teens; adult intermediate-advanced (players committed to a one-hander) [A]
drills.works: elbow leading; late contact; poor shoulder turn
drills.players: player + feeder
drills.setup: [A] Feeder across the net feeds medium-paced balls to the backhand; player at the baseline.
drills.steps: [A] (1) Turn the shoulders to 90 degrees to the net before the arm moves. (2) Have the arm straight at the bottom of the backswing before the ball bounces. (3) Swing with the upper arm close to the chest at the start of the forward swing. (4) Freeze contact: straight arm, locked wrist, ball out in front.
drills.cues: "Arm straight before the bounce"; "shoulders turned 90 degrees first"; "straight arm, locked wrist at contact" (TennisOne / Tennisplayer principles)
drills.progression: crosscourt backhand rally (D25)
drills.regression: shadow swings to a freeze; drop-feed from the side
drills.source: [TennisOne (Yandell) – theories](https://tennisone.tennisplayer.net/content/Theories/theories.Yandell.p.5.php); [TennisOne (Murphy) – backhand preparation](https://tennisone.tennisplayer.net/content/Lessons/murphy/back/prepback2.php); [Tennisplayer forum – Elbow lead on 1HB](https://forum.tennisplayer.net/forum/tennisplayer/1046-elbow-lead-on-1hb). The principles come from search summaries and were not fetched in full.
drills.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nuRh27czEy8 — "3 DEADLIEST ONE-HANDED Backhand Mistakes (And How to Fix Them!)" — VS Tennis; https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zniT2qyiN4Q — "Do this One Handed Backhand drill to Fix your Rotation." — Total Tennis Domination; https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=luJXnKy_5bs — "One-Handed Backhand - Drill #7: One And Two" — Feel Tennis Instruction; https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rX0U1gnySRI — "3 Drills For Modern One Handed Backhand in Tennis - Thiem Wawrinka Federer Backhand Technique" — Top Tennis Training - Pro Tennis Lessons; https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bdU0SFj7ToE — "You NEED to FIX Your One-Handed Backhand! Drills for Power and Control + PRO Tips and Technique!" — Chris Lewit

drills.name: Racket and Ball (rally-length scoring game)
drills.ages: all levels (source); good for adult social groups and seniors [A]
drills.works: rewarding long rallies over winners
drills.players: 2 or 4 players
drills.setup: Full court; agree a target score of at least 20.
drills.steps: (1) Every ball hit into play counts as one hit. (2) Play out the rally. (3) The winner of the rally scores points equal to the number of shots in it, and the loser scores zero. First to the target wins.
drills.cues: "Make one more ball" [A]
drills.progression: crosscourt-only boundaries [A]
drills.regression: service-box court [A]
drills.video: none verified

drills.name: Doubles with a Twist (4-shot minimum rally)
drills.ages: adult beginner-intermediate; senior; yellow juniors [A]. The source says beginner to intermediate.
drills.works: consistency in a match context
drills.players: 4 players
drills.setup: Doubles court. For beginners, use the service box or half-court.
drills.steps: (1) Serve and return. (2) The rally must reach 4 shots before the point is "live". (3) The winner of the final shot earns the point, with standard scoring.
drills.cues: "Build the point" [A]
drills.progression: start on a smaller court and move to baseline play as confidence builds (source)
drills.regression: cooperative 4-ball count, no scoring [A]
drills.video: none verified

drills.name: Cone Flip Throw to Hand-to-Racket Push-Down
drills.ages: Red 5-8, Orange 8-10 (the source is a red-ball school lesson for "Over 8s")
drills.skill: Serve (overarm foundation; also an overhead foundation)
drills.works: Overarm throwing pattern, sideways start, hitting down from above the head. Also helps kids who push the ball or serve underarm (F5, F8).
drills.players: Pairs; red balls; 21-inch rackets; 3 markers per pair; several saucer cones per player.
drills.setup: Partners face each other behind markers 2 m apart, with a third marker halfway between to make a "micro court". Saucer cones are placed upside down in front of each player. *(added: run on the red-court service area, several pairs side by side along the net.)*
drills.steps: 1) Throw overarm and try to hit the partner's cones: 1 point for a hit, 10 points if the cone flips. 2) Hand to racket: stand sideways with the racket hand at the back, racket above the head in front of the body, ball resting on the strings; push the ball downward toward the partner's cones. The partner catches and repeats. 3) Racket to racket: one player serves into the target area, the other returns; the pair scores a team point for each serve-return-catch set.
drills.cues: "Side-on", "Racket above head", "Push down from up high", *(added)* "Elbow up, throw at the cone".
drills.progression: Throw the ball from shoulder height up to the racket and strike down from above the head, then from waist height. Then make the target area smaller.
drills.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hXLeq30tGAc — "How To Teach Kids Tennis (Ep 1) - The Serve" — The Tennis Mentor
drills.regression: Non-dominant-hand throws are listed as a *variation*. *(added: easier version is a bigger target, shorter distance, or a foam ball.)*

drills.name: Three-Level Throw
drills.works: A full throwing action with leg drive and a high release. Fixes "arm-only" serving and missing short into the net (F6, F8).
drills.players: 3-6 players per court; balls. Green balls are fine; *(added: tennis balls or bean-bag balls for throwing)*.
drills.setup: All players on one side of the net in two lines behind the baseline. One line throws from the deuce side and one from the ad side, so two players throw at a time.
drills.steps: 1) Throw into the diagonal service box twice, then rotate. 2) Throw so the ball lands between the opposite service line and baseline, twice, then rotate. 3) Throw so it lands between the opposite baseline and the fence.
drills.cues: *(added)* "Side-on, throw up and out", "Front arm points up", "Push off the back foot".
drills.progression: (1) Three in a row: box, past service line, past baseline. (2) Split the box and court into two halves and throw to a named half. (3) "See who can hit opposite fence."
drills.source: [USTA Net Generation Practice Plan Green, Ch.05 "Serve to Spots" (PDF)](https://preview.usta.com/content/dam/usta/content-fragments/tennis-service-center/assets/pdfs/Net-Generation-Practice-Plan-Green.pdf)
drills.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NON_ZSYEhew — "How To Teach Kids The Tennis Serve" — My Tennis Coaching
drills.regression: *(added)* Move up to the service line, or use only the first level.

drills.name: Quarterback Throw Progression (football or tennis ball)
drills.ages: Yellow juniors 11-14, Teens; also suitable for Adult beginners *(added)*
drills.works: Sideways turn, arm positions in the trophy, and the ball "tip" pointing back behind the head. This becomes the racquet-drop and pronation pattern. Fixes no turn and a pushing arm (F5, F7, F8).
drills.players: Pairs, up to 3 pairs per side; one football per pair (a tennis ball if there are not enough).
drills.setup: Partners stand on opposite sidelines of the court.
drills.steps: 1) Play catch, throwing a spiral. 2) Add distance. 3) Add quarterback movement: face forward, turn and run back, set, throw. 4) Start facing forward with both hands on the ball, then turn sideways with the throwing arm up and to the side, bent at 90°. 5) Turn sideways with both hands on the ball and separate: front arm bent and parallel to the ground; back arm at 90° with the ball behind the head. 6) Same preparation, but point the tip of the ball backward behind the head.
drills.cues: "Turn sideways", "Front arm parallel", "Ball behind head", "Tip points back".
drills.progression: The source lists stages 1-5 as progressions.
drills.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-9cIObcQyME — "7 Serve Pronation Drills For A Better Tennis Serve" — Feel Tennis Instruction
drills.regression: Use a tennis ball. *(added: shorter distance.)*

drills.name: Fence Throws
drills.ages: Green 9-11, Yellow juniors 11-14 *(added: works for adult beginners too)*
drills.works: Throwing up rather than forward, which fixes low or flat contact and serves into the net (F6, F8).
drills.players: Pairs, 2 balls per pair, a court fence.
drills.setup: One partner outside the fence and one inside, each about 10 ft from the fence.
drills.steps: Throw the ball over the fence so the partner can catch it without moving far. Throw two balls; the partner catches and throws them back.
drills.cues: *(added)* "Up and over", "Long arm at release".
drills.progression: Start with the ball on the ground behind the back foot (pick up, load, throw). *(added: step farther from the fence.)*
drills.source: [USTA Net Generation Practice Plan Yellow, "Fence Throws" (PDF)](https://preview.usta.com/content/dam/usta/content-fragments/tennis-service-center/assets/pdfs/Net-Generation-Practice-Plan-Yellow.pdf)
drills.video: No verified drill-specific video found.
drills.regression: *(added)* Move closer to the fence.

drills.name: Two-Ball Toss-and-Throw
drills.ages: Adult beginner, Senior, Teens *(source is aimed at beginners in general)*; Orange and Green as well *(added)*
drills.skill: Serve (coordinating the toss arm and hitting arm, rhythm)
drills.works: Each arm's role, toss accuracy, balance. Fixes an inconsistent toss and arms working out of sync (F3, F4).
drills.players: Individual; 2 balls; *(added: a chalk or throw-down square on the court for toss accuracy)*.
drills.setup: Stand at the baseline in serving stance with a ball in each hand, arms in front and balls touching. *(added: mark a small square in front of the lead foot and inside the baseline.)*
drills.steps: Toss one ball straight up with the non-dominant arm while swinging the dominant arm back. Throw the second ball forward as far as possible. Do 20-30 reps.
drills.cues: "Toss with the non-dominant arm, throw with the dominant arm". Toss accuracy "within a marked square"; keep balance.
drills.progression: *(added)* Throw over the net to land in the diagonal box, then go to S7 (serve in two parts).
drills.source: [Feel Tennis, Serve Lesson for Beginners, Step 1](https://www.feeltennis.net/serve-lesson-for-beginners/)
drills.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=m4UQBa1HtiQ — "Serve Lesson for Beginners: How to Hit a Tennis Serve" — Essential Tennis - Lessons and Instruction for Passionate Players
drills.regression: *(added)* Toss only and let the ball land in the square.

drills.name: Kneeling or Sitting Serve at the T
drills.ages: Green 9-11 to Adult advanced. *(added: kneeling is a common bridge for kids, but no kid-specific source was found.)*
drills.level: Beginner to Intermediate (flat or slice); Advanced for the kick version (see S16)
drills.works: Hitting up and extending into the ball; isolates the upper body. Fixes letting the toss drop, pushing the ball, and serving into the net (F5, F8).
drills.players: Individual or a coach; a basket of balls; *(added: a knee pad, mat or racket cover under the knee)*.
drills.setup: Kneel or sit on the baseline or the service line next to the center mark (T), aiming into the diagonal service box.
drills.steps: Toss and serve from the knees or seated, swinging "up and into the ball before swinging out" to the service box. *(added: 10-15 balls per set, then 5 standing serves to transfer the feel.)*
drills.cues: "Extend up into the ball", "Same toss spot every time", "Exhale through the stroke".
drills.progression: *(added)* Kneel at the baseline instead of the service line; aim at a target cone; go to S16 (kneeling kick).
drills.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SexL4O0LaZw — "Tennis Kick Serve Drill - Serve From Your Knee For A Better Kick Serve" — Total Tennis Domination
drills.regression: Kneel at the service line *(source gives both positions)*.

drills.name: Serve in Two Parts (toss, catch, trophy check)
drills.works: A consistent toss, getting into the trophy position, and timing the swing to the toss (F3, F4, F7).
drills.players: Individual; balls; racquet in continental grip.
drills.setup: Behind the baseline in serving stance *(added: or at the service line for kids)*.
drills.steps: 1) Toss and catch the ball in the tossing hand, checking the trophy position. 2) Repeat the toss and serve. Alternate catch and serve.
drills.cues: "Toss, freeze in trophy, catch", "Guide the body toward a complete serve; it won't be smooth yet".
drills.progression: Gradually blend into a full serve motion.
drills.source: [Feel Tennis, Serve Lesson for Beginners, Step 5](https://www.feeltennis.net/serve-lesson-for-beginners/)
drills.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZFy99x_fMXc — "Tennis Serve - Serve Step 2 - Toss and Backswing" — Fuzzy Yellow Balls
drills.regression: *(added)* Do toss-and-catch with no racquet.

drills.name: Three-Level Serve (service line to baseline to fence)
drills.ages: Green 9-11, Yellow juniors 11-14 (source: Yellow Ball 2), Teens, Adult beginner/intermediate *(added)*
drills.works: Racquet-head speed and an upward swing path. Fixes decelerating or "guiding" serves (F5, F8, F11).
drills.players: 3-6 players per court; basket of balls.
drills.setup: All players on the baseline on one side of the net, half on the deuce side and half on the ad side. Two serve at a time, one from each side.
drills.steps: 1) Warm-up serves into the service box, two each, then rotate. 2) Serve so the ball lands between the opposite service line and baseline, twice, then rotate. 3) Serve so it lands between the opposite baseline and the fence.
drills.cues: "Racquet-head speed", "Hit up and out on the ball".
drills.progression: (1) Serve three in a row: box, past service line, past baseline. (2) Split the box and court into two sides and serve to a named area.
drills.source: [USTA Net Generation Practice Plan Yellow, "Three-Level Serve" (PDF)](https://preview.usta.com/content/dam/usta/content-fragments/tennis-service-center/assets/pdfs/Net-Generation-Practice-Plan-Yellow.pdf)
drills.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5a-ryZnrmh8 — "Tennis Serve - 3 Drills To Improve Power and Consistency" — Top Tennis Training - Pro Tennis Lessons
drills.regression: *(added)* Start from the service line (the USTA orange "Serve Plus One" starts at the service line).

drills.name: Toss Target ("Same Spot" Toss)
drills.works: Toss consistency and toss too far behind, in front or to the side (F3, F4). Also helps keep the tossing arm up.
drills.players: Individual; balls; *(added: a target such as a hoop, racquet face, towel or throw-down square)*.
drills.setup: Serving stance at the baseline. *(added: the target sits just inside the baseline, in front of and slightly to the hitting side of the lead foot, for flat or slice; for kick see S16.)*
drills.steps: Toss to full height with no swing and let the ball fall; it should land on or in the target. Then add the trophy position, then the swing *(added: 10 tosses per set; score the hits out of 10)*.
drills.cues: "Place the toss in the same location every time" (Human Kinetics); toss accuracy "within a marked square" (Feel Tennis); *(added)* "Lift, don't flick", "Release at eye level or above".
drills.progression: *(added)* Smaller target; toss with eyes on the contact point; add the full serve and catch any bad toss.
drills.source: [Feel Tennis, Serve Lesson for Beginners (toss into marked square)](https://www.feeltennis.net/serve-lesson-for-beginners/); [Human Kinetics excerpt (same location every time)](https://us.humankinetics.com/blogs/excerpt/thrust-launch-serve-technique)
drills.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UJ3xNfw7G3Y — "Tame Your Serve Toss With The "Keep Lifting" Drill" — Feel Tennis Instruction. Also https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9YxgjV1Dtls — "Tennis Serve Progressions Step 3: Toss" — Fuzzy Yellow Balls; https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jmYsWY36XHU — "3 Tennis Drills for Perfect Serve Toss" — Cosmin | WebTennis24
drills.regression: *(added)* Lower toss, bigger target.

drills.name: Continental Edge Tap (tapping the ball down)
drills.ages: Orange 8-10 to Senior (good for adult beginners moving from a forehand grip)
drills.works: Comfort with the continental grip; the face sits parallel to the body. Fixes the frying-pan grip (F1).
drills.players: Individual; 1 ball; racquet.
drills.setup: Anywhere on court. Hold the racquet in continental grip, choked up toward the throat.
drills.steps: Gently tap the ball downward (bounce dribble) for 2-3 minutes, keeping the face parallel to the body.
drills.cues: "Racket angled parallel to your body, not away from you".
drills.progression: *(added)* Move the hand to the end of the grip; alternate up and down taps on the same edge; walk while tapping.
drills.source: [Feel Tennis, Serve Lesson for Beginners, Step 2](https://www.feeltennis.net/serve-lesson-for-beginners/)
drills.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=quUydRpf96Q — "Fix The Most Common Error On The Serve - Continental Grip Drills That Work!!" — Patrick Smith Tennis Coaching. Also https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=85TTLdfvzPk — "How To Serve With A Continental Grip" — 2MinuteTennis
drills.regression: *(added)* Choke up more; use a red or orange ball.

drills.name: Swing on Edge / Lead With the Edge (shadow, no ball)
drills.skill: Serve (grip, swing path, set-up for pronation)
drills.works: Waiter's tray and an open face in the backswing (F2); forehand grip (F1).
drills.players: Individual; racquet; no ball.
drills.setup: Serving stance at the baseline *(added: side-on to the net, facing the side fence)*.
drills.steps: Lead with the bottom edge into the backswing, the top edge into the loop behind the back, then the bottom edge out toward an imaginary ball, finishing on the right side (right-hander). Then hold the racquet with only thumb and index finger for more freedom. A related drill: three-finger figure-8 loops while rotating the body and lifting the heel (Feel Tennis beginner Step 4).
drills.cues: "Edge leads", "Stay sideways longer", "Smooth loops".
drills.progression: Thumb-and-index-finger hold. Then add the ball and serve "with the edge" (S13).
drills.source: [Feel Tennis, Correcting the Waiter's Serve, Drill 1](https://www.feeltennis.net/correcting-the-waiters-serve/); [Feel Tennis beginner lesson, Step 4](https://www.feeltennis.net/serve-lesson-for-beginners/)
drills.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9QLLwCrQKLI — "Tennis Serve Progressions Step 1: Swing on Edge" — Fuzzy Yellow Balls
drills.regression: *(added)* Do it in slow motion in front of a mirror or the fence.

drills.name: Ground-Smack Pronation
drills.ages: Yellow juniors 11-14 to Senior *(added: gentle reps only for seniors with shoulder history)*
drills.works: Pronation with internal shoulder rotation. Fixes pushing the ball or no pronation (F8).
drills.players: Individual; balls; racquet in continental grip.
drills.setup: *(added: stand near the fence or the back of the court)*. Racquet above the shoulder in a "hammer" position, edge facing the ball.
drills.steps: Toss or drop the ball and let it bounce. Gently hit it into the ground while pronating, keeping the racquet on the dominant side at the finish. Do 30-50 controlled reps. Variation: hit the ball "backwards" after the bounce with a same-side follow-through.
drills.cues: "Start smooth; add power just before contact"; don't force the movement ("avoid forcing movements to prevent injury").
drills.progression: Pronation drills 4-5: slice to the ad court with late pronation (S14); flat serve facing the net post with forearm only.
drills.source: [Feel Tennis, Serve Lesson for Beginners, Step 3](https://www.feeltennis.net/serve-lesson-for-beginners/); [Feel Tennis, Serve Pronation, drills 6-7](https://www.feeltennis.net/serve-pronation/)
drills.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-9cIObcQyME — "7 Serve Pronation Drills For A Better Tennis Serve" — Feel Tennis Instruction. Also https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ahAGvTuiVHo — "Serve Pronation: Beginner Tennis Lesson (How-To Tips & Drills)" — Cosmin | WebTennis24
drills.regression: *(added)* Shadow swings with no ball.

drills.name: Serve With the Edge, then Fence Serve
drills.ages: Teens, Adult beginner to advanced, Senior
drills.works: Waiter's tray and early opening (F2); turning to face the court too early.
drills.players: Individual; basket of balls; a court fence.
drills.setup: Part A: baseline, normal serving position. Part B: stand about 2 ft from the fence, side-on as in serving stance, so the swing path runs along the fence.
drills.steps: A) Hit 20-30 balls keeping the racquet edge-aligned the whole way through ("technique over placement"). Then "change your mind late": pronate at the last moment so the strings meet the ball. B) Serve near the fence. If the racquet hits the fence, the face opened too early or you rotated forward too soon.
drills.cues: "Edge to the ball, strings at the last moment", "Stay sideways", "Expect resistance from the old pattern".
drills.progression: Slice to the ad court (S14), then full serves to targets (S15).
drills.source: [Feel Tennis, Correcting the Waiter's Serve, Drills 4-6](https://www.feeltennis.net/correcting-the-waiters-serve/)
drills.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=evv2WkBOAvE — "Tennis SERVE -  Correcting The Waiter's Tray" — Feel Tennis Instruction. Also https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wEygQcPoq0U — "STOP Your Waiter’s Tray Serve (5 Drills) | Fix Your Serve At Home" — 2MinuteTennis
drills.regression: *(added)* Shadow at the fence with no ball.

drills.name: Slice to the Ad Court ("pronate late")
drills.ages: Yellow juniors 11-14, Teens, Adult intermediate/advanced, Senior
drills.works: Slice spin, staying sideways, pronation timing. Fixes waiter's tray (F2) and opening up early. It is a safer second serve for seniors *(added)*.
drills.players: Individual; basket of balls.
drills.setup: Serve from the deuce side *(added: the source's "toward ad court" means sending the ball left of the body line, which keeps you sideways; a right-hander can also serve from the ad side to the wide target)*.
drills.steps: Serve slowly with the slice grip. Lead with the edge, brush the slice, and pronate after contact. At first "pronate too late", then gradually shorten the delay.
drills.cues: "Lead with edge", "Pronate too late at first", "Stay sideways".
drills.progression: Feel Tennis pronation drill 5: serve facing the net post with no body rotation. *(added: aim at the S15 wide zone.)*
drills.source: [Feel Tennis, Serve Pronation, drill 4](https://www.feeltennis.net/serve-pronation/); [Feel Tennis, Correcting the Waiter's Serve, drill 3](https://www.feeltennis.net/correcting-the-waiters-serve/)
drills.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RReBwUHe1ug — "Flat, Kick & Slice Serve Lesson with 4.5 NTRP Player" — Intuitive Tennis
drills.regression: *(added)* Do it from the service line.

drills.name: Serve Index (zone targets: T, body, wide)
drills.ages: Green 9-11 (Green 2), Yellow juniors 11-14 (Yellow 2), Teens, all Adults, Senior *(added)*
drills.skill: Serve targets; second serve and routine
drills.works: Direction, a repeatable pre-serve ritual, using spin for control. Fixes double faults under pressure (F11) and having no placement plan.
drills.players: Up to 4 per court; throw-down lines (TDLs), cones or poly-spots; extra players act as returners.
drills.setup: All players on one side; two serve at once, one from deuce and one from ad. TDLs split each service box vertically into 2 zones (a "T half" and a "wide half"), making 4 zones across both boxes. *(added: for adults, use 3 zones per box — wide, body, T — about 1 m wide each, with cones at the back of each zone.)*
drills.steps: Count how many balls it takes to serve successfully into all 4 zones; that number is your "serve index". Serves count only if the same ritual is used before each one. After everyone finishes, start again and chase a personal best. Yellow team version: add players' indexes together for a team serve index and aim for the lowest.
drills.cues: "Same ritual every serve", "Use spin to add control".
drills.progression: All serves must have spin. Yellow: right-handers must slice wide on the deuce side and down the T on the ad side (the reverse for lefties). *(added: second serves only; returner calls in/out.)*
drills.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ibD_gli8XP0 — "Tennis Serve Practice / Position of Targets Inside the Service Box #tennisservepractice" — Cosmin | WebTennis24. Also https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ygCu7BH8vlQ — "Tennis Serve Lesson: Target Practice" — Online Tennis Instruction; https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=x8id69sN1d8 — "Achieve Laser Accuracy On Your Serve Like The PROS #tennis" — Patrick Smith Tennis Coaching
drills.regression: *(added)* Bigger zones (whole half-box); serve from the service line.

drills.name: Kneeling Kick Serve Over a Raised Net
drills.ages: Teens 14-18, Adult intermediate/advanced. Not before age 13 (Emory guidance on the kick serve).
drills.works: Brushing low to high, net clearance, pronation finishing behind the back. Fixes a flat, low second serve and double faults (F11).
drills.players: Individual; basket; mat or racquet cover for the knee; a cone target; a way to raise the net *(added: a rope or string tied about 1-1.5 m above the net tape between poles, or two tall cones with a string)*.
drills.setup: Kneel on one knee at the baseline next to the center mark. *(added: put the cone deep in the diagonal box near the service line, middle or wide.)*
drills.steps: Serve kick over the higher "net" toward the cone, finishing with the arm behind the back.
drills.cues: "Brush up", "Finish arm behind back", *(added)* "Hit up to the sky; spin brings it down".
drills.progression: *(added)* Stand up and serve over the raised net; add a kick-specific toss (commonly taught as more over the head than the flat toss; see the FYB kick-toss video); Chris Lewit cone drill.
drills.source: [YouTube description: "Tennis Technique - Kneeling Kick Serve Over Higher Net Finishing with Arm Behind Back"](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QyMIKPF1FH0); age guidance from [Emory Tennis Medicine](https://www.emoryhealthcare.org/centers-programs/sports-medicine-center/tennis-medicine-program/wellness)
drills.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QyMIKPF1FH0 — "Tennis Technique - Kneeling Kick Serve Over Higher Net Finishing with Arm Behind Back" — Be Gr8 at Tennis - Rob Cherry. Also https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TkAj6MmwxHw — "Tennis Kick Serve - Kick Serve Step 1 - Toss" — Fuzzy Yellow Balls; https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=F7z7vEVqz1A — "Tennis Kick Serve Progressions: Step 1: Swing and Pronate" — Fuzzy Yellow Balls; https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HR11rSp3QnE — "Why This Simple Cone Drill Makes Your Kick Serve Explode Off the Court!" — Chris Lewit; https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QcSUVrhLTKY — "Simple Kick Serve Drill  | TENNIS SERVE" — Tennis Evolution
drills.regression: *(added)* Do it from the service line.

drills.name: Drag Serve (rhythm and relaxed arm)
drills.works: Toss before arm; relaxed hitting arm; palm down in the backswing. Fixes a rushed swing, an early or missing racquet drop, arm tension, and swinging before the toss peaks (F7).
drills.players: Pairs, 2 pairs per court.
drills.setup: Partners on the baselines, diagonally across the net from each other.
drills.steps: Start with the racquet pointing straight down, slightly behind the back leg. Toss first, and move the hitting arm only when the ball reaches its peak. Serve twice; the partner catches and serves back.
drills.cues: "Toss first", "Arm goes at the peak", "Relaxed arm", "Palm down like a throw".
drills.progression: Drag serve on one, full motion on the next.
drills.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uYguiaDTgH8 — "Tennis Serve: Racquet Drop (HUGE Mistake to Avoid & Drills To-Do)" — Tennis Evolution
drills.regression: *(added)* From the service line; toss-and-catch only.

drills.name: Thrust Launch (leg drive)
drills.ages: Teens 14-18, Adult intermediate/advanced *(added: not recommended for seniors with knee or back issues)*
drills.works: Knee bend and leg drive; landing on the lead foot. Fixes no knee bend (F6) and falling sideways (F9).
drills.players: Individual; basket.
drills.setup: Baseline or service-line center (T), in the normal service ready position.
drills.steps: Shift weight forward as in flat-serve footwork. Step up with the back foot as you toss and place it next to the lead foot. Bend both knees together, "launch up and out with the legs together", strike at the peak of the toss, then land on the lead foot and follow through.
drills.cues: "Load both knees", "Launch up and out", "Land on the front foot", "Exhale".
drills.progression: *(added)* Move to the baseline and serve to S15 zones.
drills.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6aPfX-hIOqc — "How To Tennis Serve Step By Step" — Tennis Evolution; https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_XO7IEHDkl0 — "Serve- Hip Flexor Snap Towel Drill" — Patrick Dougherty
drills.regression: Kneeling serve (S6) to teach "up", then the service line.

drills.name: Team Defender (one-serve pressure game)
drills.ages: Green 9-11 (Green 2 version), Yellow juniors 11-14 (Yellow 2 version), Teens, Adults *(added)*
drills.skill: Serve (holding serve, second serve under pressure) and return
drills.works: Using the serve and first ball offensively under scoring pressure. Fixes double faults under pressure (F11).
drills.players: At least 6 players and 2 courts; teams of 3-4.
drills.setup: Each team is assigned a court to "defend". Each team sends one player to challenge another team's court; the rest stay to defend.
drills.steps: Defenders serve to the challenger and play one point, then rotate out. Only the serving side can score; the defender can only stop the serving team scoring. The first team to a set number wins the round. Green 2 variant ("Attack second serve"): the challenger gets one serve; the defender must return and come in.
drills.cues: "Serve plus first ball", *(added)* "Same ritual", "Commit to the spin".
drills.progression: The server must hit a forehand on the first ball after the serve; 2 points for a volley or overhead winner. Green: return to the open court; serve to a set spot.
drills.video: No verified drill-specific video found.
drills.regression: *(added)* Two serves allowed; serve from the service line.

drills.name: Serve Plus One
drills.ages: Orange 8-10 (Orange 3), Yellow juniors 11-14 (Yellow 2 version from the baseline)
drills.works: Serve and return direction and consistency; continental grip and correct foot position on the serve.
drills.players: Two pairs per court; orange balls (orange) or yellow balls.
drills.setup: Each pair hits diagonally across the net (crosscourt boxes). Orange: players start on the service line. Yellow: full court, start on the baseline.
drills.steps: Serve, return, server hits one groundstroke (yellow: to the open court), and the returner traps the ball. The returner then serves and repeats. Each player does 4 sequences, then switch sides (deuce to ad). After a full rotation, play it as a game: the pair scores 1 point per three-ball sequence, plus a bonus point if the server's groundstroke lands past the service line.
drills.cues: "Continental on the serve", "Feet in position", *(added)* "Split as the server tosses".
drills.progression: Start on the baseline; serve to a set half of the box.
drills.video: No verified drill-specific video found.
drills.regression: *(added)* Drop-hit serve; returner catches and throws.

drills.name: First Four Team (serve, return, 3rd and 4th balls)
drills.works: Split-step timing for both server and returner, and recovery. Fixes a returner who stands still (F12).
drills.players: Two pairs per court.
drills.setup: Pairs diagonally across the net from each other; players start on the baseline.
drills.steps: Serve, return, then one groundstroke each; the server catches the 4th ball and starts again. 1 point per successful four-ball sequence. Play court vs court. After 4 attempts switch servers; switch sides after a full rotation.
drills.cues: "Serve and split-step", "Return and split-step, then recover".
drills.progression: Serve to a set half of the box; all four balls to set sides.
drills.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XR83yXLla8w — "Tennis Split Step Timing, Execution And Drills" — Feel Tennis Instruction. Also https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hcwNlrTKB5c — "Split-Step and Return of Serve Footwork" — TPA tennis
drills.regression: *(added)* Second-serve pace only; returner may catch the serve on the first rep.

drills.name: Serve Pyramids (aggressive return)
drills.skill: Return (aggressive / on the rise, return to target)
drills.works: Moving in and loading from the legs. Fixes a passive returner (F12).
drills.players: Two teams of 2-3, half-court; 4 balls per team for the pyramid.
drills.setup: Half-court singles. One player serves, the other returns. Each team has a set area behind the baseline where it builds a four-ball pyramid.
drills.steps: The server gets one serve; the returner gets two chances. The returner moves in, drives the ball to the open court, and plays out the point. The team adds a ball to its pyramid for each point won. First complete pyramid wins; start a new game and switch the serving team.
drills.cues: "Take it on the rise", "Load from the legs", "Drive to the open court".
drills.progression: Returner may hit to either side; must hit a forehand return; must come in.
drills.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_pS0otk2560 — "Top 3 Drills For Perfect Return of Serve in Tennis" — Top Tennis Training - Pro Tennis Lessons
drills.regression: *(added)* Returner starts at the baseline and any return in counts.

drills.name: Return the Cannon (block return vs. big serve)
drills.skill: Return (block or short-backswing return), plus serve speed
drills.works: Returning pace with a compact swing. Fixes a big backswing on the return (F13). The server gets racquet-head speed.
drills.players: Two pairs per court, half-court; TDLs.
drills.setup: TDLs split the court in half; all points crosscourt. The server stands on the service line; the returner is in the normal return position *(added: about on the baseline in the diagonal half)*.
drills.steps: The server tries to hit an unreturnable serve. The server wins the point if the returner can't return crosscourt; the returner wins by returning crosscourt. Play to 4, switch roles, then switch sides.
drills.cues: *(added)* "Short turn, firm hand", "Block it back crosscourt", "Use the server's pace".
drills.progression: Play out the point on the half-court, with the returner scoring 2 for winning the rally. The server serves from between the service line and the baseline.
drills.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3TxZTZEEg44 — "TENNIS RETURN | Block Your Return Of Serve With This Grip" — Tennis Evolution
drills.regression: *(added)* Server at three-quarter pace; returner starts a step back.

drills.name: Team Up and Down the River (return inside the baseline)
drills.skill: Return (on the rise, return to target)
drills.works: Taking the return early and moving the server. Fixes a passive returner who stands deep (F12).
drills.players: Teams of two on opposite baselines; multiple courts.
drills.setup: Full-court singles points. The returner stands inside the baseline.
drills.steps: Each team serves two points in turn. The server gets one serve; the returner drives the ball to a corner. The winning player stays in for an extra point and the loser rotates out. On "time", the winning team moves up a court and the losing team moves down (partners split).
drills.cues: "Take the return on the rise", "Drive it to a corner".
drills.progression: Returner must hit a forehand; return and come to the net.
drills.source: [USTA Yellow, Ch.02, "Team Up and Down the River" (PDF)](https://preview.usta.com/content/dam/usta/content-fragments/tennis-service-center/assets/pdfs/Net-Generation-Practice-Plan-Yellow.pdf)
drills.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9xlqYxbSnA4 — "Dominate The Return Of Serve | 4 Easy Tennis Tips" — 2MinuteTennis
drills.regression: "Serve underhand or with drop hit."

drills.name: Pinch + Step Up (compact backswing, second-serve attack)
drills.works: Taking the ball early with a compact backswing; attacking second serves. Fixes a big backswing (F13) and a passive returner (F12).
drills.players: Pairs; 2-3 pairs per court.
drills.setup: Part A, Pinch: rally with toes on the service line and no stepping backward, then back up and rally with toes on the baseline. Part B, Step Up: in points, the returner stands right behind the service line to return second serves.
drills.steps: A) Rally any groundstrokes for up to 2 minutes per line, taking deep balls on the rise and volleying anything in the air. B) Play points; on every second serve the returner steps in behind the service line.
drills.cues: "Don't step back", "Prepare early", "Compact backswing".
drills.progression: Straight ahead, then crosscourt, then one stroke crosscourt, then alternate strokes. "Return and come to net on all second serves" (Yellow "Return and Come In").
drills.source: [USTA Green, Ch.07 "Pinch" and "Step Up" (PDF)](https://preview.usta.com/content/dam/usta/content-fragments/tennis-service-center/assets/pdfs/Net-Generation-Practice-Plan-Green.pdf); [USTA Yellow, "Return and Come In" (PDF)](https://preview.usta.com/content/dam/usta/content-fragments/tennis-service-center/assets/pdfs/Net-Generation-Practice-Plan-Yellow.pdf)
drills.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PWSOJuufdpE — "Return of Serve Drill - Coaching the Advanced Tennis Player" — PlaySportsTV
drills.regression: *(added)* Do Pinch from mid-court with slower balls.

drills.name: Two-on-One Attack (return and come in)
drills.skill: Return (chip and charge, return and approach)
drills.works: Taking the return early and moving forward with a hop step. Fixes a passive returner (F12).
drills.players: 4-5 players per court.
drills.setup: One side has a net player and a baseliner covering the doubles court, with extra players lined up behind the baseliner. On the other side a single "champ" stands on the baseline covering a half-court (middle to the doubles line).
drills.steps: The champ gets one serve; the returner comes to the net and the point is played two on one. The champ can't lob the first two balls. After each point rotate: baseliner to net, net player to the back of the line. After 7 points, bring on a new champ.
drills.cues: "Take return early", "Hop move to approach".
drills.progression: Champ must lob within the first two shots; returner must use a forehand.
drills.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Dl_vM5TnDY4 — "Tennis Lesson - Return of Serve Video #3 - Ready Hop/Split Step - Insight Tennis" — Insight Tennis
drills.regression: *(added)* Champ serves second-serve pace.

drills.name: Overhead Warm-Up (cooperative drop-hit lobs)
drills.ages: Green 9-11, Yellow juniors 11-14 (Yellow 2), Teens, Adults, Senior *(added)*
drills.works: Turning and lifting both arms together, controlled direction. Fixes no turn / no pointing hand (F15) and letting the ball drop (F14).
drills.players: Pairs; 2 pairs per court on half-courts.
drills.setup: One player at the net and one at the baseline of the same half-court.
drills.steps: The baseliner drop-hits a lob; the net player smashes it back to the baseliner, who traps or stops it and repeats. After 6 successful overheads, switch.
drills.cues: "Both arms up and turn shoulders at the same time", *(added)* "Point at the ball", "Hit it at full reach".
drills.progression: Lob one short, then one deep; play a cooperative rally and keep the ball going.
drills.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=msN27A6QiAk — "Improve your tennis game: Overhead drill" — United States Tennis Association (USTA)
drills.regression: The baseliner moves to the 60-foot baseline (closer, orange-court length).

drills.name: Shadow Smash Rotation (coach-fed lobs)
drills.works: Technique through repetition and watching others; control over power. Fixes swinging too early (F16) and no turn (F15).
drills.players: 4+ players and a coach feeder; basket.
drills.setup: Two hitters at the net (*added:* one in each service box, about 2 m off the net). Two "shadow" players stand behind or beside them and mirror them. Others wait in the alley. The coach feeds from the opposite side *(added: from the baseline center)*.
drills.steps: The coach lobs to hitter 1, who smashes; hitter 2 and both shadows mirror the movement. Then a lob to hitter 2. Each hitter smashes twice, then goes to the end of the line; the shadow becomes the hitter and a waiting player becomes the shadow.
drills.cues: "Smashes should be hit cross-court, away from teacher"; control and movement over power.
drills.progression: Related Sportplan drills: "Run and Smash", "Approach and Smash", "Touch and Smash".
drills.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NOMh7eK5HY4 — "Tennis Overhead Smash Technique - How To Never Miss An Overhead Again" — PlayYourCourt.com
drills.regression: *(added)* Lower, shorter lobs; let the ball bounce first (bounce overhead).

drills.name: Smash and Touch the Net (10-in-a-row)
drills.works: Moving back with a turn, then recovering forward. Fixes late feet and letting the ball drop (F14).
drills.players: 1-3 players per coach; basket.
drills.setup: Player at the net *(added: in the middle of a service box)*; the coach feeds lobs from the opposite baseline.
drills.steps: The coach feeds alternating lobs. After each overhead the player runs up to touch the net, then moves back for the next. Count successful overheads to 10.
drills.cues: *(added)* "Turn first, then move back", "Side-shuffle or crossover", "Point at the ball".
drills.progression: *(added)* Deeper lobs that require a scissor kick (O5); a target cone.
drills.source: [CoachTube, Best Tennis Drills for Coaches – "Over Overhead" (search snippet; not fetched)](https://coachtube.com/course_lesson/best-tennis-drills-for-coaches/over-overhead/19915772)
drills.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yBtXMU7hpwY — "TENNIS OVERHEAD SMASH | Footwork For The Tennis Overhead" — Tennis Evolution
drills.regression: *(added)* Short lobs; allow a bounce.

drills.name: Three Ball Throw (move back and explode up)
drills.works: Drop-step or crossover back, loading the back leg, driving up while throwing. Fixes no leg drive (F6) and poor overhead footwork (F14, F15).
drills.players: Pairs on opposite sides of the net, up to 3 pairs per court; 3 balls per player.
drills.setup: On one side, players start at the net (one at each sideline and one in the middle). On the same side, each player has 3 balls in a straight line behind them: middle of the service box, on the service line, and on the baseline.
drills.steps: Starting at the net, turn, jog to the first ball, bend, grab it and throw it high over the net in one motion. Turn back, jog to the second ball, and so on. The partners catch all three, place them in the same spots, and switch roles.
drills.cues: "Drop-step/crossover", "Load on back leg", "Drive up with legs as you throw".
drills.progression: *(added)* Throw at a target zone; add a shadow overhead swing.
drills.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Ub2tLbOZvFg — "Overhead Smash Tennis | Footwork (Step by Step) 2018" — CLUTCH Tennis
drills.regression: "Pick up ball, pause, then throw."

drills.name: Scissor-Kick Overhead Drill
drills.ages: Teens 14-18, Adult advanced *(added: not for seniors or beginners)*
drills.works: Attacking deep lobs: jump off the back leg, legs switch in the air, land on the front leg. Fixes letting deep lobs drop and backpedalling (F14).
drills.players: Player and feeder; basket.
drills.setup: *(added)* Player starts at the net in the center; feeder at the opposite baseline lobs deep (landing around the hitter's service line or deeper).
drills.steps: *(added, from the drill format described in the source)* Feed a deep lob; the player turns, crossover-steps back, jumps off the back leg and scissors the legs while hitting, then recovers forward to the net for the next lob ("grinder" repeats, as a cardio drill).
drills.cues: *(added)* "Turn and point", "Push off the back leg", "Legs switch in the air", "Land on the front leg".
drills.progression: *(added)* Alternate deep and short lobs; finish to a target.
drills.source: [YouTube: "Tennis Scissors Kick Overhead Drill" — Topspin Tennis (search description: "Grinder Overhead Scissors Kick Drill… a cardio drill")](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=h2RPMEbPvoU)
drills.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=h2RPMEbPvoU — "Tennis Scissors Kick Overhead Drill" — Topspin Tennis. Also https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VGtXgQFcFyY — "Tennis Tip - Scissor Kick Overhead" — Edgar Giffenig Tennis - Effective Instruction; https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uzRHRX4QwEE — "Scott Nagle Tennis: Tennis Tip: Scissor Kick Overhead Smash." — Scott Nagle
drills.regression: *(added)* Shadow scissor kicks with no ball; let deep lobs bounce.

drills.name: Lob and Play (overhead in doubles context)
drills.works: Handling lobs, communication, finishing overheads in live play (F14, F15, F16).
drills.players: Two teams of 2-4 per court.
drills.setup: Teams start in the one-up, one-back doubles position.
drills.steps: Play no-ad doubles games where the returner must lob the return. Rotate players every two points and switch opponents every two games.
drills.cues: "Lob down the line over the net player", "Communicate on every lob".
drills.progression: Lob down the line; the returner comes to the net if the lob is deep.
drills.video: No verified drill-specific video found.
drills.regression: Start the point with a drop-hit lob down the line.

drills.name: Copy Cat Overhead Shadow (net to baseline)
drills.works: Moving back while turned sideways. Fixes backpedalling while facing the net and not turning (F15).
drills.players: Up to 4 players per side; no balls.
drills.setup: Players line up across the baseline.
drills.steps: The coach demonstrates and players copy: three approaches (hop move) to the net, then three shadow overheads moving from the net back to the baseline.
drills.cues: *(added)* "Turn, point, shuffle back", "Swing up at full reach".
drills.progression: Add a coach-tossed or fed ball (go to O1 or O2).
drills.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yBtXMU7hpwY — "TENNIS OVERHEAD SMASH | Footwork For The Tennis Overhead" — Tennis Evolution
drills.regression: *(added)* One overhead shadow only, standing still.

drills.name: Volley Catch (hand-tap → racquet volley)
drills.ages:
- Red 5–8 and orange 8–10.
- Adult beginner and senior.
- The LTA wrote it for secondary-school PE, roughly yellow-age beginners.
drills.works: Teaches "tap, no swing", contact in front, and racquet head above wrist. It is the first fix for swinging at volleys (X1).
drills.players: Pairs; 1 tennis ball per pair; racquets added in stage 3.
drills.setup:
- Student 1 (feeder) and Student 2 (volleyer) stand on opposite sides of the net, each about 1 m back from it, facing each other.
- Works across a low or mini net or a full net. Spread several pairs along the net.
drills.steps:
1. S1 throws underarm toward S2's right side at shoulder height. S2 taps the ball back with the right hand. Do ×5, then swap roles.
2. S1 throws to S2's left side. S2 taps it back with the left hand. Do ×5, then swap.
3. S2 now holds a racquet and repeats the sequence as forehand and backhand volleys.
drills.cues:
- Sender: "accurate underarm throw", "control direction and speed".
- Receiver: "ready position", "adapt body and racket to the ball", "racket head above the wrist", "contact in front and to the side of the shoes", "tap the ball (no swing)".
drills.progression: S1 alternates throws to right and left so S2 must choose forehand or backhand volley (×5, swap). S2 must "recover quickly into the ready position" between balls.
drills.regression: Catch the ball instead of tapping it (NG uses this as a regression in Solar System, N3). Reduce the distance. Use a red foam ball.
drills.source: [LTA Youth Schools Secondary PE Activity Card 24, "Body & Ball – Volley catch"](https://www.lta.org.uk/siteassets/education/file/secondary-pe-inc-tl-red-and-cardio/body--ball---volley-catch.pdf)
drills.video:
- [related] [Tennis Coaching for Kids: Volley Drills](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SUVyf-aype4) — intosport
- [related] [The tennis volley technique- Kids volleying drill](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=b2GDvKThRjQ) — Tennis Haus

drills.name: Volley Progression: Toss–Volley–Catch → Trap → Drop-hit Rally
drills.ages: Red 5–8 (NG Red 3); also an orange regression.
drills.works: Control. Returning to ready position after each volley. Stepping with the correct foot.
drills.players: Pairs, at most 3 pairs per court. Red balls, 19–23-inch racquets, mini-net or rope.
drills.setup: Three pairs per court on opposite sides of the net, each player about 3 ft from the net. One feeds, one volleys.
drills.steps:
1. Feeder tosses; volleyer "dinks" it back; feeder catches after the bounce. After 4 successes, switch. Once successful, the volleyer returns to ready position after every ball.
2. Both players take two steps back. The feeder, racquet under arm, tosses and traps the volley after the bounce. 4 reps, then switch.
3. Both take another step back. Feeder drop-hits; volleyer volleys so it bounces; feeder hits back; volleyer volleys again; feeder traps. 4 sequences, then switch.
4. Repeat on the backhand side: toss–volley–catch, then toss–volley–trap, then drop-hit–volley–rally–volley–trap. A coach or helper may need to feed the last stage.
drills.cues: "Return to ready position." "Step with the correct foot." (NG Goal)
drills.progression: Alternate forehands and backhands. Direct volleys to the feeder's left and right.
drills.regression:
Catch instead of volley. Coach feeds.
- **Note:** NG teaching tip: children who catch easily one-handed are candidates for the continental grip and a one-handed backhand volley.
drills.source: [USTA NG Red Ball Practice & Play Plans, Ch. 7 "Watch Me Volley"](https://www.usta.com/content/dam/usta/content-fragments/tennis-service-center/assets/pdfs/Net-Generation-Practice-Plan-Red.pdf)

drills.name: Solar System (team volley-defence game)
drills.works: A ready position held as a habit. Volleying under game pressure. Toss accuracy for the other team.
drills.players: Teams of 3–4 on opposite sides of the net. Hula-hoops in each service box on the net players' side. A bucket of balls on the opposite baseline. Seven half-cones plus one ball behind each baseline for visual scoring.
drills.setup: One team (volleyers) starts at the net in front of the hoops. The other team (tossers) starts on the service line on the other side, with the bucket behind them at their baseline.
drills.steps:
1. Two players from each team go at once.
2. The tosser grabs a ball (the "meteorite"), runs to the service line and tosses it, trying to land it past the volleyer into a hoop (a "planet").
3. The volleyer tries to volley meteorites out of the air.
4. After tossing, the tosser fetches a new ball from the bucket. Volleyers wait behind the service line for their next turn.
5. Each point (ball in hoop, or successful volley) sends that player to the scoring cones to move the ball one cone.
6. First team to 7 wins, then sides switch.
drills.cues: "Toss with accuracy." "Good ready position as volleyer." NG coaching tip: first-to-7 is red-ball tiebreak scoring.
drills.progression: Start each point with a drop-hit from the service line.
drills.regression: Players catch instead of volleying.
drills.video: [related] [Improving Reactions And Fun Tennis Volley Drill](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6qwVWIYRW3c) — Feel Tennis Instruction. Its description says reaction drills before volley training are "extremely useful" and that kids love them.

drills.name: Close the Net (approach → split-step → volley, red/orange)
drills.works: Arriving at the net on balance in ready position. A split step before the volley. Controlled volley direction. Corrects never closing in and having no split step (X5, X8).
drills.players: Pairs, two pairs per court, each on a half-court. Red balls.
drills.setup: The volleyer starts on the service line. The feeder stands at the net on the opposite side, in the same half-court.
drills.steps:
1. The volleyer drop-hits the ball down the line, moves toward the net and split-steps.
2. The feeder tosses to the volleyer, who volleys back to the feeder.
3. After 6 attempts, switch roles.
drills.cues: NG Goal: "Arrive at net on balance in ready position, and control volley."
drills.progression:
1. The volleyer hits both forehand and backhand volleys.
2. The feeder catches the approach and tosses it back.
3. The feeder has a racquet: traps the approach, drop-hits it, and traps again.
drills.regression: Go back to N2 with no approach, or start the volleyer halfway between service line and net (suggested; not in source).
drills.video: [exact concept, red group] [MatchPoint NYC QuickStart Red Ball 3 Group: Approach Volley Combination](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-P3LTb4XJMQ) — MatchPoint NYC

drills.name: Figure 8 Volley (orange) / V Volley (yellow)
drills.works: Redirecting volleys with an open face. Placement control so the partner moves no more than 1–2 steps.
drills.players: Pairs, two pairs per court, each on a half-court.
drills.setup: Both players start in the front half of the service box, on opposite sides of their half-court.
drills.steps:
**Figure 8:** 
1. Volley cooperatively. One player volleys every ball down the line; the other volleys every ball crosscourt, so the ball traces a figure 8.
2. Control each shot so the partner takes no more than one step.
3. One minute per pattern, then switch. Two rounds in total.
**V Volley:** 
1. One player sends every ball to the partner's forehand volley (isolation). The partner alternates down the line, then crosscourt.
2. Control the volley so the partner takes no more than 1–2 small steps.
3. After 1 minute, switch roles. Then isolate the backhand.
drills.cues: NG Goal: "Use an open face to keep ball in the air."
drills.progression: Increase distance from the net. One side hits all forehand or all backhand volleys. Use "excessive underspin" (yellow).
drills.regression: Use an orange ball (yellow plan "Need help?").
drills.source: [USTA NG Orange plan, Ch. 7 warm-up](https://www.usta.com/content/dam/usta/content-fragments/tennis-service-center/assets/pdfs/Net-Generation-Practice-Plan-Orange.pdf); [USTA NG Yellow plan](https://www.usta.com/content/dam/usta/content-fragments/tennis-service-center/assets/pdfs/Net-Generation-Practice-Plan-Yellow.pdf)
drills.video: [related] [Ultimate Volley Control Drill](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ho10PRSKwpU) — Essential Tennis - Lessons and Instruction for Passionate Players

drills.name: Volley Controls / Volley-to-Volley (cooperative)
drills.ages: Yellow 11–14 and teens. Adult beginner–intermediate. Seniors as a warm-up.
drills.works: Continental grip and a one-handed backhand volley (fixes X2). Consistency. "Ball should come up off the racquet" (an open face).
drills.players: Pairs, two pairs per court on half-courts. All play inside the service boxes.
drills.setup: Both players stand in the middle of the service box, on opposite sides of their half-court.
drills.steps:
1. Rally easy volleys. Start crosscourt using the "outside volley".
2. After 1 minute, move to the next progression: (a) volley crosscourt, then the same from the other side; (b) rally down the line with the outside volley, then switch.
drills.cues: NG Goal: "Keep continental grip and one hand on backhand." "Ball should come up off the racquet."
drills.progression:
"Mini-Tennis Dubz" (2 v 2 inside the service boxes):
- Any player starts the point with a drop-hit.
- All shots are slices or volleys with a continental grip.
- After the drop-hit, each side must let the ball bounce at least once before moving forward to volley.
- Rotate one spot every minute. Variants: one stroke only; no lobs.
drills.regression: "If players struggle, use an orange or red ball."
drills.video:
- [exact, chapter 1:31 "Volley to Volley"] [7 High Intensity Drills to Improve Your Tennis Doubles Play](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1Cf249OHYiw) — Meike Babel Tennis
- [related, regression] [Doubles Tactics / Strategy - Warm Up Volleys with Red Mini Tennis Ball](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ixjoXTfewNY) — Be Gr8 at Tennis - Rob Cherry

drills.name: Four Corner Volley Drill (Wayne Bryan)
drills.ages: Teens 14–18; adult intermediate–advanced; advanced yellow juniors.
drills.works: Volleying accuracy and consistency from behind the service line. Balance while moving. A short backswing (fixes X1).
drills.players: 2 players (or 2 v 2). Cones or targets in the four corners of the court.
drills.setup: Players stand behind the service line on opposite sides of the net. Place target cones in all four corners of the court.
drills.steps:
- *Defensive mode:* volley back and forth aiming at corner targets, chasing 50 volleys in a row.
- *Offensive mode:* volley directly at the opponent.
drills.cues: "Keep it simple." "Good balance when moving to the ball." "A simple backswing with a lot of control."
drills.progression: Offensive mode (hit at the opponent). Raise the target count needed.
drills.regression: Start closer to the net; lower the target count (e.g., 20). *The regression numbers are a suggestion; the source says only that intensity can be adjusted to level.*
drills.video: No exact video found. [related] [Net Drills With Jamie Murray | MASTERCLASS | ATP](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=h63xYUQbMtk) — ATP Tour

drills.name: Romanian Davis Cup (RDC) Drill
drills.ages: Teens; adult advanced (4.0–4.5); advanced yellow juniors. Intermediate players can do it with a slower ball.
drills.works: Footwork and racquet control at the net. "Independence of the hands and feet". Adjusting to different balls. Fixes reaching instead of moving (X12).
drills.players: Two volleyers across the net (per the written source).
drills.setup: Volley-to-volley positions across the net; both players shuffle side to side while volleying. *The exact spacing, start position and pattern are not given in the written source; take them from the video.*
drills.steps: Continuous volley exchange while both players shuffle laterally.
drills.cues: "Continental grip", "clean footwork", "fast hands", "real control".
drills.progression: Speed up the exchange; add direction rules (suggested).
drills.regression: Stand still for cooperative volleys first (N6).

drills.name: Up-and-Back Volley (approach → split → volley → retreat, continuous)
drills.works: Approach footwork, correct grips, ready position and split step. Fixes no split step (X8) and stopping in no-man's-land (X5).
drills.players: Pairs, two pairs per court, each on a half-court.
drills.setup: Both players start on the service line of their half-court, on opposite sides.
drills.steps:
1. P1 drop-feeds a short ball to P2.
2. P2 hits an approach shot, comes to the net and split-steps.
3. P1 hits an easy groundstroke. P2 volleys and retreats behind the service line.
4. P1 lets the volley bounce, uses it as an approach shot, comes in and split-steps.
5. P2 hits back. P1 volleys and retreats. Repeat.
drills.cues: "Approach, split, volley." Use a carioca move on a slice backhand approach and a hop move on a topspin approach.
drills.progression: Topspin approach, then slice.
drills.regression: "Trap each groundstroke and drop-hit back to partner."
drills.source: [USTA NG Orange plan, Ch. 6](https://www.usta.com/content/dam/usta/content-fragments/tennis-service-center/assets/pdfs/Net-Generation-Practice-Plan-Orange.pdf); [USTA NG Yellow plan](https://www.usta.com/content/dam/usta/content-fragments/tennis-service-center/assets/pdfs/Net-Generation-Practice-Plan-Yellow.pdf)

drills.name: Hi-Lo (volley + overhead control) / Overhead Warm-up
drills.ages: Orange 8–10 (Hi-Lo); yellow 11–14 (Overhead Warm-up); adult beginner; seniors at reduced pace.
drills.works: Split-stepping and moving forward to volley. Overhead preparation (turn plus both arms up). Fixes backpedalling for overheads (X13).
drills.players: Pairs, two pairs per court on half-courts.
drills.setup: One player at the net, the other at the baseline, on opposite sides of their half-court.
drills.steps:
1. The baseliner alternates groundstrokes and lobs, starting with a drop-hit groundstroke. The net player volleys back and the baseliner traps.
2. The baseliner drop-hits a lob. The net player hits an overhead back. The baseliner traps and continues the sequence.
3. Complete 4 sequences, then switch.
The baseliner drop-hits a lob; the net player hits an overhead back; the baseliner traps and repeats. Six successful overheads, then switch.
drills.cues: NG Goal: "Split-step and move forward to volley." Overhead: "Move both arms up and turn shoulder simultaneously."
drills.progression: A cooperative rally that keeps the ball going. The lob is hit with a continental grip (drop-hit first, then in a rally).
drills.regression:
The baseliner moves up to the service line.
- **Related USTA progression:** A three-part overhead progression: block, then catch, then hit.
drills.source: [USTA NG Orange plan, Ch. 7 "Over My Head"](https://www.usta.com/content/dam/usta/content-fragments/tennis-service-center/assets/pdfs/Net-Generation-Practice-Plan-Orange.pdf); [USTA NG Yellow plan](https://www.usta.com/content/dam/usta/content-fragments/tennis-service-center/assets/pdfs/Net-Generation-Practice-Plan-Yellow.pdf)

drills.name: Half-Volley Service-Line Drill
drills.ages: Advanced green 9–11, yellow 11–14 and teens; adult intermediate–advanced.
drills.works: Handling balls at the feet in the transition zone, which is what happens when a player is caught in no-man's-land (X5).
drills.players: 2 players (or coach plus player). Basket.
drills.setup: The player stands on the service line. The partner stands at the baseline, or at the net, on the other side.
drills.steps:
1. The partner hits medium-pace balls at the player's feet.
2. The player takes each ball immediately after the bounce with an abbreviated groundstroke.
3. Stay near the service line instead of moving forward, so the shot can be repeated.
4. "A few minutes" in each workout.
drills.cues: "Abbreviated ground stroke motion." Hit right after the bounce; the sound should be a rapid "ba-bomp".
drills.progression: After the half-volley, close forward and play the next ball as a volley (suggested; links to N9).
drills.regression: Drop-fed or hand-fed balls at the feet; an orange ball.

drills.name: Fed Approach + Split (short-ball approach progression)
drills.ages: Green 9–11, yellow 11–14 and teens; adult beginner–intermediate.
drills.works: Depth over power. Early turn and lateral (not straight-line) movement. Staying grounded (not jumping). Split step on the way in. Fixes X6.
drills.players: Feeder plus player; basket.
drills.setup:
**A:** The player stands 1–2 ft behind the service line. The feeder tosses waist-high balls straight ahead of the player for mid-court groundstrokes.
**B:** The player starts at the baseline. The feeder stands near the net on the centre line and tosses balls that bounce 1–2 ft past the player's service line (toward the baseline). The player moves forward, split-steps, then hits the approach.
drills.steps: Receive the feed, turn early, move laterally, strike without jumping, then move toward the net after contact. "Hit the same ball over and over"; the ball should drop before the baseline.
drills.cues: "Depth over power." "Turn early." "Don't jump." "Move to the net after contact." "Split when you reach the service box area." (TennisCompanion)
drills.progression:
1. Feed from the opposite baseline; add volleys.
2. Half-court points to 10 (ask "were my approaches deep?").
3. Full-court points that start with a down-the-line approach, played as tiebreakers.
drills.regression: Setup A (no movement); slower or higher feeds.

drills.name: Looking for Short Balls ("short ball attack" decision drill)
drills.ages: Teens; adult intermediate–advanced; advanced yellow juniors.
drills.works: Recognising short balls. Committing to the down-the-line approach and following it in. Fixes approaching off the wrong ball (X6).
drills.players: Coach or partner plus player. Two cones.
drills.setup: Place two cones on the player's side to form a depth line across the court. The coach or partner hits from the opposite baseline to anywhere.
drills.steps:
1. Ball lands short of the cone line: the player must hit down the line and approach the net.
2. Ball lands past the cone line: the player hits crosscourt only.
3. After a down-the-line approach, the point is open (play it out).
drills.cues: "Short = down the line and follow it in." "Deep = crosscourt and stay back." (paraphrase of the drill rules)
drills.progression: Play to 10 or play tiebreakers; the coach mixes depth more subtly.
drills.regression: Move the cone line deeper so more balls count as short (suggested; not in source).

drills.name: Triples (green) / Two-on-One Attack (yellow) — net player vs passing shots
drills.ages: Green 9–11 (Triples); yellow 11–14 (Two-on-One Attack); teens and adults (2-on-1).
drills.works: Closing the net and angling volleys. Passing shots and lobs for the baseliners. Live decision-making.
drills.players: Triples: two teams of 3–4 per court. Two-on-One: 4–5 per court.
drills.setup:
**Triples:** Three players per side: one at the net and two on the baseline. Extra players wait behind the baseline.
**Two-on-One Attack:** 
- One side: a net player and a baseliner covering the full doubles court, with extras lined up behind the baseliner.
- Other side: a single player (the "champ") on the opposite baseline covering half the court, from the middle to the doubles line.
drills.steps:
**Triples:** 
1. The coach or a player feeds the first ball to a deep player.
2. Only the net player may volley.
3. Rotate one spot after each point. Play to a set number of points, then change teams.
**Two-on-One Attack:** The champ gets one serve. The returner comes to the net. Play the point out 2-on-1. *The rest of the rotation and scoring text was not captured.*
drills.cues: NG Goal (Triples): "Use spin on passing shots, close the net and angle volleys."
drills.progression: Switch to two up / one back to encourage lobs. Use doubles or singles boundaries.
drills.regression: Fed (cooperative) first ball; net player allowed to start at the service line (suggested).

drills.name: Charge! Doubles / Team Defender / Chip & Charge (return-and-come-in transition games)
drills.ages: Orange 8–10 (Charge! Doubles); green 9–11 (Team Defender, Chip & Charge); yellow, teens and adults.
drills.works: Returning and coming in. Split step inside the service line. Taking the return early. Fixes X5 and X8.
drills.setup:
**Charge! Doubles:** 4–8 players per court in teams of 2–3.
**Team Defender:** At least 6 players, two courts, teams of 3–4. Each team defends its own court and sends one challenger to another court.
drills.steps:
**Charge! Doubles:** 
1. The serving team serves once. The receiver must come to the net after the return.
2. Play 4 points with the same serving team, then rotate. With 4 per side, rotate the team after each point; with 3, rotate one spot; with 2, play several points in a row.
3. NG Goal: "Return serve and split-step inside service line."
4. Progressions: serving team can't lob; topspin approach, then slice.
5. NG coaching tip: talk about "shading at the net in doubles (following the ball)", using guided-discovery questions.
**Team Defender:** 
1. The challenger gets one serve. The defender must return and come in.
2. Rotate after each point.
3. Goal: "Take return early and use lower body for more power."
- **Chip & Charge (green, play on your own):** Half-court points. On first serve, the server must serve and volley. On second serve, the returner must slice and come to the net.

drills.name: Moonballer (everything in the air)
drills.ages: Orange 8–10; works for yellow and adult intermediate as a fun game.
drills.works: Controlling overheads to the left and right. Coming in behind the return. Fixes backpedalling for lobs (X13).
drills.players: 4–6 players per court; full-court points.
drills.setup: One or two servers; everyone else is a returner.
drills.steps:
1. The server gets one serve. The returner must come to the net.
2. The server lobs the entire time. The returner must play every ball in the air.
3. Score servers vs returners. Rotate after a set number of points.
drills.cues: NG Goal: "Control overheads to left and right side of court."
drills.progression: Serve must go to a specific side.
drills.regression: Server lobs from the service line (suggested).
drills.video: [related] [How to get to EVERY tennis overhead - Footwork Masterclass](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=z2dOBIKitc8) — Meike Babel Tennis

drills.works: Attacking high, slow floaters from mid-court, then closing for the finishing volley. Shot selection between high volley, swing volley and overhead.
drills.players: Feeder plus player. *The written setup is not available.*

drills.cues: See the shot-selection video. Written cues were not retrieved.
drills.progression: Progression: feeds with less margin, then live finish.
