drills.name: Walking Tennis Volley Warm-up + Push-Serve-and-Volley (seniors / low-impact)
drills.ages: Seniors. Also adult beginners, players returning from injury, and players with limited mobility.
drills.works: Volley fundamentals and closing to the net without running or jumping.
drills.players:
Pairs. Modified equipment and a smaller court are allowed.
- **Walking Tennis rules (LTA):** No running or jumping. The ball may bounce twice (optional). It can be played on a smaller court with modified equipment.
drills.setup: Partners start close together on opposite sides of the net.
drills.steps:
**volley practice:** 
1. Hand-feed to a racquet; increase the distance once both are comfortable; progress to both using racquets.
2. Practise forehand and backhand volleys.
3. Next stage: start at the service line and move forward toward the ball, first with hand feeds and then with both using racquets.
**push serve:** 
1. The racquet is held directly above the head with the elbow straight (arm in line with the ear).
2. Aim the first bounce midway up the service box.
3. The returner hits after one bounce and then closes to the net. The server comes in immediately after serving (serve and volley).
drills.cues: LTA: technical guidance should be limited to fundamentals and foundational skills; keep it social, informal and fun.
drills.progression: "Double bounce box push groundstrokes" → "One in one out" (first bounce in the service box, second bounce outside it but in the court) → situational games.
drills.regression: Two bounces allowed everywhere; hand feeds only.
drills.video: [related; a 77-year-old player using simple technique] [Mastering Tennis as a Senior Player](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4KTGlCGGc_M) — TPA tennis

drills.name: Hopscotch (split-step foundation)
drills.works: The landing pattern behind the split step. Balance. The groundwork for later fixing a missing split (X8).
drills.players: One hopscotch area for every 4–6 players, made with an agility ladder, cones or chalk (traditional or non-traditional shapes). A beanbag or cone as the marker.
drills.setup: Hopscotch grids spread around the court, with players in lines at each grid.
drills.steps:
1. Place a marker for each player in one square.
2. Hop through the squares and over the marked square.
3. On the way back, pick up the marker while balancing on one leg, hop back, and hand the marker to the coach.
drills.cues: "Hop from one foot to two" (NG teaching tip). "Balance on one leg to pick up."
drills.progression:
1. Place the marker in square 1, then move it to square 2 and so on as each player succeeds.
2. Let players place the marker themselves.
3. Change the square shapes (e.g., circles) and add "islands" to jump over.
drills.regression: Two-foot hops only; fewer squares (suggested).
drills.source: [USTA NG Red plan, Red Ball 3 Athletic Skills](https://www.usta.com/content/dam/usta/content-fragments/tennis-service-center/assets/pdfs/Net-Generation-Practice-Plan-Red.pdf)
drills.video: [related] [Mini red tennis-movement drill](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XpagfhaRjAU) — Mini Tennis Insight. Its description notes safety rules: players face the net, take one ball at a time, are warned about racquets when moving backward, and lay racquet handles toward the net.

drills.name: Tunnel Ball (turn-and-chase first step)
drills.works: Turning and accelerating after a ball, and tracking.
drills.players: Pairs, 2–3 pairs on each side of the net. One ball per pair (playground or red).
drills.setup: Pairs start on the sideline facing each other about 5 ft apart. One player has the ball and both feet on the sideline; the other stands with feet apart.
drills.steps:
1. Roll the ball between the partner's legs at medium speed.
2. The partner turns, chases it down before it reaches the opposite sideline, and tosses it back.
3. After 4 successful rolls and catches, switch.
drills.cues: "Turn and go." "Catch it before the far line." (paraphrase)
drills.progression:
1. The catcher starts facing the partner, then with their back to the partner.
2. Increase roll or toss speed.
3. Toss over the partner's shoulder or head; the partner catches on the bounce before the opposite sideline, aiming for fewer bounces.
drills.regression: Slower roll; larger ball.
drills.video: [related] [5 FUN KIDS TENNIS Footwork Drills for Coaches and Parents](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5BOTmSksMAk) — Tennis Passion

drills.name: Make 'Em Move (catch → recover to home base)
drills.works: Recovering to a base after every ball, which builds the habit that prevents late recovery (X9). Tracking the ball.
drills.players: Pairs with a red ball and a TDL. At most 3 pairs on each side of the net.
drills.setup: Partners face each other 5–6 ft apart. The catcher uses the TDL as "home base".
drills.steps:
1. The feeder tosses to one side of the catcher. The catcher catches one-handed, tosses back, and recovers to home base.
2. The feeder moves the catcher left and right, with enough height to track the ball.
3. After 4 successful catches, switch.
4. If the feeder struggles, place poly-spots on either side of the catcher as toss targets.
drills.cues: "Catch, toss, back to home base." NG tip: demonstrate a simple, controlled toss.
drills.progression: Higher or lower tosses. Orange ball caught one-handed.
drills.regression: Two-handed catch; shorter distance.
drills.source: [USTA NG Red plan](https://www.usta.com/content/dam/usta/content-fragments/tennis-service-center/assets/pdfs/Net-Generation-Practice-Plan-Red.pdf) (also in the Orange plan)
drills.video: [related] [Tennis Coaching for Kids: Footwork & Stance](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=spHuQNYikH4) — intosport

drills.name: Copy Cat (shadow movement patterns: crossover recovery, hop-move approach, drop-step overhead, carioca)
drills.ages: Orange 8–10, green 9–11 and yellow 11–14. Also adults of any level as a warm-up.
drills.works: Learning recovery and approach footwork patterns without a ball. Fixes X9, X11 and X13.
drills.players: At most 4 players per side; no equipment.
drills.setup:
1. **Crossover recovery:** players lined up from the net to behind the baseline. Run to the sideline, shadow a stroke, cross over, then shuffle back to the middle. Square stance first, then open stance. Complementary skill: carioca.
2. **Hop-move approach:** players lined up across the baseline. Shadow an approach off the front foot. Complementary skill: side skips.
3. **Drop-step, crossover and run for overhead:** players lined up across the net. Complementary skills: pivots and carioca.
4. **Green version:** three hop-move approaches to the net, then three overheads moving from the net back to the baseline. Then three backhand-slice approaches with a carioca to the net; turn around and do three more back to the baseline.
drills.cues: "Square first, then open." "Cross, shuffle, back to the middle." (NG wording)
drills.progression: Add a live feed, then go to F6 / F7.
drills.regression: Walk-through tempo (suggested).
drills.source: [USTA NG Orange plan](https://www.usta.com/content/dam/usta/content-fragments/tennis-service-center/assets/pdfs/Net-Generation-Practice-Plan-Orange.pdf); [USTA NG Green plan](https://www.usta.com/content/dam/usta/content-fragments/tennis-service-center/assets/pdfs/Net-Generation-Practice-Plan-Green.pdf); [USTA NG Yellow plan](https://www.usta.com/content/dam/usta/content-fragments/tennis-service-center/assets/pdfs/Net-Generation-Practice-Plan-Yellow.pdf)

- [related] [Crossover Step | RECOVERY FOOTWORK](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9On2GDwxw6Y) — Daily Tennis Lesson
- [related] [TENNIS OVERHEAD SMASH | Footwork For The Tennis Overhead](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yBtXMU7hpwY) — Tennis Evolution
- [related] [Footwork | OVERHEAD](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rm5VR7iIaCY) — Daily Tennis Lesson

drills.name: Skate and Volley (diagonal volley footwork to the net)
drills.ages: Green 9–11, yellow 11–14 and teens; adult beginner–intermediate.
drills.works: Stepping diagonally forward to volley. Outside-foot-first movement. Upper-body turn. Fixes reaching (X12) and crossing the feet incorrectly at the net (X11).
drills.players: At most 5 players per side, spread along the baseline. Racquets in stage 2.
drills.setup: Players spread out on the baseline, facing the net in ready position.
drills.steps:
1. **Skate:** step diagonally right with the right foot and bring the left foot next to it. Step diagonally left with the left foot and bring the right foot next to it. Continue to the net, turn around, and skate back to the baseline.
2. **Skate and volley:** racquet in hand, volley-ready.
- Step diagonally to the forehand side. As the outside foot lands, pause, turn the upper body and set the hands for a forehand volley.
- Shadow the volley, stepping forward diagonally with the back foot.
- Return to ready position and do the same on the other side for a one-handed backhand volley.
- Continue this way to the net.
drills.cues: "Outside foot first." "Turn the upper body." "Step forward diagonally with back foot."
drills.progression: Skate-volley to the net and back. Then skate-volley to the net, shadow three overheads, and go back to the baseline.
drills.regression: "Just do one forehand volley, back up and do it again. Then switch to backhand."
drills.video:
- [related; split → angle step FH volley → split → angle step BH volley → shuffle back to scissor-kick overhead] [Great Volley And Overhead Drills For Tennis Players](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2xeY9qxX-0k) — The Team Forman Experience
- [related] [Tennis Footwork Drills - Net Game - Volley Two Step Pattern Drill](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=389Ab5DJYb4) — Rope Tennis Education
- [related] [Perfect Tennis Volley Footwork in 4 Steps](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Er3u5m32mtA) — Top Tennis Training - Pro Tennis Lessons

drills.name: Crossover Shuffle
drills.ages: Green 9–11, yellow 11–14 and teens; adult all levels.
drills.works: A smooth change of direction using a crossover into a shuffle. Fixes X9 and X11.
drills.players: At most 5 per side, spread from the net to the baseline. No equipment.
drills.setup: Players spread out between the net and the baseline, facing the net in ready position, with lateral space on both sides.
drills.steps:
1. From ready position, do one crossover into a shuffle and stop.
2. Switch direction and do the same movements back to the start.
3. "Start slowly until you develop rhythm, then speed up."
drills.cues: "Smooth change of direction." "Cross, shuffle, stop."
drills.progression: Go back and forth continuously. Add a shadow stroke at each end (see F4).
drills.regression: Walking tempo.
drills.video: [exact pattern] [Recovery: Crossover - Shuffle](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ChFCGVwkhfk) — Ben Morris Tennis

drills.name: Crossover–Shuffle–Split Line Touches (recovery conditioning)
drills.works: Repeating the full recovery chain (crossover, shuffle, split) at intensity. Fixes late recovery (X9).
drills.players: Individual or a group; court lines only.
drills.setup: Player on court lines. *The exact line layout is not stated in text; the coach touches lines laterally.*
drills.steps: 30 s work / 30 s rest × 3. "Players can usually touch around 20 lines or more when they get this drill down."
drills.cues: "Crossover, shuffle, split." (title of the pattern)
drills.progression: More sets; add a reaction cue for direction.
drills.regression: 20 s work / 40 s rest; walk the pattern (suggested).
drills.video: [exact] [Footwork Recovery Drill - Crossover, Shuffle, Split](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-i85rCBrqro) — Simple Coach's Tennis Videos - Coach Bryan Minton

drills.name: Serpentine Shuffle (forward and backward, facing the net)
drills.skill: Footwork (moving back for deep balls and overheads).
drills.works: Turning while still facing the net when moving backward. Fixes backpedalling and being caught flat on overheads (X13).
drills.players: At most 4 per side. Cones or TDLs in front of the net as stop markers.
drills.setup: Players start on the baseline, spread across the court.
drills.steps:
1. Shuffle toward the net: two shuffles facing one direction, then two shuffles facing the other, turning while facing the net.
2. Stop at the cones and return to the baseline, still facing the net when turning (a backward serpentine).
drills.cues: "Keep facing the net when you turn."
drills.progression: Add a shadow overhead at the end of the backward leg.
drills.regression: Walk it.
drills.video: [related] [TENNIS FOOTWORK LESSON | Tennis Footwork To Handle Deep Balls](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hS-hHJC99F4) — Tennis Evolution

drills.name: Shuffle Toss (lateral shuffle + hand–eye)
drills.works: Shuffling without crossing the feet while tracking a ball. Fixes heavy feet (X10).
drills.players: 3–4 pairs per side; one ball per pair.
drills.setup: Pairs face each other on the doubles sideline.
drills.steps:
1. While shuffling from sideline to sideline, bounce the ball downward (palm down) back and forth to the partner, watching between bounces. Use one hand to bounce and catch.
2. After two successful trips to the far sideline and back, toss and catch in the air.
drills.cues: "Watch between bounces." "One hand."
drills.progression: Left hand only, then right hand only. Different hand than the partner. Alternate two on the bounce, two in the air.
drills.regression: Two hands; walk.
drills.video: [related] [Junior Tennis Footwork Drills That You Can Do Anywhere](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xGCwrk0sWVM) — MPTennis

drills.name: Agility Ladder Series (including split-step pattern)
drills.ages: Green 9–11, yellow 11–14 and teens; adult all levels. Seniors only with low-impact steps (suggested).
drills.works: Foot speed, rhythm and split-step landing (X8, X10).
drills.players: One agility ladder per 4–6 players, at most 2 ladders per side. If no ladders, use chalk or TDLs.
drills.setup: Ladders laid out on court (e.g., parallel to the baseline). Players line up at one end.
drills.steps:
1. The coach demonstrates. Players do each movement twice before a new one is introduced.
2. The next player starts when the previous one is halfway through.
3. NG suggested movements: two feet in (1-2, 1-2 rhythm); sideways 1-2; one-leg hops; two-leg hops; "split-step outside, two feet inside"; player's choice.
4. Other ladder patterns: single-leg in/out; "Ickey shuffle" (right in, left in, step out right; left in, right in, step out left).
drills.cues: "Rhythm before speed." "Light feet."
drills.progression: Finish each ladder rep with a sprint to a fed ball.
drills.regression: Chalk boxes, walking tempo.
drills.video:
- [exact] [10 Agility Ladder Drills For Tennis Players](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XMlBOpbrrQo) — The Tennis Mentor
- [exact] [5 Easy Ladder Footwork Drills for Tennis](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=s9twENtOkwk) — TennisCompanion

drills.name: Colour-Cone Reaction (first-step "cone touches")
drills.ages: All ages. Red/orange as a game; juniors; adults. Seniors at walking pace (suggested).
drills.works: Reacting to a cue, an explosive first step and recovery. Fixes heavy feet and no split (X8, X10).
drills.players: Player plus a caller. At least 2 cones of different colours (any number can be used).
drills.setup: Place different-coloured cones around the player's start position (e.g., to the forehand, backhand and forward diagonals).
drills.steps:
1. The partner or coach shouts a colour. The player touches that cone as fast as possible and recovers to the start.
2. Variation 2: shadow a stroke at the cone instead of touching it.
drills.cues: "Split on the call." "Touch and recover." (paraphrase)
drills.progression: Add a simultaneous split step on the call (see the Athletic Performance Academy 4-cone drill). Add more cones and shorter intervals.
drills.regression: Fewer cones; point instead of calling a colour.
drills.source: [Top Tennis Training video description](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gxf4VnU7YJ4). The description says it is "great for players of all standards and ages but kids really love it".
drills.video:

- [related] [Tennis Footwork- First step speed- 4 cone drill (with simultaneous split)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=K05ducOi7fM) — Athletic Performance Academy
- [related] [Drills to Build an Explosive First Step (On-Court Fitness for Tennis](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DlJBR6FE4J4) — Tennis With Ema (the title has no closing parenthesis as returned)

drills.name: Quickstep Fan (5-cone semicircle) + Figure-8 Cones
drills.works: Sprint-and-recover to multiple directions. Shuffle recovery. Balance on change of direction.
drills.players: Player plus a feeding partner; 5 cones (fan) or 2 cones (figure 8).
drills.setup:
**Fan:** Five cones in a semicircle along the baseline; the player starts at the centre.
**Figure-8:** Two cones about 6 ft apart on the baseline; the player stands between them.
drills.steps:
**Fan:** Sprint to each cone and return four forehands to the partner, shuffling back to the start after every shot. At the final cone, switch to a backhand.
**Figure-8:** Shuffle around the right cone, then the left, in a continuous figure 8. Advanced: the partner feeds and the player hits outside each cone.
drills.cues: "Controlled sprints: fast, sharp, always ready for the next one." (On)
drills.progression: Random cone order called by the feeder; add a timed set.
drills.regression: Shadow strokes without the ball; walk-back recovery.
drills.source: [On, "7 tennis footwork drills" (drills credited to pro Flavio Cobolli)](https://www.on.com/en-us/stories/tennis-footwork-drills)
drills.video: [related] [8 Footwork Drills to Stop Being Late to Every Ball](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9bPKnqr8IO0) — JJG Tennis (cone drills)

drills.name: Spider Run (drill and test)
drills.ages: Teens 14–18; adult intermediate–advanced. Yellow juniors as a test. *Not for red or orange.*
drills.works: Stopping and starting in match-like patterns; change-of-direction speed.
drills.players: 1 player plus a timer; 5 balls; tape for a 12 × 18 inch rectangle.
drills.setup:
- Mark a 12" × 18" rectangle behind the centre of the baseline.
- Place 5 balls at: both baseline/singles-sideline corners, both singles-sideline/service-line intersections, and the centre T.
drills.steps:
1. Start in the rectangle.
2. Retrieve the balls one at a time, counterclockwise, placing each in the rectangle.
3. Time runs until the last ball is placed.
- **Work / rest:** In the touch version, sprint and touch each corner with the foot, return to the centre each time, rest 30 s, then repeat in the other direction. *That version is from a search snippet.*
- **Benchmarks:** Under 15 s is excellent. Males average 15.00–15.30 s. Females are about 3 s slower.
- **Reliability:** The spider drill has low typical error both within session (CV 1.8–4.1%) and between sessions (CV 1.2–3.7%). *Search snippet.*
drills.cues: "Decelerate under control at each ball." (implied by "stopping and starting")
drills.progression: Add a shadow shot at each station (Complete Conditioning variation).
drills.regression: Fewer stations; walk back to centre.
drills.source: [Kovacs, Roetert & Ellenbecker, *Complete Conditioning for Tennis* (USTA) — excerpt via Human Kinetics ME](https://humankinetics.me/2017/06/29/tennis-footwork-drills/); [USHSTA, Spider Drill](https://ushsta.org/?p=813); [Univ. of Hertfordshire reliability study](https://researchprofiles.herts.ac.uk/en/publications/within-and-between-session-reliability-of-the-spider-drill-test-t/)

- [exact] [Tennis Speed & Agility Exercise - The Spider Drill](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=flpvW8O97Q4) — Be Gr8 at Tennis - Rob Cherry
- [exact] [257 Fitness Drill 3 Spider Drill and Variation](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0wG5P4hZmSg) — GreatBase Tennis

drills.name: Horizontal Repeater (shuffle/sprint conditioning)
drills.works: Repeating lateral efforts as in long baseline rallies; recovery capacity.
drills.players: 1+ players; court lines (doubles sidelines, centre service line).
drills.setup: The player starts on one doubles sideline.
drills.steps:
1. Shuffle from the doubles sideline to the centre service line.
2. Sprint back to the start.
3. Sprint to the opposite doubles sideline.
4. Shuffle back to the centre line.
5. Sprint back to the start.
- **Work / rest:** 2–3 repetitions with 30 s rest.
drills.cues: "Low hips on the shuffle." "Don't cross the feet on shuffles." (coach paraphrase)
drills.progression: Hold a racquet throughout (source variation); more reps.
drills.regression: Fewer segments; longer rest.
drills.video: No exact video found. [related] [Transform Your Tennis Footwork In 10 Minutes - Instant Tennis Improvements](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lb1pW5nCPtw) — Top Tennis Training - Pro Tennis Lessons

drills.name: Lateral Cone Slalom
drills.works: Small adjustment steps for positioning. Fixes reaching (X12).
drills.players: 10–12 cones.
drills.setup: Cones along the baseline, about 1 yard apart.
drills.steps:
1. Weave through the cones with sideways adjustment steps.
2. Move diagonally forward to the end cone.
3. Backpedal through the cones to the start.
4. Repeat.
drills.cues: "Small steps, stay low." (coach paraphrase)
drills.progression: Timed; carry a racquet; finish with a fed ball.
drills.regression: Wider cone spacing; walk.
drills.video: [related] [10 Tennis Footwork Drills For Juniors & Beginners (4K)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WLEIfNn1-8M) — Martin Kares Tennistraining (line-based drills)

drills.name: Hexagon Drill / Hex Test
drills.ages: Yellow 11–14 and teens; adults. *Not for seniors or anyone with ankle issues (suggested).*
drills.skill: Agility (foot quickness while facing one direction).
drills.works: Quick multidirectional foot contacts while staying square to the opponent. Fixes heavy feet (X10).
drills.players: Tape hexagon with 24-inch sides; partner with stopwatch.
drills.setup: The player stands in the centre of the hexagon and faces the same direction throughout.
drills.steps:
1. Jump forward over the tape and back to the centre.
2. Continue around all six sides for 3 full revolutions.
3. Time runs from "Ready, go" until the feet land in the hexagon after the final revolution.
- **Benchmarks:** Under 12 s is excellent; 13 s is average. Juniors are typically 0.5 s faster.
drills.cues: "Face forward the whole time." "Quick, low hops." (paraphrase)
drills.progression: Reverse direction; single leg (advanced; suggested).
drills.regression: Step over the lines instead of jumping (suggested).
drills.video: None found.

drills.name: Mini-Tennis Z-Ball (reaction catch game)
drills.ages: Green 9–11, yellow 11–14 and teens; adults. Use the tennis-ball version for younger or beginner players.
drills.works: Reacting to unpredictable bounces; split step and first step (X8, X10).
drills.players: 2+ players; Z-ball (reaction ball); service boxes.
drills.setup: Service boxes only, players on opposite sides of the net.
drills.steps:
1. Toss underhand into the opponent's service box.
2. The ball must bounce once and be caught before the second bounce.
3. Score like a tiebreak to 7.
drills.cues: "Split as they toss." (implied; paraphrase)
drills.progression: Medicine ball (conditioning variant).
drills.regression: Tennis ball (easier).
drills.video: None found for the Z-ball version.

drills.name: Split-Step Timing Drills (feeder-cued split + jump-rope rhythm)
drills.ages:
- Hop version: red and orange, via F1.
- Feeder-cued version: green through adult.
- Jump rope: yellow and up.
drills.works: Missing or mistimed split steps (X8).
drills.players: A human feeder is preferred. Jump rope (optional).
drills.setup:
*The drill as written here is assembled from cited principles; it is not a single published drill.*
1. The player starts at the baseline and walks or jogs in toward the net. The feeder, on the other side, feeds a volley each time the player advances.
2. The player starts the hop as the feeder starts the swing, and lands as or just after contact. Landing may be one foot then the other.
3. Push off immediately toward the ball.
4. Variation: jump-rope sets to build the hop rhythm.
drills.cues:
- "Initiate a split step before the contact"; "more of a hop"; "land already knowing where the ball is going". — [Feel Tennis Instruction](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XR83yXLla8w)
- The benefit depends on the landing coinciding with the directional cue. — [Uzu et al. 2009](https://lida.sport-iat.de/twm/Record/4017156?lng=en)
- The NG Up-and-Back / Close the Net drills (N4, N9) build the split into transition patterns.
drills.progression: Random-direction feeds; live 2-on-1 (N14).
drills.regression: Hopscotch (F1); ladder "split outside, two feet inside" (F10).
drills.video:
- [exact] [Tennis Split Step Timing, Execution And Drills](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XR83yXLla8w) — Feel Tennis Instruction
- [exact] [How To Master The Split Step in 5 Minutes: Beginner to Pro](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=J1UhPl1UrYs) — Top Tennis Training - Pro Tennis Lessons
- [exact] [Tennis Beginner Lesson: Why, When and How To Split-Step + Drills](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UtARjzWH5PQ) — Meike Babel Tennis

drills.name: Walking Tennis Functional Movement Warm-up (seniors)
drills.ages: Seniors. Also adults returning from injury, limited mobility and adult beginners.
drills.works: Maintaining functional movement (lunge, lateral step, hinge, squat) that supports court movement without running or jumping. Addresses flat-footed or "frozen" seniors (X10).
drills.players: Group; court fence for incline push-ups; partners.
drills.setup: Arrive early for health check-ins (optional medical declarations), then "Walk and Talk" laps of the court.
drills.steps:
1. **Walk awareness:** walk tall with arms overhead; strike heel to toe; rotate shoulders with relaxed elbows.
2. **Shoulder patterns:** arm extensions; scapula squeezes; scissor arms; "hug"; incline push-up against the fence.
3. **Partner palm push:** 10 s each arm while lifting the same-side leg.
4. **Lateral step:** a large step to the side, flexing hip, knee and ankle; return; repeat on the other side.
5. **Reverse lunge** ("train track" feet) with arms overhead.
6. **Forward lunge with a twist** over the bent leg.
7. **Squat with arms raised.**
8. **Single-leg hinge reach** toward the floor.
9. Cool down: "really important, particularly for older participants or those with bone or muscular related health conditions".
drills.cues: Keep it social and informal; posture "walking tall".
drills.progression: Add tennis warm-up (N18), then situational games.
drills.regression: Seated or fence-supported versions (suggested).
drills.video: [related] [Mastering Tennis as a Senior Player](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4KTGlCGGc_M) — TPA tennis

drills.name: Crosscourt Half-Court Points (crosscourt-only game)
drills.ages: yellow juniors 11-14; teens 14-18; adult intermediate; adult advanced. For green 9-11, use the Net Gen "Half-Court Battle" variant below. (Stage mapping inferred.)
drills.works: hitting to the middle with no plan; changing direction too early; building crosscourt consistency and dominance.
drills.players: 2 per diagonal (4 per court using both diagonals); a basket of balls; throw-down lines (TDLs) or cones to mark the center line extension.
drills.setup: Split the court lengthwise along the extended center service line, from the center mark to the net and through to the opposite center mark. Both players stand on the forehand diagonal (deuce-to-deuce for two right-handers). The ball must land in the opponent's forehand half: singles sideline to center line, net to baseline, alley out. — [TennisOne Crosscourt Points](https://tennisone.tennisplayer.net/content/Lessons/Drills/cosscourt.points.jy/crosscourt.points.php)
drills.steps: Drop-hit to start; the point goes live after each player has hit one ball ("two hits to start"). Forehands only, so hitting a backhand loses the point. Games to 4, 7 or 11, then repeat on the backhand diagonal. — same source
drills.cues: "Crosscourt = more court, lower net." "Aggressive patience." "Change direction down the line when the time is right." (Rationale from [TalkingTennis, Lizzie Flint, LTA Level 3](https://talkingtennis.net/blog-posts/smart-tennis-why-you-should-hit-a-lot-more-balls-cross-court).) "Height over the middle of the net" is inferred.
drills.progression: Net Gen "Half-Court Battle" (green ball): serve to start, alternating every two serves, forehands only, games to 7. Progressions are to play straight ahead then crosscourt, and then the server may hit forehands only. — [USTA Net Gen Green PDF](https://www.usta.com/content/dam/usta/content-fragments/tennis-service-center/assets/pdfs/Net-Generation-Practice-Plan-Green.pdf). Another option (inferred): allow one down-the-line change of direction on a short ball, as in S6.
drills.regression: cooperative crosscourt rally count first (for example, a 10-ball streak), then compete. Use a green ball or the 60-ft court.
drills.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ESYuG4qObNc — "Tennis Tactics - Where To Aim In Singles" — Top Tennis Training - Pro Tennis Lessons

drills.name: Deep-Ball Rally (past-the-service-line game)
drills.ages: teens 14-18 (high school source); yellow juniors 11-14; adult beginner; adult intermediate (stage mapping inferred)
drills.works: going for too much (control over power), short balls, impatience.
drills.players: 2+ per court; chalk or TDLs.
drills.setup: Players stand on the baseline, either full singles court or one half of the court (straight ahead or crosscourt). The service line is the "deep line".
drills.steps: Players start rallying, and the point is "live" after each player has hit once. "Players must hit balls past the service line, or they lose the point." First to a set number of points wins. Rotate King-of-the-Court style: winners move up one court and losers move down. — [USHSTA Deep-Ball Rally](https://ushsta.org/?p=638)
drills.cues: "Control is a much more important skill… than power" (USHSTA). Height buys depth: Sportplan's "Height for Depth" puts racquets in the net to force height. — [Sportplan Height for Depth](https://www.sportplan.net/drills/Tennis/Rally-Drills/Height-for-Depth-TA00050.jsp). "Twice net height over the net" is inferred.
drills.progression: move the deep line back to ¾ court with chalk; require players to stand inside the baseline (half-volley/short-hop practice); draw a line 1–2 ft behind the baseline; after 5+ minutes, pause for a technique review and then resume. — [USHSTA](https://ushsta.org/?p=638)
drills.regression: cooperative count of balls past the service line; doubles-width court.
drills.video: none found that shows this drill. General alternative (content not confirmed to include it): https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=n-yJ_FhW8os — "Simple Yet Powerful Tennis Singles Drills To Improve Your Game Quickly" — Meike Babel Tennis

drills.name: Up and Down the River (green ball depth game)
drills.works: short, flat balls; inconsistent rallies.
drills.players: two pairs per court; green-dot balls; 25"+ racquets on the 78-ft court; TDLs. — [USTA Net Gen Green PDF](https://www.usta.com/content/dam/usta/content-fragments/tennis-service-center/assets/pdfs/Net-Generation-Practice-Plan-Green.pdf)
drills.setup: Half-courts with boundaries from the middle line to the doubles line. TDLs split each half from the service line to the baseline, creating a deep target zone.
drills.steps: Start points after a serve and return. Both players must let the ball bounce (no volleys). Play to 4 points, then volley cooperatively until the last court finishes. When all courts are done, the winner moves up half a court and the loser moves down. Goal: "Use height, spin, and speed to keep ball deep."
drills.cues: "Height, spin, speed = depth." "Roll it deep."
drills.progression: (1) start points straight ahead with one stroke only; (2) crosscourt with the outside stroke only. (USTA)
drills.regression: cooperative rally into the deep zone; coach feeds the first ball.
drills.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DVRyIjzJ3kI — "Complete Green Ball Class: Rally, Volley, & Point Play" — New Rochelle Racquet Club

drills.name: Sideliner (angle game)
drills.ages: green 9-11 (also useful for yellow juniors 11-14, inferred)
drills.works: hitting everything to the middle; not using the court's width.
drills.players: 4–6 per court; TDLs; green balls.
drills.setup: Half-court crosscourt diagonals split by TDLs, with alleys counting. Two pairs can play at the same time.
drills.steps: All points crosscourt. Start with a serve, then players must hit the outside stroke. Score for winning the point and for forcing the opponent outside the sideline. Use an up-and-down-the-river or champion-of-the-court format. Goal: "Use spin and proper height to move ball off court." — [USTA Net Gen Green PDF](https://www.usta.com/content/dam/usta/content-fragments/tennis-service-center/assets/pdfs/Net-Generation-Practice-Plan-Green.pdf)
drills.cues: "Pull them past the sideline." "Spin + height = angle." (inferred)
drills.progression: (1) every ball must bounce; (2) play the full court. (USTA)
drills.regression: cooperative "mini-tennis angles" inside the service boxes (the Net Gen warm-up "Mini-Tennis Angles" aims to make the ball bounce in the alley).
drills.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ngCFXzmP398 — "Green Ball Class: Serve and Point Play" — New Rochelle Racquet Club

drills.name: Defend and Recover (angle + recovery game)
drills.ages: green 9-11 (Net Gen Green 2 and Green 1); yellow juniors 11-14 (inferred)
drills.works: not recovering after a wide ball; using only one direction.
drills.players: teams of 2–3 on opposite baselines; green balls; cones or poly-spots for the recovery spot.
drills.setup: The feeder stands on the far right side of the baseline, behind the alley. The "angler" starts at the center of the baseline.
drills.steps: The feeder feeds crosscourt to the service box, then recovers to center and split-steps with the left foot on the center mark. The angler moves up, plays a short-court angle, recovers to the baseline, and the point is played out. Rotate after each point, play games to 7 and switch roles. Switch the feed side every other game. Goal: "Move opponent with combinations of shots (angle/down-the-line)." — [USTA Net Gen Green PDF](https://www.usta.com/content/dam/usta/content-fragments/tennis-service-center/assets/pdfs/Net-Generation-Practice-Plan-Green.pdf)
drills.cues: "Hit and recover to the middle of their possible replies." "Split as they hit." (inferred)
drills.progression: (1) the angler plays the first ball down the line and can come in; (2) the angler may choose angle or down the line; (3) an angle must bounce inside the service box, and a down-the-line ball must bounce past the service line. (USTA)
drills.regression: feeder-only (no live point); hand feed.
drills.video: none found that shows this drill.

drills.name: I'm the Boss / Who's the Boss? (change-of-direction rule game)
drills.ages: green 9-11 ("I'm the Boss", Green 1); yellow juniors 11-14 ("Who's the Boss?", Yellow 1 chapter); adaptable to adult intermediate (inferred)
drills.works: going down the line from a defensive position; no plan.
drills.players: teams of 2–3, full-court points; balls.
drills.setup: The serving team members are the "bosses". Serve from the baseline.
drills.steps: The return goes crosscourt to the server, and the point continues crosscourt with outside strokes. Only the boss may change direction, and only with a forehand; returners must hit everything crosscourt. After the first change of direction, play is open. The boss gets a bonus point for changing direction with a forehand and winning the point. On ad-side points (right-handers), the boss may change direction with an inside-in forehand. Games go to 7, then switch servers. Goal: "Wait for short ball or sitter on baseline to change directions." — [USTA Net Gen Green PDF](https://www.usta.com/content/dam/usta/content-fragments/tennis-service-center/assets/pdfs/Net-Generation-Practice-Plan-Green.pdf)
drills.cues: "Crosscourt until the short ball." "Change direction on your forehand, from inside the baseline."
drills.progression: (1) outside stroke only, then any stroke during the rally; (2) the boss gets a negative point for losing a point on a change of direction; (3) both sides can be boss. (USTA)
drills.regression: the coach feeds a designated short ball as the "change" cue.
drills.source: same USTA Green PDF (Yellow version listed in the [Yellow PDF](https://www.usta.com/content/dam/usta/content-fragments/tennis-service-center/assets/pdfs/Net-Generation-Practice-Plan-Yellow.pdf) table of contents)
drills.video: none found that shows this drill.

drills.name: Serve +1 (first-strike game)
drills.ages: green 9-11 ("Team Up and Down the River"); yellow juniors 11-14; teens 14-18; adult intermediate; adult advanced (inferred mapping)
drills.works: serving with no plan for the next ball; passive first shot.
drills.players: teams or pairs; balls; TDLs to mark the 60-ft court sidelines inside the 78-ft court for the green version.
drills.setup: Start the point with a serve and return, and the returner hits into the 60-ft-court sideline.
drills.steps: The server tries to move the opponent around and use the extra space. Play one point, rotate, play to 7 and switch servers. After both sides have served, the winning team moves up a court. Goal: "Use all five controls to move opponent: direction, height, depth, speed and spin." — [USTA Net Gen Green PDF](https://www.usta.com/content/dam/usta/content-fragments/tennis-service-center/assets/pdfs/Net-Generation-Practice-Plan-Green.pdf). Adult/teen version "Four or Less": points count only if won in 4 shots or fewer, played in 5-minute rounds. — [CoachTube 20 Mental Strength Drills](https://coachtube.com/course_lesson/best-tennis-drills-for-coaches/20-mental-strength-tennis-drills/19921068)
drills.cues: "Serve to a spot, then hit your forehand to the open court." "Serve + forehand." (inferred)
drills.progression: (1) the server must hit a forehand on the second ball; (2) use the 78-ft-court sidelines after the return and next ball (USTA). Adults (inferred): name the serve target (T or wide) and the +1 target before each point.
drills.regression: the coach acts as returner with a controlled return to the middle.

- https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2SrthNcsXOI — "How To Master The Serve Plus One" — TPA tennis
- https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GumlybS_rBo — "SERVE + 1 (Tennis Singles Strategy)" — 2MinuteTennis

drills.name: Return the Cannon / Return +1 (returning situation)
drills.ages: green 9-11 ("Return the Cannon"); teens 14-18; adult intermediate; adult advanced (Return +1) (inferred mapping)
drills.works: missed or blocked returns; no plan after the return.
drills.players: two pairs per court on half-courts; TDLs.
drills.setup: Split the court in half with TDLs and play all points crosscourt. The server stands on the service line.
drills.steps: The server tries to hit an unreturnable serve. The server wins the point if the returner can't return crosscourt; the returner wins the point for a crosscourt return. Play to 4, switch roles, then switch sides. — [USTA Net Gen Green PDF](https://www.usta.com/content/dam/usta/content-fragments/tennis-service-center/assets/pdfs/Net-Generation-Practice-Plan-Green.pdf)
drills.cues: "Gentle split step, racquet back early, meet it in front." Against big servers, "return through the center". — [Coachlife Return +1](https://www.coachlife.com/videos/from-split-step-to-return-plus-one)
drills.progression: (1) play out the point on the half-court, with the returner scoring 2 for winning the rally; (2) serve from between the service line and baseline (USTA). Adults: Coachlife Return +1, where serves come from ¾ court and the focus is the return plus the first ball crosscourt or down the line.
drills.regression: the server stands at the baseline with second serves only.
drills.video: none on YouTube found that shows this drill. Coachlife hosts its own video at the page above, which is not a YouTube link. Related USTA video in M2.

drills.name: Approach & Pass (Cautious Approach / Two-on-One Attack)
drills.ages: green 9-11 (Two-on-One Attack); yellow juniors 11-14; teens 14-18; adult intermediate; adult advanced (inferred mapping)
drills.works: approaching off the wrong ball; not closing; no passing-shot options.
drills.players: 2 (Cautious Approach) or 4–5 (Two-on-One Attack); balls.
drills.setup: Cautious Approach uses one player at the baseline (passer) and one who approaches. Two-on-One Attack puts a net player and a baseliner on one side covering the doubles court, with extra players lined up behind the baseliner. The single "champ" on the opposite baseline covers a half-court from the middle to the doubles line.
drills.steps: Cautious Approach: hit the approach, follow it to the net, and the opponent attempts a pass. "Lobs are not allowed". Swap only when the passer hits a successful pass. — [TeachPE](https://www.teachpe.com/?p=2163). Two-on-One Attack: the champ gets one serve and the returner comes to the net, then the point is played out two-on-one. The champ can't lob the first two balls. After each point, the baseliner moves to the net and the net player to the back of the line. After 7 points, a new champ comes over. — [USTA Net Gen Green PDF](https://www.usta.com/content/dam/usta/content-fragments/tennis-service-center/assets/pdfs/Net-Generation-Practice-Plan-Green.pdf)
drills.cues: "Take return early, use hop move to approach net" (USTA). Passers need three passes: "down-the-line, short-angle and topspin lob" (USTA Triples coaching tip).
drills.progression: (1) the champ must lob within the first two shots; (2) the return must be a forehand (USTA). Allow lobs in Cautious Approach (inferred).
drills.regression: the coach feeds the approach ball, and the passer may only pass down the line.

- https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vBnrDu5elS8 — "\"Collect Your Points\" - Excellent Tennis Drill To Practice Passing Shots | \"Drill of the Week\" #052" — Martin Kares Tennistraining

drills.name: King/Queen of the Court (singles)
drills.ages: all stages, from green 9-11 through senior (inferred). Groups of 3–6.
drills.works: match intensity; playing one point at a time; keeping large groups active.
drills.players: 3+ players; one court; balls.
drills.setup: The "king/queen" stands on one side; challengers line up behind the opposite baseline.
drills.steps: A challenger plays a singles point started with a serve or drop hit. If the challenger wins, they replace the king; the loser goes to the back of the queue. The king scores a point for each point won while on the throne, and the coach times rounds. — [Wikipedia: Tennis games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tennis_games). USHSTA uses an elimination King/Queen format for its short crosscourt angle drill. — [USHSTA Short, Crosscourt Angles](https://ushsta.org/?p=372)
drills.cues: "One point at a time." "Start every point with a plan." (inferred)
drills.progression: the challenger must win 2 in a row to take over; serve starts only; the king must win with a forcing shot.
drills.regression: coach feed starts; cooperative "3-ball rally before live".
