drills.name: Plus/Minus (+7 / −7)
drills.ages: teens 14-18; adult intermediate; adult advanced (Sportplan rates it intermediate–advanced); yellow juniors 11-14 (inferred)
drills.works: going for too much / unforced errors; also passive "not-losing" play.
drills.players: 2; full court; balls.
drills.setup: Full singles court, with points started from the hand (drop feed).
drills.steps: +1 for a clear winner or forced error, −1 for any unforced error. First to +7 or −7. — [Sportplan](https://www.sportplan.net/drills/Tennis/Rally-Drills/Plus-and-Minus-Rewards-TA00011.jsp). LTA variant: "+/- Five". — [LTA](https://www.lta.org.uk/play/tennis-tips-and-techniques/how-to-get-more-from-your-tennis-practices/)
drills.cues: "Win the point, don't just avoid losing it" (Sportplan's emphasis). "Make them hit one more" (inferred).
drills.progression: start with a serve; −2 for a double fault or an unforced error inside the first 4 shots.
drills.regression: +/−5; ball must land past the service line (combine with S2).
drills.video: none found that shows this drill.

drills.name: Moonball Challenge ("The Switch – 2" / "beat the pusher" tiebreak)
drills.ages: yellow juniors 11-14; teens 14-18; adult intermediate (league players who lose to pushers) (inferred)
drills.works: frustration or errors against moonballers; impatience.
drills.players: 2; full court.
drills.setup: Full singles court.
drills.steps: Switch – 2: players alternate by point between "ONLY high balls (moonballs)" and "ONLY regular (drive) shots", to 7 points. Small Changes – 4: a regular tiebreak where one player "is allowed to hit only moon balls", to test the ability to "beat the pusher". — [CoachTube 20 Mental Strength Drills](https://coachtube.com/course_lesson/best-tennis-drills-for-coaches/20-mental-strength-tennis-drills/19921068)
drills.cues: "Patience is a weapon." "Take it early or step in and swing high-to-high." (inferred)
drills.progression: the attacking player may only win the point at the net (swinging volley or overhead).
drills.regression: cooperative rally of moonballs landing past the service line (S2 rules).
drills.video: none found that shows this drill.

drills.name: Crazy Feed (heavy-topspin attack/defend)
drills.skill: singles tactics (attacking with height and spin)
drills.works: flat, short attacking balls; not using the court's length and width.
drills.players: teams of 3–4 on opposite baselines; green balls.
drills.setup: Full-court points, two players at a time. One side attacks and the other defends.
drills.steps: The attacker self-feeds a deep ball from behind the baseline, hitting high and deep to the opponent's weakness, then the point is played out. The attacker can't come to the net off the feed. Rotate every point. Attackers score 1 for winning a point and defenders score 2. First to 7, then change teams or order. Goal: "Take advantage of increased length and width by rolling balls deep to corners." — [USTA Net Gen Green PDF](https://www.usta.com/content/dam/usta/content-fragments/tennis-service-center/assets/pdfs/Net-Generation-Practice-Plan-Green.pdf)
drills.cues: "Loop it high and heavy." "Push them behind the baseline." (inferred)
drills.progression: (1) self-feed forehands, then backhands; (2) the defender feeds a high, deep ball with little spin and the attacker hits back with heavy topspin. (USTA)
drills.regression: the coach feeds; points count only if the attacker's ball lands past the service line.
drills.video: none found that shows this drill.

drills.name: Rally Poaching (crosscourt rally with live net players)
drills.ages: teens 14-18 (high school source); adult intermediate; adult advanced (inferred)
drills.works: frozen net players; watching their partner instead of the opponents.
drills.players: 4; balls.
drills.setup: Two baseliners stand crosscourt from each other on one diagonal. Each baseliner's partner starts at the service line in the other half of the court.
drills.steps: Either baseliner drop-hits and the two rally crosscourt. "As soon as the second baseline player hits the ball, the service line players may move to net positions." Baseliners use depth, short balls, spin and speed to force errors. Net players watch their baseline opponents and pick off weak balls. No lobs unless both opponents are at the net. Play 10 points, then baseliners and net players swap and play 10 more. Step 5 variation: start with second serves only, where one fault loses the point and each player serves 4+ points. — [USHSTA Rally Poaching](https://ushsta.org/?p=558)
drills.cues: "Watch their racquet, not your partner." "Pick off the floater."
drills.progression: second-serve start (above). Inferred: allow down-the-line passes at the net player.
drills.regression: net players start already at net; the baseline rally must stay cooperative for 3 balls before going live.
drills.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=S7g7z6RJtKA — "Tennis Drills - Doubles Tactics - Situation Drills - Doubles Poaching Drill #1" — Rope Tennis Education

drills.name: Poaching on an Angle (feed drill)
drills.works: poaching sideways along the net (which loses angle and time); bad poach footwork.
drills.players: one line of players plus the coach; basket.
drills.setup: Player A stands at the net in the deuce court, with others lined up behind the service line. The coach stands on the baseline opposite Player A.
drills.steps: (1) A volleys the coach's first feed back to the coach. (2) The coach plays the ball crosscourt, simulating a return; use a bounce-feed if control is limited. (3) As the ball bounces, A "moves to poach immediately… on an angle… finishing two steps past the center service line". (4) A volleys at the feet of the opposing net player or on a sharp angle away from both. (5) A rotates to the end of the line. — [USHSTA](https://ushsta.org/?p=542)
drills.cues: "Go forward AND across." "Two steps past the center line." "Volley to the feet or the angle."
drills.progression: live returner chooses crosscourt or down the line; poacher fakes or goes.
drills.regression: start at the service line with a mid-court volley before the poach (USHSTA variation).
drills.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iURc4-VGurs — "The CORRECT Poaching Footwork for Doubles Tennis" — Coach Adrian

drills.name: Poach and Play (live poach off the serve)
drills.ages: green 9-11 (Green 1 "Double Trouble"); yellow juniors 11-14 (Yellow 1); adult intermediate (inferred)
drills.works: not moving at the net; late poach timing.
drills.players: 4–6 per court; balls.
drills.setup: One up / one back formation, with the coach as returner at first.
drills.steps: Start the point with a serve, and the return must go crosscourt. The server's partner "moves diagonally forward as serve bounces, and intercepts return as volley". Play out the point. Adjust scoring and rotation to the group size and give equal time on the deuce and ad courts. Goal: "Time poach so that movement to volley is continuous." — [USTA Net Gen Green PDF](https://www.usta.com/content/dam/usta/content-fragments/tennis-service-center/assets/pdfs/Net-Generation-Practice-Plan-Green.pdf); [Yellow PDF](https://www.usta.com/content/dam/usta/content-fragments/tennis-service-center/assets/pdfs/Net-Generation-Practice-Plan-Yellow.pdf)
drills.cues: "Go on the bounce of the serve." "Poach as if you're alone on your side" (USTA tip).
drills.progression: (1) players return serves; (2) the returner's partner poaches off the second-serve return; (3) the returner can hit crosscourt or down the line, and the net player can fake, stay or poach (USTA). Home challenge: "Poach a minimum of one time per game when partner serves."
drills.regression: the coach hand-feeds the "return" to a fixed spot.
drills.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ks63muAmqaI — "How To Poach And Beat Poachers In Doubles - Pro Tennis Strategy" — Patrick Smith Tennis Coaching

drills.name: I-Formation Serving Games
drills.ages: teens 14-18 (high school doubles); adult intermediate; adult advanced (league 3.5–4.5) (inferred; Wikipedia says the formation suits league, club and intermediate players)
drills.works: predictable serving team; returner grooved crosscourt; no communication.
drills.players: 4; balls.
drills.setup: The net player crouches on the center service line about 10 ft from the net (halfway between the net and service line), low enough not to be hit. The server stands near the center mark, directly behind, forming the "I". — [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I-formation_(tennis)); [Krajco/TennisServer](https://www.tennisserver.com/wildcards/wildcards_02_10.html)
drills.steps: The net player gives a hidden hand signal for which side they will cover. The server serves (ideally to the T) and moves to the opposite side. The net player moves at the sound of the serve. Play out the point. (Formation facts are from the sources above.) Inferred game format: the serving team must use the I on every point of the game; the server must call "yes/no" to confirm the signal; the serving team gets a bonus point for a winning poach volley; rotate servers each game.
drills.cues: "Signal, confirm, go on the sound of the serve." "Serve the T." "Server goes opposite." (sourced elements)
drills.progression: mix the I with Australian and standard formations at random (Krajco: most effective "mixed with normal Australian Doubles"); fake signals.
drills.regression: Australian formation first, with the net player on the same side as the server.
drills.video:
- https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KlbA7kajPdE — "How to do I-Formation | Doubles Tactics | Tennis Coaching | Jamie Murray" — Jamie Murray
- https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NtNK9ucoY0E — "Why You Should Be Using \"I\" Formation in Doubles Tennis!" — Coach Adrian

drills.name: All Position Doubles (rotate one spot every point)
drills.ages: yellow juniors 11-14 (Yellow 2); teens 14-18; adult beginner–intermediate; senior (inferred)
drills.works: poor positioning in each of the four roles; one up/one back gaps.
drills.players: 4–6 per court (with 5, one player waits at the net post; with 6, one at each net post).
drills.setup: Players begin in one up / one back formation.
drills.steps: Play doubles points and rotate positions one spot at a time, so everyone plays server, server's partner, returner and returner's partner. Goal: "Move with ball at net, rally crosscourt from baseline." — [USTA Net Gen Yellow PDF](https://www.usta.com/content/dam/usta/content-fragments/tennis-service-center/assets/pdfs/Net-Generation-Practice-Plan-Yellow.pdf). Wikipedia lists the same game (8+ players, first to 10 total points, clockwise rotation to the end of the next line). — [Wikipedia: Tennis games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tennis_games)
drills.cues: "Net player shifts with the ball." "Baseliner rallies crosscourt." Coach freezes play to ask "what should you have done?" (USTA coaching tip).
drills.progression: (1) server and returner must stay back; (2) one side can come in on short balls; (3) no lobs, then lobs allowed. (USTA)
drills.regression: coach-fed starts; mini-tennis "dubz" in the service boxes first.
drills.video:
- https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_3C3dCSaO-0 — "Net Position & Movement in Doubles Tennis (O - N - D)" — The Tennis Tribe
- https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=227hFGyVUe8 — "The Simple Doubles Strategy To Always Be In Right Position - The Pros Know This But Do You?" — Patrick Smith Tennis Coaching

drills.name: Gladiator Dubz (approach on the short ball, Champs vs Challengers)
drills.works: staying back on short balls; one up/one back gap.
drills.players: pairs, up to 4 pairs per court.
drills.setup: The Champs team is on one side. Challenger teams line up behind the opposite baseline. Both teams start one up / one back.
drills.steps: Challengers serve to the Champs and play the point. "After serve, if ball bounces inside service box, baseliner must come to net." Challengers rotate after each point. Challengers keep score, and on reaching 2 points they must shout "Gladiator" before serving. If they shout and win the point, they take the Champs spot (no shout means no takeover). Countdown 3-2-1 when new Champs come over. Goal: "take short ball on the rise and split-step inside service line." — [USTA Net Gen Yellow PDF](https://www.usta.com/content/dam/usta/content-fragments/tennis-service-center/assets/pdfs/Net-Generation-Practice-Plan-Yellow.pdf)
drills.cues: "Short ball = go." "Split inside the service line."
drills.progression: (1) Challengers take over only if the point is won with a volley or overhead; (2) players decide which ball to approach on. (USTA)
drills.regression: the coach feeds a short ball to start every point.
drills.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=g81yoE59R5k — "Doubles - Competitive Drills & Games" — Tennis Coaching Education - Geoffrey Jagdfeld. A search snippet says it includes a "Move Together" drill at about 1:19, but this was not verified.

drills.name: Lob or Lose / Over Your Head (lob offense and defense)
drills.ages: yellow juniors 11-14; teens 14-18; adult intermediate; senior (lob tactics are key for seniors per Walters) (inferred)
drills.works: both-up teams that can't handle lobs; no switch communication; both-back teams with no lob option.
drills.players: 4 (Lob or Lose) or 6 (Over Your Head, 3v3).
drills.setup: One team stands at the baseline and the other at the net.
drills.steps: Lob or Lose: "Team 1 is only allowed to lob," and the objective is to clear the net players. Over Your Head (3v3): the baseline players may hit only lobs, and the net players defend with overheads. — [TeachPE](https://www.teachpe.com/?p=2163). Deep Desperation: the coach lobs over the challengers' heads to start points; winners replace the baseline team. — [Wikipedia: Tennis games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tennis_games)
drills.cues: "Call it: 'Mine' / 'Switch'." "Turn and run, don't backpedal." "Lob over the backhand shoulder."
drills.progression: live point after the first lob; net team scores double for an overhead winner.
drills.regression: coach-fed lobs; overhead off the bounce allowed.
drills.video:
- https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gVQ00JCgjbg — "Doubles Tennis Tactics - Defending Against The Lob" — Jeff Lewis Tennis
- https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3yY-PotN3_k — "LOB JOB - 3 Defensive Lob Tennis Drills!" — TargetSlam
- https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZwDesgpDCCg — "The Lob Strategy 90% of Doubles Players Don't Know" — 2MinuteTennis

drills.name: Doubles Move Up (winners step in)
drills.ages: adult beginner; adult intermediate; yellow juniors 11-14; senior (inferred)
drills.works: teams staying back; partners not moving forward as a unit.
drills.players: 4 (2v2); full court.
drills.setup: Standard doubles court.
drills.steps: "Whichever team wins the point must step up to the service line to start the next point." Three consecutive wins are needed to advance positions. First to win 5 games. — [TeachPE](https://www.teachpe.com/?p=2163)
drills.cues: "Move up together, like a rope ties you." "Split as they hit."
drills.progression: the advanced position is at the net; the opposing team may lob.
drills.regression: coach feeds; no lobs.
drills.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dd7lPpZe3ig — "The #1 Doubles Positioning Mistake (3 Steps To Fix It)" — The Tennis Mentor

drills.name: Miss the Middle / Monkey in the Middle (net interception)
drills.works: net player not covering the middle; baseliners feeding the net player.
drills.players: 4–6 (Miss the Middle), 6+ (Monkey in the Middle).
drills.setup: Miss the Middle: two baseline players per side plus one net player. Monkey in the Middle: triples formation on the doubles court.
drills.steps: Miss the Middle: baseline players try to get the ball past the net player, and a net player who wins three intercepts switches position. — [TeachPE](https://www.teachpe.com/?p=2163). Monkey in the Middle: feed to a baseline player, 1 point per rally won and 2 points if the net player wins it, with continuous play and the next feed to the opposite team. — [Wikipedia: Tennis games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tennis_games)
drills.cues: "Own the middle." "Hands out front, step diagonally."
drills.progression: baseliners may hit down the line; the net player must volley at the opposing net player's feet.
drills.regression: coach feeds to the baseliners at a slower pace.
drills.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aLoDF0-rB_0 — "Excellent Tennis Doubles Tactics Drill For Net Player \"Net Interceptor\" - Drill of the Week #060" — Martin Kares Tennistraining

drills.name: Both Sides Attack / Chip and Charge Dubs (transition to net)
drills.ages: green 9-11 (Green 1); yellow juniors 11-14; teens 14-18; adult intermediate (inferred)
drills.works: returners who stay back; serving team stuck one up / one back.
drills.players: 4–6 per court; 2–3 teams rotating.
drills.setup: Full doubles court, one up / one back.
drills.steps: Both Sides Attack: play doubles points where players must serve-and-volley and must return-and-come-in; the returner can't lob. Goal: "Keep closing on net to end points." Chip and Charge Dubs: one serve only; the returner must slice and come to the net; play out the point. Goal: "Take return on the rise and keep ball low to force opponent to hit up." — [USTA Net Gen Green PDF](https://www.usta.com/content/dam/usta/content-fragments/tennis-service-center/assets/pdfs/Net-Generation-Practice-Plan-Green.pdf)
drills.cues: "Chip low, follow it in." "Split, then close."
drills.progression: Both Sides Attack: (1) topspin approach, then slice approach; (2) the return must go crosscourt. Chip and Charge: (1) singles lines; (2) no lobs. (USTA)
drills.regression: second serves only; coach feeds the return ball.
drills.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ius5Yh2nZjQ — "Top 5 Tennis Drills For Doubles Players - Top Tennis Training" — Top Tennis Training - Pro Tennis Lessons

drills.name: Ping Pong Dubz (alternate-hit doubles)
drills.ages: yellow juniors 11-14 (Yellow 1); teens; adult social groups (inferred)
drills.works: poor recovery and spacing between partners.
drills.players: teams of 2, two teams per court.
drills.setup: Singles points on the full court.
drills.steps: One team serves two points, then the other team serves two, then servers change. Points are played as singles, but partners alternate hitting the ball, ping-pong style. Players may stand anywhere after hitting. On "time", the winning team moves up a court and the losing team moves down, and partners split when they move. Goal: "Create difficult situations for the opponent." — [USTA Net Gen Yellow PDF](https://www.usta.com/content/dam/usta/content-fragments/tennis-service-center/assets/pdfs/Net-Generation-Practice-Plan-Yellow.pdf)
drills.cues: "Hit and get out of the way." "Move them, not you."
drills.progression: (1) no volleys; (2) players must hit one stroke. (USTA)
drills.regression: service-box court with a green or orange ball.
drills.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qSW97ZTENsI — "Tennis Doubles Drill With 2 People [One Up, One Back]" — The Tennis Tribe

drills.name: Canadian Doubles (2 v 1)
drills.ages: all stages; useful for odd numbers in adult and senior groups (inferred)
drills.works: the pair's teamwork and accuracy; the single player's coverage and shot-making.
drills.setup: The pair hits only into the single player's singles court. The single player may hit into the pair's full doubles court. — [Wikipedia: Canadian doubles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canadian_doubles). Used to work on "shot-making, accuracy and teamwork" (search-result excerpt of the same article).
drills.steps: serve normally; play games or first to 11; rotate so each player is the single.
drills.cues: pair: "Squeeze the middle, poach the floater." Single: "Use the doubles alleys."
drills.progression: the pair must stay one up / one back (no two-up).
drills.regression: the pair must let the ball bounce (no volleys).
drills.video: none verified.

drills.name: 16-Second Cure Routine Reps ("routine points")
drills.ages: yellow juniors 11-14; teens 14-18; adult intermediate; adult advanced; senior. Green 9-11 can use a simplified 2-step version (inferred).
drills.works: no between-point routine; carrying errors into the next point; rushing.
drills.players: 2 (or 4 for doubles); a coach or a third player as "routine judge"; optional phone timer.
drills.setup: Normal singles or doubles points with serve.
drills.steps: After every point, the player must visibly complete Loehr's four stages: (1) positive walk, shoulders back; (2) relax and look at the strings; (3) decide the first-shot target while looking across the net; (4) serve or return ritual (bounces, breath). — [Tennis.com/Loehr](https://www.tennis.com/news/articles/playing-with-fire-the-delicate-role-of-emotion-in-pro-and-rec-tennis). Inferred scoring: the judge awards +1 "routine point" for each complete routine, and the routine score is combined with the match score. A player who skips a stage forfeits the next point's first serve.
drills.cues: "Walk tall." "Strings, breathe." "Pick your target." "Ritual, then go." USTA cues: "in control," "trust it," "go for it."
drills.progression: run the routine only after errors and on big points (30-40, deuce) under time pressure (25 s serve clock).
drills.regression: practise the routine during cooperative rally breaks with no score.
drills.video:
- https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=awbsmYIgoVE — "A Key Element to Mental Toughness in Tennis: Routines In-Between Points" — Aubone Tennis
- https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aJFMjRMbM1E — "12 Habits for Mental Tennis Toughness" — Tennis with Coach Alfred

drills.name: Start at 0-30 / 30-40 Down (pressure-score games)
drills.ages: yellow juniors 11-14; teens 14-18; adult intermediate; adult advanced (league players)
drills.works: tightness on big points; serving under pressure.
drills.players: 2 or 4; full court.
drills.setup: Normal court.
drills.steps: "Start every service game 0-30 down." Optionally "Second serves only". — [LTA](https://www.lta.org.uk/play/tennis-tips-and-techniques/how-to-get-more-from-your-tennis-practices/). Inferred extension: start at 30-40 (server facing break point); a set to 4 or 6 games.
drills.cues: "Breathe, routine, first-serve percentage." "Play the score, not the scoreboard."
drills.progression: start at 15-40; the server gets one serve only.
drills.regression: start at 15-30; two serves.
drills.video:
- https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xydqnX8wv5s — "USTA Improve Your Game: Serve and Return Pressure Drill" — United States Tennis Association (USTA)
- https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rpE7QWqcOZI — "How to Train Mental Toughness in Tennis — Joel Myers’ Pressure Method" — Coachlife - Tennis

drills.name: Deuce-Start Sets & Sudden Death at 40
drills.ages: teens 14-18; adult intermediate; adult advanced; yellow juniors 11-14 (inferred)
drills.skill: mental (pressure, focus on the final points of a game)
drills.works: choking on game points; losing focus after reaching 40.
drills.setup: Normal court.
drills.steps: Small Changes – 3: "Each game starts at deuce (40-40)", first to 6 games, best of three sets. Small Changes – 5: "Either player who gets to 40 will have to win the next point; otherwise, he/she will go back to the score of 0." Small Changes – 1: no-ad, games end at 40. — [CoachTube](https://coachtube.com/course_lesson/best-tennis-drills-for-coaches/20-mental-strength-tennis-drills/19921068)
drills.cues: "Same routine on every point." "Big point = high-percentage target."
drills.progression: combine with second-serve-only.
drills.regression: no-ad scoring only.
drills.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=n3Csx1NZTh8 — "Playing Tennis Matches - 5 Tips On Dealing With Pressure" — Feel Tennis Instruction

drills.name: Three in a Row ("Belts" / "Three to Win Three")
drills.works: losing focus after winning or losing a point; streaky concentration.
drills.setup: Singles court with a serve start.
drills.steps: Three to Win Three: a player must win "three points in a row" to win a game, first to three games. — [CoachTube](https://coachtube.com/course_lesson/best-tennis-drills-for-coaches/20-mental-strength-tennis-drills/19921068). Belts (LTA): both players serve twice, and winning three consecutive points earns a "belt". — [LTA](https://www.lta.org.uk/play/tennis-tips-and-techniques/how-to-get-more-from-your-tennis-practices/)
drills.cues: "Next point is the only point." "Reset after every point."
drills.progression: four in a row; the streak must include a serve and a return point.
drills.regression: two in a row.
drills.video: none verified that shows this drill.

drills.name: Hit–Bounce–Hit (concentration rally)
drills.ages: green 9-11; yellow juniors 11-14; adult beginner; senior (inferred)
drills.works: lapses in focus, late preparation, mind wandering.
drills.players: 2; any court size.
drills.setup: Cooperative rally, any zone.
drills.steps: Say "Hit" when the opponent contacts the ball, "Bounce" when it lands on your side and "Hit" when you swing. — [CoachTube](https://coachtube.com/course_lesson/best-tennis-drills-for-coaches/20-mental-strength-tennis-drills/19921068). Inferred scoring: count the longest rally with all calls correct.
drills.cues: "Say it out loud." "Eyes on the ball, quiet mind." (inferred)
drills.progression: competitive points while keeping the calls; add a doubles net player.
drills.regression: service-box mini-tennis with a slower ball.
drills.video: none verified that shows this drill.

drills.name: Error Reset with Cue Words
drills.works: negative self-talk; losing focus after errors.
drills.players: 2+; an index card for each player's cue word.
drills.setup: Each player writes 1–2 personal cue words using the five-step method (identify trigger errors, notice where attention goes, pick a positive phrase, practise, visualize). — [Physical Education Update](https://www.physicaleducationupdate.com/public/860.cfm)
drills.steps: Play points with Plus/Minus scoring (S11). After every unforced error, the player must turn away, say the cue word aloud ("Next time", "Rebound", "Get back"), take one slow breath with a long exhale (see the 4-7-8 note above), and look at the strings before stepping to the line. A negative comment or gesture costs the player the next point. The coach tallies resets.
drills.cues: "Next Time," "Nice Try," "Get Back," "Rebound" (source). USTA: "in control," "trust it."
drills.progression: silent cue (internal) with only a visible gesture; play at 30-40.
drills.regression: reset only after every second error; drill-only (feeds).
drills.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aJFMjRMbM1E — "12 Habits for Mental Tennis Toughness" — Tennis with Coach Alfred

drills.name: One-Serve / Second-Serve-Only Pressure
drills.ages: yellow juniors 11-14; teens 14-18; adult intermediate; adult advanced
drills.works: double faults under pressure; tight second serve.
drills.players: 2 (or 4 for doubles).
drills.setup: Normal serve-and-return points.
drills.steps: 1st Serve Only: "The server is only allowed 1 serve on each point", and a miss gives the point to the opponent. — [TeachPE](https://www.teachpe.com/?p=2163). Attack the Second Serve: play to 7 with second serves only; if the serve lands, the returner must hit an approach and play the point at the net. — [CoachTube](https://coachtube.com/course_lesson/best-tennis-drills-for-coaches/20-mental-strength-tennis-drills/19921068). Small Changes – 6: an ace wins a game and a double fault loses a game. — same
drills.cues: "Spin it in, aim big." "Same routine every serve."
drills.progression: Small Changes – 6 (ace or double-fault game swings).
drills.regression: Small Changes – 7, "The server gets 3 tries" (CoachTube).
drills.video: see M2 (USTA Serve and Return Pressure Drill).

drills.name: Make It Happen (50-ball rally with 3 balls)
drills.ages: green 9-11; yellow juniors 11-14; adult beginner; adult intermediate; senior (inferred)
drills.works: losing focus late in rallies; impatience.
drills.players: 2 baseliners; coach feeds.
drills.setup: Both players on the baseline.
drills.steps: Goal: "a 50-ball rally using no more than 3 balls". Count consecutive hits per feed and add across the three feeds. — [CoachTube](https://coachtube.com/course_lesson/best-tennis-drills-for-coaches/20-mental-strength-tennis-drills/19921068)
drills.cues: "Same height, same target." "Breathe on every hit."
drills.progression: all balls past the service line (S2), or crosscourt only (S1).
drills.regression: 30 balls with 5 feeds, on a shorter court.
drills.video: none verified.

drills.name: Serve It Out (closing-out game)
drills.ages: teens 14-18; adult intermediate; adult advanced; senior (inferred)
drills.works: can't close out leads; playing not to lose.
drills.players: 2 or 4.
drills.setup: Normal court.
drills.steps: Start sets at 5-3 or 5-4 with the leader serving. The leader must hold to win the "set". If broken, play continues as a tiebreak to 7. Rotate who leads. Required behaviors from the sources: 3–4 deep breaths before the game; first serve in with "a little pace off"; "stick with the tactics that helped you get where you are"; optional "reverse the score" self-talk (think 3-5, not 5-3). — [Tennis.com/Fernandez](https://prod.tennis.com/news/articles/mental-tricks-to-closing-out-matches); [Tennis.com 2010](https://www.tennis.com/news/articles/tip-serving-out-the-match)
drills.cues: "First serve in." "Same patterns." "Play to win, not to not-lose." "Breathe 3 times."
drills.progression: the leader starts the game at 0-15; one serve only.
drills.regression: start at 5-2.
drills.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=twMrBvmrUb0 — "Stop choking! Simple Mental Toughness strategies to close out tennis matches" — Meike Babel Tennis

drills.name: Cardio Mini-Tennis Tap-Out (USTA Cardio Tennis)
drills.ages: adult beginner; adult intermediate; senior (at reduced intensity); teens (inferred)
drills.works: low activity in clinics; short-stroke control and footwork.
drills.players: 4 per court (more rotate in); low-compression balls (orange or green per the LTA guidance); music.
drills.setup: Mini-tennis inside the service boxes; extra players queue at the side.
drills.steps: Keep the rally going with short strokes. After an error, the player "taps the doubles alley" before rotating back in. Challenge: sprint to the back fence. — [USTA/Michael Harper](https://www.usta.com/en/home/improve/tips-and-instruction/national/cardio-tennis-with-michael-harper-tap-out-on-the-courts.html). Inferred: 60–90-second rounds with HR checks.
drills.cues: "Small swings, quick feet." "Keep it alive." "Check your heart rate."
drills.progression: sprint to the back fence (USTA); two balls in play (inferred).
drills.regression: walk instead of sprint; red or foam balls for seniors and beginners.
drills.video:
- https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cL61d7s2PYM — "Fun Tennis Drills For Improving Cardio - For Any Age!" — OnCourt OffCourt
- https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3fZEFrRwbPE — "Cardio Tennis Drills" — MGTACADEMY

drills.name: One Ball Live / Two Ball
drills.works: low engagement; reaction to the "live" ball; transition to full-court doubles.
drills.players: 8+ (4 on court, others waiting); 2 balls per start.
drills.setup: The court is split vertically down the center line, with a crosscourt or straight 1v1 on each half. — [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tennis_games)
drills.steps: Both halves start with a simultaneous drop-hit. When one ball dies, "One ball live!" is called and the remaining ball is played across the full doubles court 2v2. The winning team stays and new players replace the losers. First to 10. — [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tennis_games); [TeachPE summary](https://www.teachpe.com/?p=2163)
drills.cues: "Talk: 'one ball!'" "Find your partner's side fast."
drills.progression: serve starts instead of drop-hits.
drills.regression: coach feeds both balls.
drills.video: none verified.

drills.name: Around the World
drills.ages: green 9-11; yellow juniors; adult beginner; adult intermediate; Cardio Tennis groups (inferred)
drills.works: consistency; movement; fun with large groups.
drills.players: 4+; one court.
drills.setup: Two lines behind opposite baselines.
drills.steps: A player feeds, then runs to the opposite baseline line after hitting, so players cross the court after each shot. Three errors eliminates a player. When two remain, they spin racquets for the final (Wikipedia). One variant has the last two players spin 360° after every hit instead of running. — [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tennis_games); [CoachTube Around the World (search excerpt)](https://coachtube.com/course_lesson/best-tennis-drills-for-coaches/around-the-world/19917389)
drills.cues: "Hit and go." "Height and middle."
drills.progression: crosscourt only; volley at the net instead of running.
drills.regression: no elimination (count team rally); walk.
drills.video: none verified.

drills.name: Champs and Chumps
drills.works: competitive intensity in a social setting.
drills.players: 6+; one court.
drills.setup: Full singles court (or doubles with pairs, inferred).
drills.steps: Serve or drop-hit start. Points accumulate in a timed game. Winners move to the "champs" line and losers to the "chumps" line. — [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tennis_games)
drills.cues: "One point, full effort."
drills.progression: champs side must win with a forcing shot.
drills.regression: coach feeds.
drills.video: none verified.

drills.name: Wipe Out
drills.ages: green 9-11; yellow juniors; adult social clinics (inferred)
drills.works: low engagement; handling 2v1 or 3v1 scenarios.
drills.players: variable; singles or doubles court depending on numbers.
drills.setup: Two teams.
drills.steps: Start 1v1 with a drop hit. The loser is replaced, and the winning side adds a player (1v2, 1v3…) until a whole team is on court. — [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tennis_games)
drills.cues: "Talk with your new partner."
drills.progression: serve start; fewer lives.
drills.regression: coach feed.
drills.video: none verified.

drills.name: Team Doubles / Triples / King of the Court Doubles
drills.ages: adult beginner–advanced; senior; yellow juniors; green 9-11 (Net Gen Triples) (inferred)
drills.works: playing all doubles positions; volley and passing play; social mixing.
drills.players: 6+ per court.
drills.setup: Team Doubles: full doubles court, first to 7 or 11, clockwise rotation after each point through the serving and returning positions. Triples: doubles court with 3v3, the coach or a sitting-out player feeds, first to 10, clockwise rotation. King of the Court Doubles: the winning team replaces the "kings". — [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tennis_games). Net Gen Triples (green): three per side (one at the net, two on the baseline), extra players behind the baseline, coach feeds the deep player first, only the net player may volley, rotate one spot per point. Progressions: switch to two up/one back to encourage lobs; use doubles or singles boundaries. — [USTA Net Gen Green PDF](https://www.usta.com/content/dam/usta/content-fragments/tennis-service-center/assets/pdfs/Net-Generation-Practice-Plan-Green.pdf)
drills.steps: as above.
drills.cues: "Close the net and angle volleys"; passers use "down-the-line, short-angle and topspin lob" (USTA).
drills.progression: as in the USTA progressions above.
drills.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=T5I-GL_7qJk — "RSPA Quick Tips -- Cardio Tennis Volley Drill" — Racquet Sports Professionals Association
drills.regression: coach feeds every ball.

drills.name: Up and Down the River (adult social round robin)
drills.works: social mixing; competitive matching by level.
drills.players: multiple courts, 4 per court.
drills.setup: Courts ranked from top court to bottom court.
drills.steps: Timed rounds (10–15 min) or tiebreak format. Winners move up a court and losers move down, and partners split so players face new partners and opponents. — [VisitMO event listing](https://www.visitmo.com/events/up-and-down-the-river-doubles). The same up/down rule appears in Net Gen junior games (S3, D11).
drills.cues: "Introduce yourself to your new partner." "Play the score."
drills.progression: start each round at 30-all.
drills.regression: coach-fed points; no-ad.
drills.video: none verified.

drills.name: Cardio Tennis Session Template (LTA/USTA format)
drills.ages: adult beginner–intermediate; teens (the LTA school version targets teenage girls); senior (lower intensity) (inferred)
drills.works: fitness plus tennis in one session; keeping 10–12 players active.
drills.players: 10–12 per court (minimum 5); low-compression balls; HR monitors or manual checks; music; cones and ladders for sideline stations. — [LTA Cardio Tennis PDF](https://lta.org.uk/4912a5/siteassets/roles/teachers/file/cardio-tennis/cardio-tennis-introduction.pdf)
drills.setup: Hitting stations on court plus sideline fitness stations, with continuous rotation.
drills.steps: Warm Up, then theme and key shots, then Drills (rotating hitting and sideline stations), then Conditioned Points, then Cool Down, keeping HR at 65–85% of max with regular checks. Themes: Baseline Warrior, Get Into Win, Got It Covered, Serve and Return, Working Together, Putting it All Together. — LTA PDF. Insert G1–G6 as the drills and conditioned points.
drills.cues: "Check your zone." "Everyone moving, all the time."
drills.progression: shorter rest, two-ball feeds.
drills.regression: longer sideline stations; walking rotations; red balls.
drills.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IWPFjdt2gCY — "Cardio Tennis - Games - Charge" — LTA

faults.name: Arming the ball / no unit turn
faults.looks: The body stays square to the net and the arm generates the stroke; shoulders barely rotate; legs and hips are static. The ball "floats back like a beach ball", with little pace or penetration and inconsistent direction. — [PlayYourCourt 2026](https://www.playyourcourt.com/news/why-your-forehand-has-no-power-and-how-to-fix-it-for-good/)
faults.cause: Skipping the body's biggest force producers. Late or no coil, where the player only "moves the racquet back". — [PlayYourCourt 2026](https://www.playyourcourt.com/news/why-your-forehand-has-no-power-and-how-to-fix-it-for-good/); [USTA, Gladstone 2018](https://www.usta.com/en/home/improve/tips-and-instruction/national/improve-your-tennis-game--get-your-forehand-flowing.html)
faults.cues:
- "Unit turn": hips and upper body rotate as one unit. — [USTA](https://www.usta.com/en/home/improve/tips-and-instruction/national/improve-your-tennis-game--get-your-forehand-flowing.html)
- Pivot the outside foot on the split step; the non-dominant hand points at the incoming ball; strings face the side fence; "arm is the messenger, not the engine". — [PlayYourCourt 2026](https://www.playyourcourt.com/news/why-your-forehand-has-no-power-and-how-to-fix-it-for-good/)
- Start the turn before or as the ball bounces. — [PlayYourCourt (Baxter 2019)](https://www.playyourcourt.com/news/forehand-killer-part-2/)
faults.drills: D33 Unit-Turn Catch then Hit; shadow swings (D33 regression); D2
faults.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MWVBsnwv7dM — "How to Fix the Most Common Forehand Power Mistake (Step-by-Step)" — Essential Tennis - Lessons and Instruction for Passionate Players; https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=du5uOZfKArw — "Why The Split Step & Unit Turn Are CRUCIAL For Your Tennis Game" — Gaby Paz - Vantage Tennis

faults.name: Late contact
faults.looks: The ball is struck beside or behind the body rather than in front. The result is a loss of control and power. — [Tennis Uni](https://tennis-uni.com/en/tennis-forehand/); [PlayYourCourt 2026](https://www.playyourcourt.com/news/why-your-forehand-has-no-power-and-how-to-fix-it-for-good/)
faults.cause: Hitting too close to the body and late preparation (Tennis Uni). Rushed "spastic late motion" with no separated takeback (Baxter). On one-handers, an elbow lead (see F9).
faults.cues:
- "Strike ball further forward"; contact in front with the racket face parallel to the net. — [Tennis Uni](https://tennis-uni.com/en/tennis-forehand/)
- Ball "a little bit in front of you" (backhand). — [USTA basics, Pettit 2017](https://www.usta.com/en/home/improve/tips-and-instruction/national/learning-the-basics--backhand.html)
- Prepare before the bounce. — [PlayYourCourt 2019](https://www.playyourcourt.com/news/forehand-killer-part-2/)
faults.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NsRlIN9See4 — "LATE Forehand Fix - tennis lesson" — Essential Tennis - Lessons and Instruction for Passionate Players; https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=c5SqRb9i020 — "Forehand Contact Point Correction | 3.5 NTRP Tennis Lesson" — Intuitive Tennis

faults.name: Hitting off the back foot / no weight transfer
faults.looks: Flat feet, standing tall, no load on the outside leg, weight staying centred or falling backward. The ball lands short with weak pace. — [PlayYourCourt 2026](https://www.playyourcourt.com/news/why-your-forehand-has-no-power-and-how-to-fix-it-for-good/)
faults.cause: Inadequate weight transfer. — [Tennis Uni](https://tennis-uni.com/en/tennis-forehand/). Poor depth reading of the incoming ball [A].
faults.cues: "Shift weight to front foot during forward swing" (Tennis Uni). Knees bent with weight on the balls of the feet, load the outside leg during the turn, "push the ground away with your back foot", and use a semi-open or open stance (PlayYourCourt 2026).
faults.drills: D4 Forward and Backward; D14 Call the Bounce; D34 Drop-Hit Freeze-Finish
faults.video: none verified that is specific to this fault. See the general https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BuBaV8zjo78 — "7 Tennis Forehand Mistakes EVERY Player Makes (And How to Fix Them)" — Patrik Broddfelt (content not confirmed).

faults.name: Wristy flip (and its opposite, the locked death-grip)
faults.looks: A wrist snap or flick at contact gives unpredictable results. On slice, a loose wrist gives a floater that invites attack. — [Sportplan Apr 2026](https://www.sportplan.net/drills/Tennis/trends/slice-backhand-tactical-weapon-2025-04.jsp). The opposite fault is a death grip with a rigid wrist, which slows racquet speed and loses the whip. — [PlayYourCourt 2026](https://www.playyourcourt.com/news/why-your-forehand-has-no-power-and-how-to-fix-it-for-good/)
faults.cause: Independent hand action replacing body rotation (flip); excess tension (lock).
faults.cues:
- Shadow swings holding the racquet throat with the non-hitting hand until the forward swing begins, to reinforce a one-unit turn; firm wrist through slice contact. — [Sportplan](https://www.sportplan.net/drills/Tennis/trends/slice-backhand-tactical-weapon-2025-04.jsp)
- Grip pressure "about a 3" out of 10. — [USTA basics](https://www.usta.com/en/home/improve/tips-and-instruction/national/learning-the-basics--backhand.html)
- Relaxed grip with controlled lag. — [PlayYourCourt 2026](https://www.playyourcourt.com/news/why-your-forehand-has-no-power-and-how-to-fix-it-for-good/)
faults.drills: D33 (non-hitting hand on the throat during the turn), D29 (slice firm wrist), D34
faults.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8kDLHFtVT5c — "5 Drills To Improve Your Forehand FAST I TENNIS LESSON" — Tennis Evolution. Its description mentions wrist control.

faults.name: No follow-through / abbreviated finish
faults.looks: A sudden stop at contact; a "jab"; jerky deceleration; leaning away. Energy doesn't transfer, so the ball is weak and short. — [PlayYourCourt 2026](https://www.playyourcourt.com/news/why-your-forehand-has-no-power-and-how-to-fix-it-for-good/)
faults.cause: Braking the racquet before or right after impact, often from fear of hitting long [A].
faults.cues:
- Finish over the non-dominant shoulder; "swing as if hitting three stacked balls". — [PlayYourCourt 2026](https://www.playyourcourt.com/news/why-your-forehand-has-no-power-and-how-to-fix-it-for-good/)
- Follow-through over the left shoulder with the upper body rotating (right-hander). — [Tennis Uni](https://tennis-uni.com/en/tennis-forehand/)
- Two-hander: finish with the non-dominant elbow pointing across the net and "airing the armpits". — [USTA](https://www.usta.com/en/home/improve/tips-and-instruction/national/improve-your-tennis-game--the-driving-force-in-your-two-handed-b.html)
- "Strong follow-through". — [Tennis Companion](https://tenniscompanion.org/12-essential-tennis-drills-for-beginners-and-kids/)
faults.drills: D13 Net-Clearance Crosscourt; D34 freeze-finish; D1
faults.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BuBaV8zjo78 — "7 Tennis Forehand Mistakes EVERY Player Makes (And How to Fix Them)" — Patrik Broddfelt

faults.name: Ball goes long (missing low-to-high / too much pace for level)
faults.looks: Balls sail past the baseline. — [USTA forehand basics](https://www.usta.com/en/home/improve/tips-and-instruction/national/learning-the-basics--forehand.html), from search summary: "The harder you swing, the farther the ball is going to go."
faults.cause: A flat swing path without topspin brush, or swing speed beyond the player's control. USTA says beginners' "number 1 priority" is keeping the ball on court. — [USTA forehand basics](https://www.usta.com/en/home/improve/tips-and-instruction/national/learning-the-basics--forehand.html)
faults.cues:
- Brush low to high, "6 o'clock to 12 o'clock". — [USTA backhand basics](https://www.usta.com/en/home/improve/tips-and-instruction/national/learning-the-basics--backhand.html)
- "Small swing, short distance; bigger swing, greater distance". — [USTA Tennis 101 for Adults](https://www.usta.com/content/dam/usta/content-fragments/tennis-service-center/assets/pdfs/USTA-Tennis-101-for-Adults.pdf)
- "Use height, spin, and speed to keep ball deep". — [USTA Green plans](https://www.usta.com/content/dam/usta/content-fragments/tennis-service-center/assets/pdfs/Net-Generation-Practice-Plan-Green.pdf)
faults.drills: D9 Tempo (spin for consistency), D11 Up and Down the River, D12 Height for Depth, D16 Crazy Feed (heavy topspin)
faults.video: none verified that is specific to topspin-for-control

faults.name: Poor spacing / crowding the ball
faults.looks: Crowded position; contact level with or behind the hips; no room to extend. The contact is off-centre and the shot feels like it has "no power". — [PlayYourCourt 2026](https://www.playyourcourt.com/news/why-your-forehand-has-no-power-and-how-to-fix-it-for-good/)
faults.cause: Incorrect footwork or positioning, with the feet adjusted too late. — [Tennis Uni](https://tennis-uni.com/en/tennis-forehand/)
faults.cues: Contact slightly in front of the front hip at waist-to-chest height, with a comfortably extended arm and about 12-18 in of space (PlayYourCourt 2026). "Adjust feet early" (Tennis Uni).
faults.drills: D34 Drop-Hit Freeze; D3 Side-to-Side; D4 Forward/Backward
faults.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8kDLHFtVT5c — "5 Drills To Improve Your Forehand FAST I TENNIS LESSON" — Tennis Evolution. Its search description mentions "proper spacing, extension".

faults.name: Two-handed backhand: dominant-arm takeover
faults.looks: For right-handers, the stronger right arm dominates, so the player "pull[s] the racquet instead of driving it" and the shot is weakened. — [Tennis.com 2010](https://tennis.com/news/articles/tip-remember-the-other-hand)
faults.cause: The bottom (dominant) hand powers the swing and the top hand is passive.
faults.cues: "A left-handed forehand with the right hand along for the ride" ([Tennis.com](https://tennis.com/news/articles/tip-remember-the-other-hand)). Top hand = "driver", bottom hand = "passenger"; finish with the non-dominant elbow pointing across the net ([USTA, Davies 2018](https://www.usta.com/en/home/improve/tips-and-instruction/national/improve-your-tennis-game--the-driving-force-in-your-two-handed-b.html)).
faults.drills: D31 non-dominant-hand forehands; D32 OK-sign grip
faults.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xn-Bdd74F5c — "Top 3 Drills For Two Handed Backhand In Tennis - Transform Your Tennis Backhand" — Top Tennis Training - Pro Tennis Lessons; https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=M0aIRntFvcE — "How to immediately improve your two handed tennis backhand | + Drills!" — Meike Babel Tennis

faults.name: One-handed backhand: elbow leading
faults.looks: The arm and elbow move ahead of the racquet. A bent elbow needs time to straighten; if it doesn't, contact is late and control is lost. — [Tennisplayer forum: Elbow lead on 1HB](https://forum.tennisplayer.net/forum/tennisplayer/1046-elbow-lead-on-1hb); [TennisOne](https://tennisone.tennisplayer.net/content/Theories/theories.Yandell.p.5.php). These come from search summaries, and the forum is a lower-tier source.
faults.cause: Not turning, or turning very late. The shoulders should reach 90 degrees to the net before the arm moves.
faults.cues: A straight arm at the bottom of the backswing before the ball bounces; a straight arm and locked wrist at contact; minimal elbow bend on the takeback; the upper arm close to the chest at the start of the forward swing. — [TennisOne – Murphy](https://tennisone.tennisplayer.net/content/Lessons/murphy/back/prepback2.php)
faults.drills: D35 One-Hander Straight-Arm Feed; D33-style catch turn on the backhand side [A]
faults.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nuRh27czEy8 — "3 DEADLIEST ONE-HANDED Backhand Mistakes (And How to Fix Them!)" — VS Tennis; https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bdU0SFj7ToE — "You NEED to FIX Your One-Handed Backhand! Drills for Power and Control + PRO Tips and Technique!" — Chris Lewit; https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zniT2qyiN4Q — "Do this One Handed Backhand drill to Fix your Rotation." — Total Tennis Domination

faults.name: Wrong grip for the intended spin
faults.looks:
- Eastern forehand: hard to handle very high balls. — [PlayYourCourt – Eastern vs Western](https://www.playyourcourt.com/news/eastern-vs-western-grip-tennis/?amp=1)
- Eastern gives flat, hard trajectories; Western gives topspin but less power and is difficult to execute. — [Tennis Uni](https://tennis-uni.com/en/tennis-forehand/)
- On slice, an Eastern backhand grip "produces flat, floating results". — [Sportplan 2026](https://www.sportplan.net/drills/Tennis/trends/slice-backhand-tactical-weapon-2025-04.jsp)
faults.cause: The grip doesn't match the spin or contact height the player needs.
faults.cues: Semi-western for most juniors, with Eastern as a stepping stone ([PlayYourCourt](https://www.playyourcourt.com/news/eastern-vs-western-grip-tennis/?amp=1)). Eastern "shake hands" grip for adult beginners ([USTA basics](https://www.usta.com/en/home/improve/tips-and-instruction/national/learning-the-basics--forehand.html)). Continental for slice ([Sportplan](https://www.sportplan.net/drills/Tennis/trends/slice-backhand-tactical-weapon-2025-04.jsp)).
faults.drills: D16 Crazy Feed and D9 Tempo (topspin), D29 (slice grip)
faults.video: none verified that is specific to grip

faults.name: Flat feet / no (or mistimed) split step
faults.looks: Without a split step, the feet are flat and the player is "always a step behind". Heel-down players are flat-footed at the opponent's contact. — [Tennis Nation footwork guide](https://www.tennisnation.com/blog/technique/ultimate-tennis-footwork-guide/); [MyTennisHQ split-step guide](https://mytennishq.com/tennis-split-step-a-comprehensive-guide-with-videos/). Both come from search summaries.
faults.cause: Splitting at contact, which is too late at higher levels, or not at all.
faults.cues: Start the split early so you are in the air as the ball leaves the opponent's racquet. Land wider than shoulder width, knees bent, weight equal on both feet. (Same sources.)
faults.drills: D14 Call the Bounce; D3 Side-to-Side; D15 X Drill; D28 Defend and Recover (split step with the left foot on the centre mark)
faults.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XR83yXLla8w — "Tennis Split Step Timing, Execution And Drills" — Feel Tennis Instruction; https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=J1UhPl1UrYs — "How To Master The Split Step in 5 Minutes: Beginner to Pro" — Top Tennis Training - Pro Tennis Lessons; https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AYe0uBf_Zis — "How to Master the Tennis Split Step | Timing, Footwork & Movement with Vin Baccelli" — Coachlife - Tennis

faults.name: Opening up too early
faults.looks: The chest and shoulders rotate to face the net before the forward swing has started. It is named as a common flaw on both the serve and the forehand. — [PlayYourCourt, search summary](https://www.playyourcourt.com/news/?p=9454). Ball result: no sourced description [A].
faults.cause: An incomplete unit turn. — [Tennis Uni](https://tennis-uni.com/en/tennis-forehand/)
faults.cues: "Keep shoulders closed longer during swing" (Tennis Uni). Separate the stroke into turn/takeback, then drop-and-swing ([PlayYourCourt 2019](https://www.playyourcourt.com/news/forehand-killer-part-2/)).
faults.drills: D33 Unit-Turn Catch; D17 Figure 8. The down-the-line hitter must stay turned longer [A].
faults.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BuBaV8zjo78 — "7 Tennis Forehand Mistakes EVERY Player Makes (And How to Fix Them)" — Patrik Broddfelt

faults.name: Floating slice (bonus)
faults.looks: A high, slow slice that sits up for the opponent; or no backspin at all. — [Sportplan 2026](https://www.sportplan.net/drills/Tennis/trends/slice-backhand-tactical-weapon-2025-04.jsp)
faults.cause: A face opened too much plus a high-to-low swing with no forward extension (floater). A face perpendicular to the ground at contact (no spin). An Eastern backhand grip.
faults.cues: Push forward toward the target after contact, not just chop down; face 10-15 degrees open; continental grip; firm wrist; use the ball-on-strings tilt check.
faults.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zw-1nzGwhrA — "The Backhand Slice Explained: Stop Floating the Ball (Fix This Mistake!)" — Coachlife - Tennis

faults.name: Disjointed vs rushed one-motion forehand (bonus)
faults.looks: Either a disjointed stroke that breaks tempo, or an overcorrection into "one continuous motion" with no hold after the unit turn. The rushed version loses control because joint positions can't be held. — [PlayYourCourt, Scott Baxter, June 20 2019](https://www.playyourcourt.com/news/forehand-killer-part-2/)
faults.cause: Poor timing of preparation relative to the bounce.
faults.cues: Finish the unit turn and racquet preparation before the ball bounces; a "slight pause" at the top; two segments, turn/takeback then drop-and-swing.
faults.video: none verified that is specific to this fault

faults.name: Frying-pan / forehand grip on the serve
faults.looks: The palm sits behind the handle and the strings face the target from the start. Serves are flat and pushed with little spin; it is hard to get power or spin, and second serves "pat".
faults.cause: Learning the serve with the forehand grip; muscle memory persists after switching ([Feel Tennis](https://www.feeltennis.net/correcting-the-waiters-serve/)).
faults.cues: "Continental: shake hands with the edge", "Racket parallel to your body" ([Feel Tennis beginner](https://www.feeltennis.net/serve-lesson-for-beginners/)), "Expect 3-6 months to feel comfortable".
faults.drills: S10 Continental Edge Tap → S11 Swing on Edge → S13 Serve With the Edge → S14 Slice to Ad.
faults.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kcxwqOJZV9g — "How To Switch From Forehand To Continental Grip On The Serve | Tennis Serve Lesson" — Performance-Plus Tennis

faults.name: Waiter's tray (racquet face open in the backswing / trophy)
faults.looks: In the backswing the strings face the sky like a waiter carrying a tray. The ball is pushed, short and spinless; there is little power, and the player often faces the net early.
faults.cause: The four Feel Tennis causes above, especially facing the court too early and forehand-grip memory.
faults.cues: "Lead with the edge", "Stay sideways longer", "Strings at the last moment" ("change your mind late").
faults.drills: S11, S13 (edge serve, then fence serve), S14, S3 (Quarterback "tip points back").
faults.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bc3VkS8tAxY — "Transform Your Tennis Serve Technique - Fix The Waiter's Tray with these simple steps" — Meike Babel Tennis. Also https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=evv2WkBOAvE — "Tennis SERVE -  Correcting The Waiter's Tray" — Feel Tennis Instruction; https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=O9zc6hXfPR8 — "How To Fix Your Tennis Waiter Tray Serve In Tennis (With Just 2 Fingers)" — Total Tennis Domination; https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EMJKMuUxTQU — "Fix The Waiter's Tray Tennis Serve With One Simple Trick" — Meike Babel Tennis

faults.name: Inconsistent toss
faults.looks: The toss lands in a different place each time and the player chases it. Results vary between net, long and mishits; often there are many catch-and-retoss moments.
faults.cause: Releasing the ball low or flicking the wrist; the toss arm bending or dropping early; the toss height changing *(cause list is coaching consensus from the toss videos below, not a federation text)*.
faults.cues: "Place the toss in the same location every time" ([Human Kinetics](https://us.humankinetics.com/blogs/excerpt/thrust-launch-serve-technique)), "Keep lifting", *(added)* "Straight arm, release high".
faults.drills: S9 Toss Target, S5 Two-Ball Toss-and-Throw, S7 Serve in Two Parts.
faults.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UJ3xNfw7G3Y — "Tame Your Serve Toss With The "Keep Lifting" Drill" — Feel Tennis Instruction. Also https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nmDO2mdNyZU — "Tennis Serve Toss Tips and Drills" — Tom Avery Tennis - CTW Academy; https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XO5W7vCf3hc — "Improve your tennis serve with these 3 drills for a consistent ball toss" — Meike Babel Tennis; https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HsnXfnsy3C8 — "5 Tips To Fix Your Serve Toss..." — Total Tennis Domination; https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Ta8J7tHZXkw — "Tennis Serve Toss and Follow-Through Drills With Harsh Mankad " — Tenicity

faults.name: Toss too far behind or too far in front (or too far left/right)
faults.looks: Too far behind: the back arches, the ball goes long or is shanked, and it puts strain on the back. Too far in front: the player falls forward, the ball is hit down into the net, and it is hard to hit up. *(Ball results are coaching consensus; no federation text was found.)*
faults.cause: A toss arm path that is not aligned with the target (for example swinging across the body), or releasing too early or late. For kick serves, players often confuse the kick toss with the flat or slice toss.
faults.cues: *(added)* "Toss in front and to the hitting side for flat or slice", "Let it drop: it should land just inside the baseline, in front of the front foot", "For kick, toss more over the head".
faults.drills: S9 Toss Target (with a target placed per serve type), S7, S16 (kick toss).
faults.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iYpl8PbxAWc — "Fix Your Toss With This Simple Tip (Tennis Serve Technique)" — 2MinuteTennis. Also https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TkAj6MmwxHw — "Tennis Kick Serve - Kick Serve Step 1 - Toss" — Fuzzy Yellow Balls

faults.name: Tossing arm drops early / no "pointing" tossing arm
faults.looks: The tossing arm falls before the hitting arm rises. The shoulders open early, the player loses height and power, and the ball often goes into the net.
faults.cause: Rushing; not coordinating the two arms ("toss with one, throw with the other").
faults.cues: "Keep the tossing arm up longer", "Toss arm ahead of hitting arm" (USTA Drag Serve "Mission").
faults.drills: S5, S17 Drag Serve, S3 Quarterback (front arm parallel).
faults.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IHcHQQzDKLU — "How To Keep Your Tossing Arm Up Longer (Tennis Serve Drill)" — 2MinuteTennis. Also https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=G5S6lMBwzXU — "Tossing Arm Serve Drill To Improve Your Technique" — Tennis Evolution

faults.name: No knee bend / no leg drive
faults.looks: Straight legs and all arm. There is little pace, and the shoulder and elbow carry the load.
faults.cause: No load phase; feet static; often fear of losing balance.
faults.cues: "Bend the knees", "Launch up and out", "Drive up with legs as you throw". Emory: more knee flexion reduces shoulder and elbow torque ([Emory](https://www.emoryhealthcare.org/centers-programs/sports-medicine-center/tennis-medicine-program/wellness)).
faults.drills: S18 Thrust Launch, O4 Three Ball Throw, S2 Three-Level Throw, S8 Three-Level Serve.
faults.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_XO7IEHDkl0 — "Serve- Hip Flexor Snap Towel Drill" — Patrick Dougherty *(related; hip action)*; https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=upcyHOegDLI — "The Tennis Serve Simplified - 6 Steps To An Advanced Serve" — PlayYourCourt.com

faults.name: Dropping the racquet head early / no "racquet drop"
faults.looks: The racquet falls behind the back before the toss peaks (early drop), or never drops at all (a stiff, pushing arm). Rhythm is off, racquet-head speed is low, and contact is often late or low.
faults.cause: Swinging before the toss reaches its peak; a tense arm.
faults.cues: "Toss first; arm moves at the peak", "Relaxed arm", "Palm down like a throw" (USTA Drag Serve).
faults.drills: S17 Drag Serve, S7 Serve in Two Parts, S3 Quarterback.
faults.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uYguiaDTgH8 — "Tennis Serve: Racquet Drop (HUGE Mistake to Avoid & Drills To-Do)" — Tennis Evolution. Also https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=S7t0gV1Hu10 — "Tennis Serve Tip: Improve Your Racket Drop" — Online Tennis Instruction

faults.name: Pushing the ball / no pronation
faults.looks: The strings meet the ball flat from early on and the arm "pushes" toward the target. Serves are slow and short, there is no snap, and the finish lands on the wrong side.
faults.cause: Not trusting pronation; a forehand grip (F1); facing the net too early ([Feel Tennis](https://www.feeltennis.net/correcting-the-waiters-serve/)).
faults.cues: "Lead with edge, pronate", "Finish on your dominant side first (ground smack), then across", "Accelerate naturally and pronate your forearm" ([Feel Tennis pronation](https://www.feeltennis.net/serve-pronation/)).
faults.drills: S12 Ground-Smack Pronation, S14, S6 Kneeling Serve, S1/S3 throwing.
faults.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=urCqh8-W5EM — "TENNIS SERVE LESSON: How To Master Pronation On Your Serve (Pronation Drills)" — Tennis Evolution. Also https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CJlW6tOT4Ho — "5 Drills For EASY Serve Pronation! Tennis Serve Lesson" — Performance-Plus Tennis

faults.name: Landing on the wrong foot / falling sideways
faults.looks: The player lands on the back foot or falls toward the side fence. The serve sprays sideways, recovery is slow, and the server is out of position for the return.
faults.cause: The toss is too far to the side or behind (F4); no forward weight transfer; legs drive sideways instead of up and in.
faults.cues: "Land on lead foot" ([Human Kinetics](https://us.humankinetics.com/blogs/excerpt/thrust-launch-serve-technique)), *(added)* "Toss into the court", "Balance and hold the finish for 2 seconds".
faults.drills: S18, S9 (toss into the court), S5 (balance in the two-ball throw).
faults.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=n274VekfB1U — "Serve Drill: Toss and Balance | Tennis" — SIKANA English

faults.name: Foot faults
faults.looks: Stepping on or over the baseline before contact, walking or running into the serve, or crossing the centre-mark or sideline extension. It is a fault and gets called in officiated play.
faults.cause: A front foot that slides or creeps during the toss or leg drive; standing too close to the line; the back foot stepping through early (pinpoint stance).
faults.cues: Rule 18 basics (no walking or running; don't touch the baseline, the sideline extension or the centre-mark extension), *(added)* "Start a ball-width behind the line", "Front foot stays planted until contact".
faults.drills: *(added)* S18 done with a throw-down line placed just behind the baseline; S15 with a "foot-fault = lost zone" rule.
faults.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vBnjtbNGQno — "How To Stop Foot Faulting on the Serve | Tennis Technique" — Intuitive Tennis

faults.name: Double faults under pressure
faults.looks: Second serves into the net or long at key scores; the player slows the arm down ("guides" it).
faults.cause: No reliable spin second serve; no routine; decelerating.
faults.cues: "Same ritual every serve", "Use spin to add control" (USTA Serve Index); "Racquet-head speed, hit up and out" (Three-Level Serve).
faults.drills: S15 Serve Index (with ritual), S19 Team Defender (one serve), S8, S16 (kick, 13+), S14 (slice).
faults.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HCrpSKYvLoo — "Kick Serve Drills THAT WORK!!! | INSANE KICK" — Supreme Tennis. Also https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=x6toBHiG8Z0 — "Kick Serve Secret (Revealed) | TENNIS SERVE LESSON" — Tennis Evolution

faults.name: Returner too passive / standing still
faults.looks: No split-step and flat feet. Late, weak or short returns; the returner gets aced or jammed.
faults.cause: Split-step mistimed (too early or late) or missing; standing too deep.
faults.cues: "Split-step as the server makes contact", *(added)* "Land your split as you read the serve"; "Return and split-step with recovery" (USTA First Four); "Take return early" (USTA Two-on-One).
faults.drills: R2 First Four, R3 Serve Pyramids, R5 Up and Down the River, R6 Step Up, R7 Two-on-One.
faults.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Dl_vM5TnDY4 — "Tennis Lesson - Return of Serve Video #3 - Ready Hop/Split Step - Insight Tennis" — Insight Tennis. Also https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XR83yXLla8w — "Tennis Split Step Timing, Execution And Drills" — Feel Tennis Instruction; https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Z8CNYjf-Uyk — "THE SPLIT STEP: ESSENTIAL DRILLS FOR ADVANCED CONDITIONING AND MOVEMENT I TENNIS ON DEMAND" — tennisondemand

faults.name: Big backswing on the return
faults.looks: A full groundstroke backswing against a fast serve. The return is late, framed or sprayed wide.
faults.cause: Treating the return like a rally ball; late unit turn.
faults.cues: "Compact backswing" (USTA), *(added)* "Shoulder turn, not arm swing", "Block and use the server's pace".
faults.drills: R4 Return the Cannon, R6 Pinch + Step Up.
faults.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3TxZTZEEg44 — "TENNIS RETURN | Block Your Return Of Serve With This Grip" — Tennis Evolution. Also https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_pS0otk2560 — "Top 3 Drills For Perfect Return of Serve in Tennis" — Top Tennis Training - Pro Tennis Lessons

faults.name: Overhead: letting the ball drop too low
faults.looks: Contact at head height or below. The smash goes into the net or becomes a weak push, and is often framed.
faults.cause: Late movement back; not getting behind the ball; standing still.
faults.cues: *(added)* "Turn and move early", "Hit it at full reach, like a serve", "Get behind the ball"; *(added)* on very high lobs, let it bounce.
faults.drills: O3 Smash and Touch the Net, O5 Scissor Kick, O1, O4.
faults.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NOMh7eK5HY4 — "Tennis Overhead Smash Technique - How To Never Miss An Overhead Again" — PlayYourCourt.com

faults.name: Overhead: no turn / no pointing (tracking) hand
faults.looks: Square to the net, backpedalling, hitting arm only. Timing and direction are poor and the player risks falling backward.
faults.cause: Footwork not trained; arms and shoulders not coordinated.
faults.cues: "Move both arms up and turn shoulder simultaneously" ([USTA Yellow](https://preview.usta.com/content/dam/usta/content-fragments/tennis-service-center/assets/pdfs/Net-Generation-Practice-Plan-Yellow.pdf)), *(added)* "Point at the ball", "Shuffle or crossover back, never backpedal".
faults.drills: O7 Copy Cat shadow, O1 Overhead Warm-Up, O4.
faults.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yBtXMU7hpwY — "TENNIS OVERHEAD SMASH | Footwork For The Tennis Overhead" — Tennis Evolution. Also https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Ub2tLbOZvFg — "Overhead Smash Tennis | Footwork (Step by Step) 2018" — CLUTCH Tennis

faults.name: Overhead: swinging too early
faults.looks: The racquet swings before the ball arrives, so contact is late or low on the frame. Mishits and balls into the net.
faults.cause: The racquet starts already behind the back with no "trophy" pause; no tracking hand to time the ball.
faults.cues: *(added)* "Racquet up early, then wait", "Track with the non-hitting hand", "Swing when the ball reaches the top of your reach".
faults.drills: O2 Shadow Smash (control over power), O1 (short and deep lobs), O6.
faults.video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=msN27A6QiAk — "Improve your tennis game: Overhead drill" — United States Tennis Association (USTA)

faults.name: Swinging at volleys (big backswing / follow-through)
faults.looks: The racquet goes back past the shoulder and there is a long follow-through. Volleys fly long or into the net, are mishit, and are late against pace.
faults.cause:
- Treating the volley like a groundstroke.
- No time-saving block or tap concept.
- Late preparation, which leads to a compensating swing (see X4).
- *Cause attribution is coaching inference consistent with LTA's "tap the ball (no swing)".*
faults.cues: "Tap, no swing." "Contact in front and to the side of the shoes." "Short backswing, lots of control." — [LTA](https://www.lta.org.uk/siteassets/education/file/secondary-pe-inc-tl-red-and-cardio/body--ball---volley-catch.pdf); [Wayne Bryan via TennisResources](https://www.tennisresources.com/?p=9435)
faults.drills: N1 Volley Catch; N2 toss–volley–catch; N6 Volley Controls; N7 Four Corner (defensive mode).
faults.video:
- [Two Common Mistakes On The Volley | Tennis Volley Technique](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Fm48pbfyl-4) — Intuitive Tennis
- [Tennis Volley Transformation - Rubbish To Rock-Solid in 8 Minutes](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=a1RvPCA3ubg) — Top Tennis Training - Pro Tennis Lessons

faults.name: Wrong grip at the net (forehand/semi-western grip on volleys; switching grips)
faults.looks:
- Backhand volleys are awkward or wristy, or the player switches to a two-hander late.
- Low volleys are closed-faced and go into the net.
- High backhand volleys are weak.
faults.cause: Groundstroke grip carried forward. No time to change grips at the net. *Inference consistent with NG's "change grip and/or hand position between groundstrokes and volleys" goal* ([NG Orange plan](https://www.usta.com/content/dam/usta/content-fragments/tennis-service-center/assets/pdfs/Net-Generation-Practice-Plan-Orange.pdf)).
faults.cues:
"Keep continental grip and one hand on backhand." "Ball should come up off the racquet." (NG Yellow)
- **Caution:** some modern coaches recommend a slightly modified (not strict continental) volley grip; see the debate in the findings above.
faults.drills: N6 Volley Controls and Mini-Tennis Dubz (all continental, slice and volley); N5 V Volley; N2 (the NG tip spots one-handed catchers as continental candidates).

- [TENNIS VOLLEY GRIP | The Correct Tennis Volley Grip](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=s0uSVhqb1mU) — Tennis Evolution

Continental? Not Quite. Myth Busted!!!](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yyQ8XI5nU-0) — Fundamental Tennis

faults.name: Racquet head dropping below the wrist / wrist collapsing on low volleys
faults.looks: On low balls the player drops the racquet head instead of bending the knees. The face closes or the wrist flips, and the ball goes into the net or pops up.
faults.cause: Not getting low with the legs; arm-only adjustment; a weak, floppy wrist. *Inference.*
faults.cues:
- Beginners: "Racket head above the wrist" (LTA).
- Low balls: "Bend your knees, keep the face open, ball comes up off the racquet" (NG wording on open face). *The knee-bend part is coach paraphrase.*
- **Nuance:** 2MinuteTennis argues against always keeping the racquet head up. Advanced players may let the head drop on very low balls while keeping the face open.
faults.drills: N1 (cue racquet head up); N5 / N6 (open face); N11 half-volley drill (low balls with the legs); F5 Skate and Volley (get low on the step).
faults.video:
- [Don’t Keep Your Racket Head Up On Volleys (Tennis Technique Explained)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3z683nkuBqo) — 2MinuteTennis
- [5 Reasons Why You’re Missing Tennis Volleys & How To Fix The Mistakes](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5c8I4lL_jjo) — Meike Babel Tennis

faults.name: Late volley preparation (hitting volleys late / beside or behind the body)
faults.looks: Contact beside or behind the hip. The ball sprays wide or is pushed weakly. The player gets jammed by body shots.
faults.cause: No split step or a late one (X8); a big take-back (X1); the racquet resting low in the ready position. *Inference.*
faults.cues: "Contact in front and to the side of the shoes" (LTA). "Recover quickly into the ready position" (LTA progression).
faults.drills: N1 (alternating sides); N2; N3 Solar System (ready position under pressure); N8 RDC.
faults.video:
- [Stop Hitting Volleys Late! - Tennis Volley Tips Part 1](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uvmjtGb8GS8) — Feel Tennis Instruction
- [Stop Missing Easy Volleys!](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AlYgf3WqGFk) — Essential Tennis - Lessons and Instruction for Passionate Players

faults.name: Stopping or backing up in no-man's-land (not closing after the approach or return)
faults.looks: The player hits the approach, then stops at or behind the service line, or retreats. They face balls at their feet, half-volleys and passing shots.
faults.cause:
- Fear of being lobbed or passed.
- Not knowing the target position.
- Not following the ball.
- TennisCompanion warns against both over-closing (lob target) and under-closing (passing shots).
faults.cues:
- "Approach, split, volley." "Arrive at net on balance in ready position." (NG)
- "Return serve and split-step inside service line." (NG Charge! Doubles)
- Shade toward the ball's direction (NG doubles tip).
- **Nuance:** some coaches teach that there are legitimate moments to be in mid-court; see the Daily Tennis Lesson videos.
faults.drills: N4 Close the Net; N9 Up-and-Back Volley; N15 Charge! Doubles / Team Defender; N11 (if caught there, handle the half-volley); N14 Triples ("close the net and angle volleys").
faults.video:
- [No Man's Land MASTERY - competitive tennis game](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=S6w2hnwwT8w) — Essential Tennis - Lessons and Instruction for Passionate Players
