- [3 Times You Should Be In "No Man's Land" | POSITIONING](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ENSLigmlqMY) — Daily Tennis Lesson

faults.name: Approach shot too hard, too short, or off the wrong ball (and running straight at it / jumping)
faults.looks:
- The approach is over-hit long, or lands short with pace and sits up for a pass.
- The player approaches off deep balls.
- The player sprints straight at the ball and arrives too close or jams themselves.
- The player jumps into the shot and loses control.
faults.cause: Going for winners instead of depth; poor short-ball recognition; footwork error (straight-line run). — [MyTennisHQ](https://mytennishq.com/tennis-approach-shots-5-drills-to-improve-them/); [TennisCompanion](https://tenniscompanion.org/approach-shot/)
faults.cues:
- "Depth over power" and "the same ball over and over".
- "Turn early, move laterally."
- "Don't jump."
- "Only approach off a short ball."
- Down-the-line approach, then follow it in.
faults.drills: N12 Fed Approach + Split; N13 Looking for Short Balls; N9 Up-and-Back (topspin vs slice approach footwork); F4 Copy Cat (hop-move / carioca approach).
faults.video:
- [IMPROVE Your APPROACH Shots By Avoiding These Two Mistakes - Tennis Lesson](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IAfDPa-k5wE) — PlayYourCourt.com
- [This is a textbook approach shot mistake](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=H-R2iXIvvb8) — Fuzzy Yellow Balls
- [When to Approach The Net In Tennis For 80% Success Rate](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7iuSdv5yeEE) — Feel Tennis Instruction

faults.name: Over-closing / getting lobbed at the net, and poor overhead handling
faults.looks: The net player crowds the net too tightly and gets lobbed, then backpedals and mishits the overhead.
faults.cause: Closing too far, which "creates easy lob targets" ([TennisCompanion](https://tenniscompanion.org/approach-shot/)); no drop-step / crossover pattern for moving back (see X13).
faults.cues: Close to a balanced volley position, not onto the net. Overhead: "Move both arms up and turn shoulder simultaneously" (NG Yellow).
faults.drills: N10 Hi-Lo / Overhead Warm-up; N16 Moonballer; F8 Serpentine Shuffle; F4 (drop-step overhead pattern).
faults.video:
- [Tennis: Up and Back Drill for Volleys and Overheads with Bethanie Mattek-Sands](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AYFCcB3L9KM) — Tennis Warehouse
- [Improve your tennis game: Overhead drill](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=msN27A6QiAk) — United States Tennis Association (USTA)

faults.name: No split step, or a mistimed split step (too early → flat on the ground; too late → still in the air)
faults.looks:
- No hop at all, or a hop well before or well after the opponent's contact.
- A slow first step and frequent wrong-footing.
- At the net: jammed volleys and missed reflex balls.
faults.cause:
Timing taught as "jump when they hit" instead of starting the hop during the opponent's swing; jumping too high; no read on landing.
- Evidence: the split step speeds lateral response (764 vs 868 ms) only when the landing matches the cue. — [Uzu 2009](https://lida.sport-iat.de/twm/Record/4017156?lng=en)
- Experts land about 133 ms after the server's contact. — [Navia 2022](https://researchportal.port.ac.uk/en/publications/the-spatiotemporal-control-of-expert-tennis-players-when-returnin/)
faults.cues: "Start the hop before contact." "Small hop, not a jump." "Land knowing where the ball is going." "Push off immediately." — [Feel Tennis](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XR83yXLla8w)
faults.drills: F18 split-step timing; F1 Hopscotch (kids); F10 ladder "split outside, two feet inside"; F11 colour-cone with split; N4 / N9 / N15 (split in transition).
faults.video:
- [Tennis Split Step Timing, Execution And Drills](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XR83yXLla8w) — Feel Tennis Instruction
- [How To Master The Split Step in 5 Minutes: Beginner to Pro](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=J1UhPl1UrYs) — Top Tennis Training - Pro Tennis Lessons
- [You’ve Been Lied to About the Split Step - Here’s the TRUTH](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LQvsolevkJU) — Essential Tennis - Lessons and Instruction for Passionate Players
- [Is The Split Step Killing Your Volleys? Do THIS Instead!](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=i-x_NmAJ_oA) — PlayYourCourt.com

faults.name: Late recovery to centre (admiring the shot)
faults.looks: After a wide ball the player stays put, watches, or walks back. The next ball goes to the open court.
faults.cause: Recovery not trained as part of the stroke; no crossover in the recovery; poor conditioning for repeated efforts. Kovacs calls recovery movement "arguably the most important type of training for tennis-specific movement". — [Kovacs Academy snippet](https://kovacsacademy.com/2020/09/24/tennis-movement-footwork-using-common-language-a-recovery-movement-focus)
faults.cues:
- "Hit, cross over, shuffle, split." (NG Copy Cat / Bryan Minton drill)
- Use the crossover when pulled wide and the crossback when inside the court with the recovery point behind you. — [Columbia Association](https://columbiaassociation.org/blog/racquet-sports/tennis/recovery-footwork-101/)
faults.drills: F3 Make 'Em Move (kids); F4 crossover-recovery shadow; F6 Crossover Shuffle; F7 Crossover–Shuffle–Split 30/30; F12 Quickstep Fan; F14 Horizontal Repeater.
faults.video:
- [Footwork Recovery Drill - Crossover, Shuffle, Split](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-i85rCBrqro) — Simple Coach's Tennis Videos - Coach Bryan Minton
- [How To Move After You Hit The Ball (Tennis Recovery Footwork Explained)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cBLjBqN9v2Y) — 2MinuteTennis
- [How To Recover On Your Groundstrokes (4 steps) I TENNIS LESSON](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NhNNs6ieUOo) — Tennis Evolution

faults.name: Flat-footed / heavy feet / standing still
faults.looks: Heels down between shots, no small adjusting steps, and a slow first step. This is especially common among seniors and beginners.
faults.cause:
- Low foot-speed habits; fatigue.
- For seniors, a belief that movement means speed. A senior coach frames the #1 mistake as "standing still": stay in motion, not necessarily fast. *Low-authority podcast summary.* — [Castfox](https://www.castfox.net/podcast/insiders-playbook-smart-strategies-for-competitive-senior-tennis-players-over-50-7487951/episode/the-tennis-footwork-myth-killing-senior-players-do-this-instead-i-john-craig-1898933)
faults.cues: "Light, active feet." "Stay in motion." Jump-rope for light feet (On).
faults.drills: F10 ladders; F9 Shuffle Toss; F11 colour-cone; F16 hex; F17 Z-ball; for seniors, F19 functional warm-up plus F11 at walking tempo.
faults.video:
- [Seven keys to improve your footwork | TENNIS MASTERCLASS](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BoXkdu9ozJM) — Patrick Mouratoglou
- [10 Agility Ladder Drills For Tennis Players](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XMlBOpbrrQo) — The Tennis Mentor

faults.name: Crossing feet incorrectly (shuffling when a crossover is needed, crossing on short adjustments, wrong first step at the net)
faults.looks:
- Using many small shuffles to reach a wide ball, so the player arrives late. A crossover is the quickest lateral pattern (Tennisplayer.net snippet).
- Crossing over when only a small adjustment is needed, which leaves the player off-balance.
- At the net, crossing in front instead of stepping diagonally with the correct foot.
faults.cause: Footwork patterns never trained separately; no sense of when each pattern applies. *Inference.*
faults.cues:
- "Long distance = crossover; short adjustment = shuffle."
- At the net, "step with correct foot" (NG Red) or "outside foot first" (NG Green).
- Recover with crossover then shuffle.
faults.drills: F6 Crossover Shuffle; F5 Skate and Volley; F15 Lateral Cone Slalom; N8 RDC.
faults.video:
- [Crossover Step | RECOVERY FOOTWORK](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9On2GDwxw6Y) — Daily Tennis Lesson
- [Improve Your Volley With Perfect Footwork (Tennis Volley Footwork Explained)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Gp9t3q8SQHI) — 2MinuteTennis
- [Tennis Footwork Drills - Net Game - Volley Two Step Pattern Drill](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=389Ab5DJYb4) — Rope Tennis Education

faults.name: Reaching instead of moving the feet (arm-only volleys and groundstrokes)
faults.looks: Lunging arm-first. Contact too far from or too close to the body. Weak volleys with no body weight. Off-balance groundstrokes and poor weight transfer.
faults.cause: Late read or late first step (X8); no adjustment steps; NG notes that body mass and footwork carry the volley. *Cause is inference.*
faults.cues: "Step with correct foot" (NG Red goal). "Adapt the body and racket to the incoming ball" (LTA). Small adjustment steps before contact.
faults.drills: F5 Skate and Volley; F15 Lateral Cone Slalom; N1 Volley Catch (adapt body); N8 RDC (shuffle to the ball); F3 Make 'Em Move (move to catch).
faults.video:
- [Common Tennis Forehand & Backhand Weight Transfer Mistake](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SHB7xsIPv5E) — Feel Tennis Instruction
- [Perfect Tennis Volley Footwork in 4 Steps](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Er3u5m32mtA) — Top Tennis Training - Pro Tennis Lessons
- [8 Footwork Drills to Stop Being Late to Every Ball](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9bPKnqr8IO0) — JJG Tennis

faults.name: Backpedalling for lobs/overheads (instead of drop-step + crossover / turning sideways)
faults.looks: The player runs backward facing the net, the heels catch, and they lose balance or fall. The overhead is hit late and off-balance, often into the net.
faults.cause: No drop-step/turn pattern trained; late recognition of the lob. *Inference.*
faults.cues:
- "Drop-step, crossover and run." (NG Copy Cat)
- "Move both arms up and turn shoulder simultaneously." (NG Yellow)
- Keep facing the net when turning (serpentine).
faults.drills: F4 (drop-step overhead pattern); F8 Serpentine Shuffle; N10 Hi-Lo / Overhead Warm-up; N16 Moonballer.
faults.video:
- [TENNIS OVERHEAD SMASH | Footwork For The Tennis Overhead](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yBtXMU7hpwY) — Tennis Evolution
- [How to get to EVERY tennis overhead - Footwork Masterclass](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=z2dOBIKitc8) — Meike Babel Tennis
- [Footwork | OVERHEAD](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rm5VR7iIaCY) — Daily Tennis Lesson

faults.name: Going for too much / unforced errors
faults.looks: low-percentage winners from neutral or defensive positions; errors into the net or long early in rallies; down-the-line attempts from wide positions.
faults.cause: overvaluing power; not knowing the crosscourt margin (net 6 in lower in the middle, 82.5 ft diagonal vs 78 ft) ([TalkingTennis](https://talkingtennis.net/blog-posts/smart-tennis-why-you-should-hit-a-lot-more-balls-cross-court)); scoring that rewards winners without punishing errors.
faults.cues: "Control is a much more important skill… than power" ([USHSTA](https://ushsta.org/?p=638)); "aggressive patience" crosscourt (TalkingTennis); require a "rally of four before you can win a point" ([LTA](https://www.lta.org.uk/play/tennis-tips-and-techniques/how-to-get-more-from-your-tennis-practices/)); make errors cost a point ([Sportplan +/-](https://www.sportplan.net/drills/Tennis/Rally-Drills/Plus-and-Minus-Rewards-TA00011.jsp)).
faults.drills: S1, S2, S11, M8; CoachTube "Put-Away is a No-Way", where points can be won only by opponent errors ([CoachTube](https://coachtube.com/course_lesson/best-tennis-drills-for-coaches/20-mental-strength-tennis-drills/19921068)).

faults.name: No plan / hitting to the middle
faults.looks: every ball goes back to the center; opponents are never moved; no serve or return targets.
faults.cause: practice limited to cooperative rallying; ball controls (direction, height, depth, speed, spin) not trained for tactical use ([USTA Net Gen](https://www.usta.com/content/dam/usta/content-fragments/tennis-service-center/assets/pdfs/Net-Generation-Practice-Plan-Green.pdf)).
faults.cues: "Use all five controls to move opponent"; crosscourt until a short ball, then change direction ("Wait for short ball or sitter on baseline to change directions") (USTA); serve to a spot, then forehand to the open court.

faults.name: Losing focus after errors
faults.looks: errors come in clusters; the player rushes the next point; body language drops.
faults.cause: no between-point routine; attention stays on the past error ([Physical Education Update](https://www.physicaleducationupdate.com/public/860.cfm)).
faults.cues: Loehr's four stages, with eyes on the strings "so your eyes have a place to rest" ([Tennis.com](https://www.tennis.com/news/articles/playing-with-fire-the-delicate-role-of-emotion-in-pro-and-rec-tennis)); cue words "Next Time / Rebound / Get Back".

faults.name: Tight under pressure / choking on big points
faults.looks: shorter swings, pushing the ball, double faults at 30-40 or deuce; going for nothing or everything.
faults.cause: practice never includes pressure; breathing becomes shallow ("in tense situations, we sometimes forget to breathe", [Fernandez/Tennis.com](https://prod.tennis.com/news/articles/mental-tricks-to-closing-out-matches)); no performance cues.
faults.cues: create stress in practice through routines and scoring ([USTA PD](https://www.playerdevelopment.usta.com/news/habits_for_tennis_success_package_mental_skills_into_routines)); deep breathing before the stance (USTA PD cites Djokovic); cues "trust it", "go for it" (USTA PD); pressure training is effective when coach-controlled ([JYU thesis](https://jyx.jyu.fi/jyx/Record/jyx_123456789_87780/Details)).

faults.name: Poor doubles positioning (both back with a gap, one up one back with a diagonal hole, partners not moving together)
faults.looks: a gap opens between partners; the net player stays planted while the ball goes wide; the team doesn't move forward after short balls.
faults.cause: the four positions have never been taught; no rule to "move with the ball"; uncertainty about when to come in.
faults.cues: "Move with ball at net, rally crosscourt from baseline" ([USTA Net Gen Yellow](https://www.usta.com/content/dam/usta/content-fragments/tennis-service-center/assets/pdfs/Net-Generation-Practice-Plan-Yellow.pdf)); on a short ball, the baseliner must come in and split inside the service line (Gladiator Dubz); winning team steps up ([TeachPE Move Up](https://www.teachpe.com/?p=2163)).
faults.drills: D5, D6, D8, D11; video [dd7lPpZe3ig](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dd7lPpZe3ig) ("The #1 Doubles Positioning Mistake (3 Steps To Fix It)", The Tennis Mentor).

faults.name: Not moving at net in doubles (the "statue" net player)
faults.looks: the net player never crosses; the returner rallies crosscourt freely; the net player turns to watch their partner hit.
faults.cause: fear of being passed; not reading the opponent; poaching sideways instead of forward.
faults.cues: watch the baseline opponents, not your partner ([USHSTA Rally Poaching](https://ushsta.org/?p=558)); move "diagonally forward as serve bounces" and "poach as if… alone" on your side ([USTA](https://www.usta.com/content/dam/usta/content-fragments/tennis-service-center/assets/pdfs/Net-Generation-Practice-Plan-Yellow.pdf)); finish "two steps past the center service line" and volley to the feet or the angle ([USHSTA](https://ushsta.org/?p=542)).

faults.name: No between-point routine
faults.looks: the player walks straight to the line and plays fast after both wins and losses; inconsistent serve rhythm.
faults.cause: routines are not taught or practised; players don't know that roughly 16 seconds can be used to recover ([TennisOne/Loehr excerpt](https://tennisone.tennisplayer.net/content/MentalToughness/Loehr/training2/train2.htm)).
faults.cues: use the four stages and personalize them, since Loehr's 16 seconds is "a starting place" (TennisOne); routines are "a series of behaviors and thoughts… to get to the next serve or return" (USTA PD).

faults.name: Negative self-talk
faults.looks: verbal self-criticism, racquet abuse, "I always miss this".
faults.cause: anger rehearsed as habit; Guhde: "we rehearse our rage" ([Tennis.com](https://www.tennis.com/news/articles/playing-with-fire-the-delicate-role-of-emotion-in-pro-and-rec-tennis)); no replacement script.
faults.cues: a five-step cue-word method with phrases like "Nice Try" and "Rebound" ([Physical Education Update](https://www.physicaleducationupdate.com/public/860.cfm)); "positive and productive self-talk" as a core skill ([USTA PD](https://playerdevelopment.usta.com/About-USTA/Player-Development/habits_for_tennis_success_develop_the_mental_skills_foundation)); identify the real source of frustration (for example an untrusted backhand) and train it (Tennis.com).

faults.name: Can't close out leads
faults.looks: broken when serving for the set; softer swings at 5-3; premature net rushes.
faults.cause: "playing not to lose"; anxiety-driven tactical changes; low first-serve percentage under tension.
faults.cues: "Get the first one in… take a little pace off" and "stick with the tactics that helped you get where you are" ([Tennis.com 2010](https://www.tennis.com/news/articles/tip-serving-out-the-match)); 3–4 deep breaths, play to win, and reverse the score mentally ([Gigi Fernandez](https://prod.tennis.com/news/articles/mental-tricks-to-closing-out-matches)).
faults.drills: M9, M3 (sudden death at 40), M7; video [twMrBvmrUb0](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=twMrBvmrUb0) ("Stop choking! Simple Mental Toughness strategies to close out tennis matches", Meike Babel Tennis).

faults.name: Losing to pushers / moonballers
faults.looks: impatience against high, slow balls; errors from overhitting.
faults.cause: never practised against height; poor attack options against high balls.
faults.cues: practise "beat the pusher" with one player restricted to moonballs, and alternate moonball and drive points ([CoachTube](https://coachtube.com/course_lesson/best-tennis-drills-for-coaches/20-mental-strength-tennis-drills/19921068)).
faults.drills: S12, S2, S9 (approaching off high balls).

faults.name: Poor lob defense / no lob in doubles
faults.looks: a two-up team gets lobbed repeatedly with no switching; a two-back team never lobs.
faults.cause: overheads rarely practised; no switch communication.
faults.cues: lob-only constraint games and coach-lob starts ([TeachPE](https://www.teachpe.com/?p=2163); [Wikipedia "Deep Desperation"](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tennis_games)); for seniors, use the lob "to break the rhythm or catch your breath" ([Walters](https://swnewsmedia.com/lakeshore_weekly/news/opinion/columnists/commentary-tennis-tips-for-senior-players/article_1c2a8197-2623-5dd4-b459-6714ccdf3db9.html)).
faults.drills: D7, G6 (Triples with two up / one back).
